Since 2002, the PBC has chosen Shanghai as the venue for the newly established institutions including the Gold Exchange, China Union Pay, Clearing House, Credit Reference Center, Anti-money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center and the Central Bank Clearing Center. In August 2005, the PBC opened its Head Office in Shanghai to provide efficient service to the financial markets in Shanghai and support Shanghais growth into an international financial center. Other financial institutions have followed suit and opened their head offices in Shanghai. In 2012, the PBCs Financial Consumer Protection Bureau was established in Shanghai. Moreover, with the PBCs support, two central banks, i.e. the Norges Bank and the Bank of Korea opened representative offices in Shanghai. The two offices have played an important role in promoting bilateral financial cooperation with Norway and Korea. Overseas monetary authorities and international financial organizations have become investors on the inter-bank bond market in Shanghai. 4 II. Shanghai has the advantages and potential to become an international financial center At present, Shanghai has a multiple of advantages and the potential to become an international financial center. First of all, the countrys rapid growth and transformation of growth pattern provides a solid foundation. Fairly rapid and stable growth in China, accelerated development of modern service sector, advanced manufacturing sector and strategic emerging sector, and increased overall strength of the economy will provide a solid real economy foundation and naturally require better and more sophisticated financial services from Shanghai as a financial sector. Second, China is a large economy with a high savings rate. Chinas GDP is more than 50 trillion yuan, among which savings amount to 25 trillion yuan. At the moment, most savings are kept as bank deposits. The development of direct financing has been emphasized in recent years. With the development of direct financing, capital market has the potential to attract more investment. The development of international financial center in other parts of the world has shown that attracting large groups of investors and lots of fund is an important condition to become a financial center and prompts a financial center to play a bigger role. With an increasingly larger share of savings being invested in the capital market, Shanghai will have greater potential and stronger drive to become an international financial center. In particular, as most of the domestic saving is RMB denominated, the expansion of the cross-border use of RMB and the rising of RMBs status in the world will become a new force supporting Shanghais growth into a an international financial center. Third, as is highlighted by this round of global financial crisis, the international monetary and financial system needs to be adjusted. As the emerging market and developing economies become more active in world trade and financial markets, they will gain a larger say. Against such a background, the international community will increasingly value the stable economic and financial environment in China. These developments will provide a favorable external environment for Shanghais efforts to build an international financial center. Last but not least, after many years development, Shanghai has consolidated her status as an important financial center in China and become more influential in the 5 global financial market. The good momentum is continuing. III. Ideas on further steps to build Shanghai into an international financial center Under the new circumstances and in the new environment, to promote the stable and healthy development of the Chinese economy, to upgrade the growth pattern in Shanghai and in China, optimize the distribution of productive forces, and promote economic and financial reform and opening-up, it is necessary to accelerate the paces to build Shanghai into an international financial center. Going forward, in accordance with the decisions adopted by the State Council, we will actively support and promote the development of Shanghai as an international financial center, redouble the efforts of opening-up to promote the development of Shanghai as an international financial center to a higher level. 1. The cross-border use of RMB will be expanded to turn Shanghai into a global center for RMB products innovation, trading, pricing and settlement After the outbreak of the global financial crisis, we took measures to meet market demands, actively implemented the pilot program of RMB settlement in cross-border trade, advanced the RMB settlement of cross-border investment, steadily developed the RMB loan business for overseas projects, strengthened and deepened bilateral monetary cooperation with other countries. Currently, the cross-border use of RMB has grown to a fairly large scale. As the facilitation of the cross-border use of RMB is a gradual process supported by the strength of the Chinese economy, we have adopted a strategy of promoting the use of RMB in a low-key, pragmatic and effective way, respecting market and meeting market demand, adopting a gradual approach, and keeping risks within a controllable range. The rapid development of cross-border RMB business is a major opportunity for Shanghai to build an international financial center in the next five years. While RMB is in wider use in cross-border transactions and international business, we will, based on the arrangement of the 12th Five-Year Plan for Economic Development and Social Progress, actively promote Shanghai to develop into a center for RMB products innovation, trading, pricing and settlement. 6 First, expanding the cross-border use of RMB, and gradually increasing the proportion of RMB settlement in cross-border trade. We will support the domestic and foreign-funded multinational companies to launch cross-border RMB management business, so that the RMB will be included in the asset portfolio of multinational companies. The cross-border RMB trade refinancing market will be launched to enlarge the scale of RMB trade financing. Second, supporting the two-way opening-up of cross-border RMB investment and financing business. Research will be made in order to launch the pilot program of Qualified Domestic Individual Investor Scheme (QDII2) and Renminbi Qualified Domestic Limited Partner (RQDLP) business. Third, supporting the infrastructure development for cross-border use of RMB. The Cross-border Inter-bank Payment System (CIPs) which is being developed in Shanghai, is an important step to support the cross-border use of RMB, improve the RMB payment and clearing system, guard against and defuse risks in RMB cross-border payment, create a fair and competitive market environment, and facilitate the development of Shanghai as an international financial center. 2. The opening-up of financial market will be accelerated to promote a multi-levelled and well-functioning financial market system to emerge in Shanghai that is accessible to domestic and international investors The PBC will actively promote the reform, opening-up and development of financial markets including money market, bond market and foreign exchange market, and etc, deepen and broaden the financial market, support innovation in order to build a financial market system with diversified ways of trading, diversified groups of participants, increasingly rich products, transparent and effective market regulation. First, promoting the two-way opening-up of bond issuing market. We will encourage more qualified international development institutions to issue RMB bonds in the domestic market, expanding the scale of RMB bonds issued by international development institutions on the interbank market, and allow qualified foreign commercial institutions with high credit ratings to issue RMB bonds in China. 7 Second, increasing the participants on the money market. We will continue to support foreign-funded commercial banks and their branches, foreign-funded non-banking financial institutions to enter the interbank borrowing market and interbank foreign exchange market, increase the number of foreign-funded institutions, and enlarge their transaction volume on the money market within the approved quota. Under the precondition of controllable risks, foreign RMB participating banks and other banks have direct access to interbank borrowing market and interbank foreign exchange market to support the coordinated development of the onshore and offshore RMB market. Third, deepening and broadening the foreign exchange market. Measures will be adopted to support foreign-funded financial institutions to participate in the interbank foreign exchange market. With the RMB clearing banks in Hong Kong and Macao already in the interbank market, other RMB clearing banks and participating banks will be allowed to enter the interbank foreign exchange market, so that the domestic RMB exchange rate will guide the rate movements on the international market. On the basis of direct trading of RMB against USD, JPY and AUD, the direct bilateral exchange rate regime of RMB against more currencies will be established, and the exchange rate of RMB against currencies of emerging economies and surrounding countries will be quoted on the interbank foreign exchange market. 3. The capital and financial account convertibility will be advanced based on the progress of economic and financial reform and in view of domestic and international environment The capital and financial account convertibility is planned in several documents of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the State Council. Progress in this area is also included in the 12th Five Year Plan for Economic Development and Social Progress. The gradual realization of capital account convertibility is conducive to financial innovation and financial market development. It promotes the clustering of financial institutions and internationalization of financial system, facilitates the cross-border use of RMB, improves the mechanism of market economy, enables the market to play a fundamental role in resource allocation on a larger scale, meets market participants demand for international investment and financing, and increases the openness of the economy comprehensively. It is also of major importance to the development of 8 Shanghai as an international financial center. In 1993, the Third Plenary Session of the 14th Central Committee of CPC decided that RMB should be a freely convertible currency. In 1996, China fulfilled the obligation under the Article  of IMF Articles of Agreement and announced that RMB was convertible under the current account. Entering the new century, the conditions are increasingly available to promote capital account convertibility with the growing strength of the Chinese economy, and the deepening of interest rate, exchange rate, state-owned banks and financial market reforms. Under the new circumstances, the process of RMB capital account convertibility will be accelerated in order to further open up, promote trade and investment facilitation, improve financial services to the real economy, build Chinas capacity and efficiency to participate in global allocation of resources, and improve peoples livelihood. Capital account convertibility is a flexible institutional arrangement, not a black or white option. According to international experience, even after the capital account convertibility is realized, suspicious fund flow, external debt and short-term capital flow can still be managed from a macroprudential perspective to effectively guard against the risks in cross-border capital flow, seek advantages and avoid disadvantages, so that the capital account convertibility will play a positive role in various fields. In the meantime, the timing of convertibility measures will be flexibly arranged based on developments in the domestic and international economy and financial market as well as the basic conditions of reform. The measures will be launched one by one whenever the time is right for one of them. 4. The international financial exchange and cooperation will be strengthened, and the financial cooperation between Shanghai and Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taiwan deepened to enhance the influence of Shanghai as an international financial center Measures in this regard include strengthening international and regional financial cooperation, participating in global economic and financial governance, enabling Shanghai to play a role in the international exchange in order to enhance the 9 influence of Shanghai in the international financial sector. The complementarity, mutual assistance and interactions between the financial markets in Shanghai and Hong Kong will be enhanced, the mechanism for financial cooperation between Shanghai and Hong Kong will be improved, and their exchange and cooperation in the market, institutions, products, business and human resources will be strengthened. The financial market products and financial infrastructure between Shanghai and Hong Kong will be connected. The financial exchange and cooperation between Shanghai and Taiwan will be actively promoted. The establishment of a cooperation mechanism will be studied to expand cooperation between Shanghai and Taiwan. 5. PBC will actively participate in and promote the development of the pilot Free Trade Zone in Shanghai which is under research While visiting the Yangtze River Delta, Premier Li Keqiang asked relevant departments in Shanghai to study how to start the pilot free trade zone based on the Shanghai Free Trade Zone. In accordance with the latest decision of the State Council, the PBC will focus on overall financial sector reform and opening-up, create and optimize the financial environment that is compatible with the development of the pilot free trade zone, and establish an interaction mechanism between the free trade zone and an international financial center in Shanghai. In view of Chinas economic and financial situations, the Central Economic Work Conference convened at the end of last year decided that a sound monetary policy will be implemented this year. Currently, performance of Chinas economy and the financial sector is sound, prices are stable, indicating that the sound monetary policy is appropriate and effective. In the meantime, the global economic and financial situations are complex and changing, and the domestic economy faces new situations and problems. Financial markets have been sensitive to any market signal and responded quickly, thus it is easy to identify and correct problems. The PBC will continue to implement a sound monetary policy, make the policy measures more forward-looking, better-targeted and more flexible, and conduct preemptive adjustments and fine-tunings in a timely and appropriate manner. We will work together with relevant authorities to guide financial institutions to provide 10 rational credit supply, properly manage the total volume of assets and liabilities as well as maturity structure, support the structural adjustment, transformation and upgrading of the real economy. Besides, a number of monetary policy instruments and measures will be adopted to adjust market liquidity timely, maintain the overall market stability, and create sound monetary conditions for the stable performance of financial market and economic development. Since the beginning of this year, Chinas economic growth is generally stable. Measures of structural adjustment have been intensified too. Although the growth rate has slowed down, it is rational in general and reflects a stable-yet-progressive trend. Furthermore, the dividend of reform will be further released as the effect of streamlining administrative measures unfolds, the adjustment of economic structure and economic upgrading accelerates, and the quality and efficiency of economic growth improve. China is and will be in a period of strategic opportunities and enjoy enormous potential. From a global perspective, China remains an important engine for global growth. We have confidence in the economic growth, financial sector and market development of the whole country, and in Shanghais development as an international financial center. 11

Title: Moving Faster to Shore up Weaknesses in the Social Field and Promoting Domestic and International Circulations - Mr. Guo Shuqing, Secretary of the CPC PBC Commi...
text: Home News & Events Speeches To Read Chinese Version Moving Faster to Shore up Weaknesses in the Social Field and Promoting Domestic and International Circulations - Mr. Guo Shuqing, Secretary of the CPC PBC Committee, Chairman of the CBIRC a Moving Faster to Shore up Weaknesses in the Social Field and Promoting Domestic and International Circulations Keynote Speech at the Financial Street Forum 2022 Mr. Guo Shuqing Secretary of the CPC PBC Committee, Chairman of the CBIRC 21st November 2022 Dear Secretary Yin Li, Acting Mayor Yin Yong, Colleagues and friends, Ladies and gentlemen, It is a great pleasure to attend the Financial Street Forum 2022. Under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, the Beijing Municipal Party Committee and Municipal Government have coordinated pandemic prevention and control with economic and social development, achieved new breakthroughs in the reform and opening up, made new strides in high-quality development, and took the lead in preventing and resolving financial risks across China. What is impressive in particular was that despite the complex and severe pandemic, Beijing held the 24th Winter Olympics and the 13th Winter Paralympics on schedule, which are splendid, distinctive and successful. Lets once again extend warm congratulations to Beijing, and pay tributes to the Beijing Municipal Party Committee and Municipal Government and the people of the city! The 20th National Congress of the CPC has drawn up a grand blueprint to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization. To fully build a modern socialist country, we must focus on the problem of unbalanced and insufficient development and strive to solve the structural shortage on the supply side. Affected by multiple factors, Chinas social undertakings generally face a number of pending issues and obviously lag behind compared with the actual needs and potentials, though they have made great historic progress along with the rapid economic growth. By the end of 2021, in per capita terms, the number of intensive care unit (ICU) beds in China was only about one-seventh of that in developed countries. The number of beds for the elderly was about 50% of the average in developed countries, the supply of nursing care for the disabled elderly was strained, and it was difficult to find a bed in an organization with good medical and nursing services. National education varied greatly between urban and rural areas and between regions, and children of new urban residents encountered many difficulties in schooling. The proportion of the working-age population who had received higher education was about half of that in developed countries. The per capita sports area was 2.41 square meters, compared with 15 to 20 square meters in developed countries. The number of libraries and museums was less than one-fifth of that in developed countries. Social undertakings bear on peoples livelihoods, connect with peoples support, and deliver on the peoples growing expectation for a better life. At the same time, social undertakings are mostly high value-added service industries in the economic sense, an important part of the modern economic system, and a key link in fostering the new development paradigm. In the Report to the 20th National Congress of the CPC, General Secretary Xi Jinping pointed out that China aims to become a leading country in education, science and technology, talent, culture, sports, and health for the year 2035. Undoubtedly, that means gathering a huge amount of factor resources, building more construction projects and grand digital economic infrastructure, and promoting the leapfrog improvement of hardware and software in the social sector. When it comes to investment in social undertakings, its easy to think of government finance first. Everyone hopes that financial input could be increased. Indeed, financial input can be continuously raised, but it is certainly far from enough compared with the actual needs. China has a high aggregate savings rate and relatively abundant social funds. Only by coordinating the efforts of the government, enterprises, public institutions and residents can we optimize the allocation of various resources and comprehensively accelerate the process of shoring up weaknesses in the social sector. The first thing I need to stress is that finance can play a special and important role in facilitating the development of social undertakings. Since the reform and opening up, China has created a world legend in transportation construction. Starting from the construction of the Shenyang-Dalian Expressway in 1984 and the Qinhuangdao-Shenyang Passenger Dedicated Line in 1999, China has built the worlds largest expressway network and high-speed railway network in less than 40 years. The financial system has turned huge national savings into effective investment, providing strong support for the leapfrog development of transportation. We should learn from the successful practice of building roads with loans and repaying loans with fees to reform and improve the investment and financing system in the social sector. We need to strengthen the coordination between financial policies and fiscal policies, between policy finance and commercial finance, and between direct financing and indirect financing, to support qualified hospitals, schools, and cultural, sports, elderly care and child care institutions etc. in achieving high-quality development with a variety of financing instruments. To be frank, there have been some negative cases in the past that several hospitals and schools fell into operating difficulties due to blind borrowing or poor management. To avoid similar problems, we must follow the inherent laws of various social undertakings, and establish sound restraint mechanisms of government agencies, financing entities and financial institutions respectively in a differentiated manner. We should also focus on cash flow balance and scientifically set early warning and monitoring indicators for debt financing to ensure the healthy and sustainable development of institutions and projects. The second is to develop a multi-level and multi-pillar pension insurance system, which is a key measure to improve the supply of the social sector. By the end of 2021, Chinas first pillar of basic old-age insurance covered 1,029 million people, with the fund balance of 6.4 trillion yuan. The second pillar, enterprise annuities and occupational annuities, covered more than 70 million employees and accumulated 4.4 trillion yuan of funds. As for the third pillar, after the rectification in recent years, the insurance products that really have the attributes of providing care for the elderly are growing rapidly, accumulating over 5 trillion yuan of liability reserves. Since the exclusive commercial pension insurance pilot program began a year ago, more than 250,000 people have been insured, including 47,000 workers in new industries, new business forms and various types of flexible employment. 49 pension wealth management products have been launched, with the total amount of 100 billion yuan. Yesterday, the pilot specific pension savings products were rolled out in five cities. Not long ago, the Rules on the Implementation of Private Pension was officially released, and relevant supporting policies have been successively introduced, thus enabling private pension to be implemented on the ground. The top priority of developing the third pillar of pension insurance in a well-regulated way is to encourage financial institutions to offer commercial pension products that are worthy of the name and operate safely. By optimizing asset allocation, we can set up return smoothing funds and risk reserve funds to provide targeted pension products for groups with different risk appetite and risk tolerance. Also under the concept of long-term investment with long-term yields, value investment with value creation, and prudent investment with reasonable returns, a certain proportion of the pension insurance funds accumulated in the three pillars can be invested in social undertakings and industries to play a powerful role as the high-speed train featuring Electrical Multiple Unit (EMU). The third is to develop charitable and public-interest initiatives, which is of great significance for enhancing the investment and financing capacity in the social sector and promoting common prosperity. As noted in the Report to the 20th National Congress of the CPC, we will build an institutional framework under which primary, secondary, and tertiary distribution are well coordinated and mutually complementary. We will provide guidance and support for enterprises, social organizations, and individuals who have the desire and ability to actively participate in charitable and public-interest initiatives. This has charted the course for the development of public-interest initiatives in the new era. To promote charitable and public-interest initiatives in China, we benefit not only from the advantages of the socialist system, but also the valuable traditional Chinese culture. We should have full confidence that China will be able to deliver world-class public-interest and charitable undertakings. As of the end of 2020, China's charitable organizations accounted for 1.1% of registered public organizations, and the donation amount in that year accounted for about 0.2% of GDP. However, in some developed countries, the donation amount accounted for more than 2% of GDP in the specific year. In some developing countries, although the total donation amount was not very large, the proportion of people who participated in the donation initiatives was as high as 70%. History at all times and all over the world shows that charity can, in addition to helping the poor and providing relief, play an irreplaceable role than the government and others in promoting education, science, culture and talent development. We should learn from international good practices, develop more standardized and convenient institutional arrangements for charitable activities, and advance the development of charitable undertakings. We must face up to the detours and disgraceful events that China's charitable undertakings had once gone through, and learn from the profound lessons. Charity is the sunniest and noblest cause in the world. It must not be rigged or under the radar, and it must not allow any cross-the-line behavior for personal gains. The principles of equity, justice and openness should be carried through. The whole process of charity management should be transparent, and ensure that all donated assets are properly managed and efficiently used for public- interest and charitable initiatives. To promote the healthy development of charitable undertakings in China, we need to carry out the following work. The first is to promote charity culture. Since ancient times, China has advocated caring for the world and giving to the public. People would spontaneously help each other and give to others when they can. It is necessary to pay equal attention to policy incentives and spiritual incentives, such as establishing charity awards, and creating a social atmosphere that honors those who donate and respect those do good deeds, so that charity becomes a noble cause in which all sectors of society and the people want to participate in. The second is to strengthen legal protection. The Charity Law is being amended, and relevant implementation rules will be formulated, so as to establish and improve the institutional system for non-profit legal entities, improve the regulations on registration of public organizations and management of foundations, and ultimately forming a complete charity regulation system. The third is to facilitate tax incentives. China has given charity a lot of tax reliefs through relevant laws, but the public knows little about it. Besides, in practice many conditions and procedural constraints are attached. We should follow the principle of substance over formality, use tools like the Internet and big data and adopt simple methods and measures, so that the policy objectives of supporting public-interest and charitable initiatives can be achieved. The fourth is to strengthen supervision and management. Efforts should be made to improve the multi- tiered and classified prudent supervisory system in a stringent manner, and strengthen government supervision, industry self-discipline, social media oversight and public surveillance. The nature of charity featuring public interest and altruism should be upheld, and donors and beneficiaries should be completely separated through the dedicated operation of third-party organizations. Commercial operations or other arbitrage activities under the cover of charity donations should be prevented. Fifth, we shall actively develop charitable trusts. This is the root of the trust business, which has a history of more than 400 years in the world, and has played a unique role in promoting the standardized development of philanthropy. Trust mechanism has the advantages of property independence, bankruptcy isolation, professional management and efficient operation, etc. We should put in more efforts to promote charitable trusts. Since the promulgation of the Charity Law, charitable trusts in China have developed rapidly, with a total registered value of more than 4 billion yuan. By the registered value of charitable trust, Zhejiang, Guangdong and Gansu provinces are in the lead in China, while by the number of charitable trusts registered, Zhejiang, Gansu and Shaanxi provinces are among the top three. It is both thought-provoking and encouraging that tertiary distribution can be cultivated both in economically backward areas and developed areas. Sixth, the financial industry should strive to make new and greater contributions to charitable initiatives. Financial institutions have been at the forefront of the country in fulfilling their social responsibilities, and especially in the battles against the epidemics, they have made new and substantial progress and achievements. We suggest that banking and insurance institutions provide financial services such as financing, settlement and risk protection for public-interest organizations and charitable activities at more favorable prices. Ladies and gentlemen, Since the beginning of this year, the inflation in the United States and Europe has reached the highest level in 40 years, and the monetary policies took a sharp U-turn from extreme easing to aggressive rate hikes. Above and beyond that, repeated resurgence of the COVID-19, geopolitical conflicts and other problems have greatly increased the difficulty and uncertainty of world economic recovery. China has institutional advantages of unique social systems, the most complete industrial sectors and the broadest unified market in the world. Chinas economy has strong resilience, great potential, ample policy room, and the most solid fundamentals for long-term sound development. Recently, overseas media has continued to hype about Chinas "real estate crisis and "decline of construction industry. In fact, China is still in the peak period of urbanization and the initial stage of rural revitalization, and the overall fixed-asset investment still has great potential for further growth. We are full of confidence in realizing Chinese-style modernization and building a new form of human civilization. The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered a historical process that it is irreversible and no force can change! Adhering to opening up has always been China's basic national policy. At present, China's financial industry has entered a new stage of high-level opening to the outside world. Since the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the assets of foreign banks operating in China have increased by nearly 30%, and those of foreign insurance companies in China have increased by about 120%. A number of foreign-controlled wealth management, asset management, fund and insurance group companies have started operations one after another. We will, as always, welcome foreign-funded financial institutions with sound operations, good qualifications and outstanding specialties to participate in Chinese market, share the historic growth opportunities and jointly contribute to the economic and financial development. While paying attention to the macro-financial environment, we are always concerned about our peoples asset security. We have noticed that recently, because the market became optimistic about the prospect of economic recovery, bond yields have increased, which has caused fluctuations in the net value of some banks wealth management products. This is the market's self-adjustment, and the overall risk is completely controllable. On the other hand, we are fully aware that the financial products that individual investors can choose from are becoming more diverse, and the risks they face are becoming more complex. They need to manage the trade-off between risk and return. Under market economy, high returns are bound to be accompanied by high risks. Advertising "principal ensured with high return" and "low risk and high return" is definitely financial frauds. We should persist and spare no efforts in increasing financial literacy, so that people can always be alert to the temptation of high returns, avoid being deceived, so that they gain reasonable returns through rational investment, and safely and steadily increase their property income. Finally, I wish the forum a complete success! Thank you! Date of last update NOV. 21,2022

Title: Transcript of Group Interview with Pan Gongsheng, Spokesperson for the Central Financial System Delegation to the 20th CPC National Congress
text: Home News & Events Speeches Transcript of Group Interview with Pan Gongsheng, Spokesperson for the Central Financial System Delegation to the 20th CPC National Congress a To Read Chinese Version On October 20, the press center for the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) hosted a group interview with the spokespersons for the delegations from Qinghai, Ningxia, Xinjiang, the central Party and government departments, the central financial system, and the centrally administered state-owned enterprises (in Beijing). Speaking on behalf of the delegation from the central financial system, Pan Gongsheng, member of the CPC PBC Committee and deputy governor of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC), also secretary of the CPC Leadership Group of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and SAFE administrator, introduced the delegations study of the report to the 20th CPC National Congress and answered questions from journalists. The transcript is as follows. Moderator: Now Id like to give the floor to Comrade Pan Gongsheng from the central financial system delegation. Pan Gongsheng: Good evening, everyone. There have always been good interactions between the media and the financial system. Today, on behalf of the central financial system delegation and all the staff of the financial system, I would like to take this opportunity to extend sincere thanks to you for your support. The delegation from the central financial system has 44 delegates, who come from financial regulatory agencies and financial institutions, and many work at the primary level. In recent days, we have been studying conscientiously General Secretary Xi Jinpings report to the 20th CPC National Congress and have had lively discussions to share our understandings with each other. We unanimously agree that the report, with its distinctive theme and holistic perspective, is both pragmatic and inspiring. We pledge all our support for it. Deeply grounded in social practice, as we can see from the great changes that have taken place in the past decade of the new era, the report comes from practice and stands as the theoretical advancement of practice. It is a political manifesto and action plan that will guide and inspire all Party members and all the Chinese people to take strides on the journey toward realizing the Second Centenary Goal. The financial system will thoroughly implement the spirit of the 20th CPC National Congress. We will uphold the strong leadership of the Party over financial work and ensure that financial work adheres to its political character and serves the interests of the people. We will pursue a path of financial development with Chinese characteristics to provide strong financial support for the building of a great modern socialist country in all respects. Thank you. China Banking and Insurance News: Over the past decade, China has seen a historic rise in its economic strength. As finance is the lifeblood of the real economy, will you introduce the achievements made in Chinas financial work over the past decade? Thank you. Pan Gongsheng: Thank you for your question. Over the past decade, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has attached great importance to financial work, on which a series of important decisions and arrangements have been made. As a result, the financial cause of China has witnessed significant achievements. First, the quality and efficiency of financial support for the real economy have been improved substantially. With continued efforts to advance the supply-side structural reform of the financial sector, China has developed a financial market system, a financial institution system and a financial product system that feature a broad range of categories and adequate competition, covering credit, insurance, bonds, stocks, foreign exchange, etc. The quality, efficiency and inclusiveness of financial services have seen dramatic improvements. With regard to monetary and financial environment, China is one of the few major economies that have stuck to a normal monetary policy in recent years. The sound monetary policy has created a favorable financial environment for stabilizing economic growth, prices, employment and the balance of payments. In terms of promoting high-quality development, the financial structure has been optimized markedly, providing strong support to major national strategies as well as key fields and weak links in economic and social development, such as poverty eradication, micro and small businesses, sci-tech innovation, green development, rural revitalization and the building of China into a manufacturing powerhouse. Second, we have made important achievements in forestalling and defusing financial risks. In line with the strategic deployments made by the CPC Central Committee on fighting the critical battle of forestalling and defusing major risks, we have effectively resolved a number of prominent risks in the financial field, so that financial risks have subsided overall and the financial system is generally stable. The banking, insurance and securities sectors have witnessed sound development while the stock market, the bond market and the foreign exchange market on the whole perform stably. Third, sustained efforts have been made to deepen the reform and opening-up of Chinas financial sector. We have continuously optimized the financial system, improved the modern financial enterprise system, moved ahead with the development of a multi-tiered capital market, and improved the financial regulatory system so that they will become more market-oriented and law- based. Following the principles of self-determination, progressiveness, equality and security, we have been prudently moving ahead with the high-quality two-way opening-up of the financial sector. Reform and opening-up have greatly modernized Chinas financial governance system as well as governance capacity. Fourth, Chinas financial sector has become much more competitive and influential globally. Currently, Chinas banking sector ranks first in the world by total assets; China has the worlds second largest stock market, bond market and insurance market; and Chinas foreign exchange reserves have been the highest globally for 17 consecutive years. Also, China is one of the leading countries in the world in the areas of green finance, inclusive finance and digital finance. The RMB has seen its international status rising significantly, with its weighting in the third place in the International Monetary Funds Special Drawing Rights basket. More than 80 countries and economies in the world have included the RMB in their reserve currencies. The reason why these achievements have been made over the past decade lies essentially in the scientific guidance from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the steering role of General Secretary Xi Jinping, and the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee. Thank you. Hong Kong Economic Times: As set out in the report to the 20th CPC National Congress, China will accelerate the building of a new development paradigm and promote high-quality development. Accordingly, a series of arrangements have been made for financial work to do. So my questions are: What will the financial system do to implement these requirements? What will be the focus of financial work in the upcoming period? Thank you. Pan Gongsheng: The financial system takes it as an important political task to thoroughly implement the spirit of the report to the 20th CPC National Congress. We will follow the guidance of the report. From macro and strategic perspectives, we will focus our work on the following. First, we will uphold the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee over financial work. We will stress the Partys leadership throughout the process and in every respect of financial work. We will implement resolutely and efficiently the major decisions and arrangements of the CPC Central Committee. Furthermore, we will continue to improve the systems and mechanisms for the exercise of the Partys leadership over financial work so as to turn the institutional advantages, as shown by the Partys leadership, into financial governance capacity. Second, we will stay committed to providing financial support for the real economy. We will pursue a sound monetary policy, strengthen cross-cycle and countercyclical adjustments, and create a monetary and financial environment conducive to boosting economic growth, expanding employment, stabilizing prices and maintaining the balance of payments. We will guide financial resources to better support the key fields and weak links in economic and social development, and offer high-quality financial services to promote high-quality development of the Chinese economy. Third, we will always coordinate development and security and firmly defend the bottom line whereby no systemic financial risk will occur. Forestalling and defusing financial risks is an eternal theme for the financial sector. The financial system will give higher priority to the prevention and control of financial risks and will improve the mechanisms for risk prevention, early warning and resolution to safeguard Chinas financial stability and financial security. Fourth, we will continue to deepen financial reform and opening-up. We will push further ahead with the supply-side structural reform of the financial sector, put efforts into developing inclusive finance, green finance, sci-tech finance and digital finance, and promote the sound and stable development of a multi-tiered capital market. We will deepen the market-oriented exchange rate reform and keep the RMB exchange rate basically stable at an adaptive and equilibrium level. In addition, we will promote the high-quality two-way opening-up of the financial sector and actively participate in international financial governance. We will enhance financial regulatory capacity and strengthen the financial legal system. Fifth, we will continue to strengthen Party self-governance in every respect and conduct high- quality Party building to promote high-quality financial development. We will carry on the building of a team of financial professionals who are loyal and upright and have a strong sense of responsibility. We will severely punish corruption in the financial field and ensure that financial work adheres to its political character and serves the interests of the people. We firmly believe that under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, we will take solid steps forward on the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics and provide strong financial support for the pursuit of the Chinese path to modernization. Thank you. Date of last update OCT. 21,2022

Title: The Dollar Cycle and Chinas Foreign Exchange Market - Remarks by PBC Deputy Governor and SAFE Administrator Pan Gongsheng at Annual Conference of Financial St...
text: Home News & Events Speeches The Dollar Cycle and Chinas Foreign Exchange Market - Remarks by PBC Deputy Governor and SAFE Administrator Pan Gongsheng at Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2022 a To Read Chinese Version November 21,2022 Honorable Party Secretary Yin Li, Acting Mayor Yin Yong, President of Xinhua News Agency Fu Hua, and distinguished guests, Good afternoon! Since this year, as inflation rises and monetary policy tightens, the global financial markets, including the foreign exchange markets, have gone through violent turbulence, whilst the Chinese foreign exchange market remains generally resilient. So now I would like to share with you some of my thoughts on the topic of dollar cycle and Chinas foreign exchange market. The fluctuations of the US Dollar in an extended cycle are an important factor affecting the global financial markets. Since the collapse of the Bretton Woods System, the USD has gone through three cycles of appreciation and depreciation. This round of appreciation has lasted for 11 years since mid- 2011. For a rather long period since the 2008 global financial crisis, the world faced low growth, low inflation, and low interest rate, until 2021 when inflation started to rise rapidly. The major dollar cycle is driven by multiple factors. First, changes in the long-term economic growth potential are an important determinant, and the US labor productivity growth is highly correlated with USD movements. Second, the interest margin advantage from policy divergence drives cross-border capital flows and amplifies cyclical volatility. Third, there is a self-reinforcing mechanism for USD appreciation. As the USD is a major global financing currency, there is a cycle of USD appreciation - asset price adjustments in emerging markets- capital flow back to the US -USD appreciation. From the perspective of a long historical period, the global macro environment is likely to shift from general easing to high volatility. The period from the 1980s to 2019 can be regarded as an era of general easing, when the global economy witnessed low inflation and mild fluctuations at a macro level. However, this trend changed in 2021. The large-scale incentive policies in the major developed economies since the outbreak of the COVID-19 have boosted demand, but the recovery of supply has been suppressed by supply chain disruptions, labor market tensions, and geopolitical conflicts. These countries witnessed inflation way higher than their policy targets and drastically increased fluctuations in their economic data. The global economy may have entered an era of great volatility. To fight inflation, major central banks have sped up the pace of their monetary policy tightening. The Federal Reserve (Fed) has sharply raised interest rates and shrunk its balance sheet, tightening its monetary policy faster than ever. The European Central Bank (ECB) has also taken big steps in rate hikes, raising its policy rates to the highest since 2009. Given that inflation still hovers high and economic growth has slowed down, major central banks will face a dilemma between stabilizing growth and controlling inflation in policy decisions. From the beginning of this year, high inflation and tightened monetary policy have caused severe volatility in the global financial markets. The prices of equities, bonds and other global financial assets fell across the board. The USD has strengthened rapidly, with the US Dollar Index (USDX) going up since early 2022 by nearly 20 percent to a 20-year-high of over 114. From this October, as the market expected a slowdown in interest rate hikes by major central banks, the USDX fell back from its high level, yet the year-to-date rise is still rare over the past four decades. Chinas foreign exchange market demonstrates new features and increasing resilience. Compared with the previous two periods of USD appreciation, the RMB exchange rate has been less sensitive to the USDX fluctuations since 2021. Globally, the depreciation of the RMB is at an average level compared with the currencies of major developed economies and emerging markets. Cross-border capital flows have been generally stable and orderly despite fluctuations. Multiple factors contribute to the stronger resilience of the foreign exchange market. First, the RMB exchange rate moved in both directions with enhanced flexibility and played a better role as an automatic stabilizer for the balance of payments, which helped relieve external pressures in time. Second, the basic balance of payments surplus has played a dominant role. In the first three quarters of this year, Chinas current account surplus was USD310.4 billion, the highest in the same period in history, and the ratio of the surplus to the gross domestic product (GDP) in the same period was 2.4 percent, remaining within a reasonable and equilibrium range. Direct investment witnessed a net inflow, and cross-border capital flows were stable and orderly. Third, the external debt structure has been optimized as a whole. Traditional external debt financing increased slightly, and the structures of external debt type, currency and maturity have all been optimized. Fourth, the proportion of the RMB use in cross-border transactions has been increasing, which is conducive to lowering the risk of currency mismatch. Fifth, with the promotion and popularization of exchange rate hedging tools, businesses have been remarkably more adaptable to exchange rate fluctuations. People attach growing importance to RMB-denominated assets as a choice for risk aversion. This year, bonds of major countries have generally seen rising yields and falling prices, making RMB bonds one of the few financial assets of stable prices. Unlike other emerging market bonds, RMB bonds are quasi-safe assets whose risk-return features are similar to those of developed country bonds. As China focuses on domestic conditions concerning macroeconomic policies, its interest rate and exchange rate movements are relatively independent from those of other economies, giving the RMB bonds a diversification advantage in global asset allocation. Looking forward, the sound performance of Chinas foreign exchange market will continue. Firstly, major developed economies face growing recession risks. With inflation higher than their policy targets, they will maintain tightened monetary policies generally. The USD is still likely to fluctuate at a high level in the short term, while market institutions forecast the momentum of USD appreciation is waning and this strong appreciation cycle is close to its end. Secondly, the fundamentals for Chinas sound economic growth over the long run remain unchanged. The twenty COVID-19 countermeasures, which further optimize the pandemic containment, will improve the reasonability and accuracy of the prevention and control, and coordinate the containment and economic and social development in a more effective manner. The implementation of a series of policy measures to stabilize economic growth with tangible results will also further unleash the momentum of Chinas economic growth. In addition, the financial authorities have unveiled a number of supportive financial policies to work with the real estate market authorities and local governments to support both the basic home-buying demand and the improvement demand, and to maintain steady and orderly real estate financing. These policies are also expected to enhance financial support for ensuring housing project delivery, protect the legitimate rights and interests of housing consumers, resolutely block and reduce risk spillovers, and stabilize market expectations and confidence. These policies have played a marked role in counter-cyclical adjustments and produced positive market effects. Following the central governments policies on the development of the real estate market, we will, based on market principles and the rule of law, balance short-term and long- term goals, and address both the symptoms and the root causes for the healthy and sustainable development of Chinas real estate market. In the future, changes in the internal and external macro environment will contribute to the sound functioning of Chinas foreign exchange market. Over the past decade, we have coordinated opening-up and security, and made remarkable achievements in the reform and opening up in the field of foreign exchange. First, the market-based formation mechanism of the RMB exchange rate has been gradually improved, and with enhanced elasticity of the RMB exchange rate, two-way fluctuations have become the norm and the RMB exchange rate has remained basically stable at an adaptive and equilibrium level. Second, the opening of the capital account is steadily advancing, and a relatively high level of convertibility has been achieved. In particular, cross-border direct investment has been basically convertible, cross- border securities investment has realized multi-channel and multi-level two-way opening, and cross- border financing now allows market entities to carry out financing activities at their discretion under the macro-prudential management framework. Third, the entities, scale and products of foreign exchange market transactions have been growing rapidly, and an open, diversified, full-fledged, competitive and orderly foreign exchange market has basically taken shape. Fourth, a basic equilibrium has been maintained in the balance of payments with enhanced stability and resilience. The ratio of current account balance to GDP has remained in a reasonable range and registered at around 2 percent in recent years. Cross-border trade, investment and financing have become more active, and the scale of cross-border payments and receipts have grown rapidly. Fifth, the foreign exchange market management framework incorporating both macro-prudential management and micro supervision, has been established. The supervisory early warning and response mechanisms for cross-border capital flows continue to improve, and macro-prudential tools have been more sophisticated. Sixth, the safety, liquidity, value preservation and appreciation of foreign exchange reserve assets have been secured. In the future, while earnestly implementing the guidelines of the 20th CPC National Congress, we will coordinate financial opening-up and security, and make every effort to build a foreign exchange management system that adapts to high-quality opening up. We will deepen reform and opening up in the field of foreign exchange, further facilitate cross-border trade, investment and financing, so as to maintain the sound functioning of the foreign exchange market and to safeguard national economic and financial security. I wish the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum a complete success. Thank you! Date of last update NOV. 21,2022

Title: Speech by PBOC Deputy Governor and SAFE Administrator Pan Gongsheng at the Press Briefing on Launching Financial Support Policies for Building Hengqin and Qianh...
text: Home News & Events Speeches Speech by PBOC Deputy Governor and SAFE Administrator Pan Gongsheng at the Press Briefing on Launching Financial Support Policies for Building Hengqin and Qianhai Cooperation Zones a To Read Chinese Version Distinguished Chief Executive He Yicheng, Vice Governor Zhang and dear guests, Its a great pleasure to attend the press briefing on launching financial support policies for Hengqin and Qianhai cooperation zones, an event organized by the People's Government of Guangdong Province. First of all, on behalf of the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the Guangdong Provincial Committee of the CPC and its People's Government, the Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions, as well as friends from the media for your long-standing attention and support to financial work. Taking forward the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Greater Bay Area) is a major strategic decision made by the CPC Central Committee, and General Secretary Xi Jinping attaches high importance to and cares deeply for its progress. The Report to the 20th CPC National Congress makes it clear that China will continue to develop the Greater Bay Area, and support Hong Kong and Macao in better integrating themselves into Chinas overall development and playing a greater role in realizing national rejuvenation. Hengqin in Zhuhai and Qianhai in Shenzhen are important platforms for the cooperative development of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao. Besides, increasing financial support for development of Hengqin and Qianhai is a specific measure to thoroughly follow the guidelines of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important speech and instructions, and to actively implement the major strategic arrangements of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council. This measure is of great significance to deepening the Chinese mainland's cooperation with Hong Kong and Macao, and advancing the reform and opening up of the financial sector. Approved by the State Council, the PBOC, together with the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the SAFE and the People's Government of Guangdong Province, issued the Opinions on Providing Financial Support for Building the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin and the Opinions on Providing Financial Support for the Comprehensive Deepening Reform and Opening-up of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone. In accordance with the principle of "considering both long- and near-term needs, prioritizing people's well-being, taking steady and incremental steps, and stressing risk prevention and control", the two documents focus on the key areas of financial reform, and put forward 30 financial reform and innovation tasks in six areas for each cooperation zone, so as to meet the needs of high-quality economic development. While attaching importance to common priorities in Guangdong-Macao and Shenzhen-Hong Kong cooperation, such as easy access to financial services and market connectivity, the two documents also propose special projects for Guangdong-Macao cooperation and Shenzhen-Hong Kong cooperation respectively based on their regional situations. The policies in common are as follows. The first is to give priority to financial innovation that serves the peoples livelihood. Better, more diversified and more accessible financial services will be provided through measures such as facilitating credit financing and employment for Hong Kong and Macao residents and providing easy access to mobile payment. The second is to deepen the connectivity among financial markets and infrastructures. Financing is expected to be easier in the Greater Bay Area, underpinned by greater interconnection among financial markets, improved account management and upgraded cross-border insurance services. The third is to facilitate cross- border trade, investment and financing. To pilot foreign exchange administration reform and RMB internationalization, we will facilitate cross-border trade settlement and improve the cross-border investment and financing policies. The fourth is to strengthen financial regulation. We will perfect the financial risk prevention and control mechanism, which shall conform to the level of opening-up, by means of establishing a cooperation mechanism for financial regulation and innovating cross-border financial regulation. In terms of special projects, taking into account the strategic positioning and unique needs of Guangdong-Macao cooperation and Shenzhen-Hong Kong cooperation, we will foster the development of distinctive financial industries and expand cooperation scope. Based on the position of Hengqin as a zone "serving Macaos long-term development and promoting the integrated development of Hengqin and Macao", an "electronic fence" system for capital will be built to explore for free flow of cross-border capital. Also, some modern financial industries such as asset management, bond market, financial leasing and green finance will be developed in an innovative manner based on the needs of Macao for appropriately diversified economic development. Adhering to Qianhai's mission of "relying on Hong Kong, serving the mainland, and facing the world", we will expand the development space of Hong Kong's financial sector and develop green finance, supply chain finance, shipping finance, and sci-tech innovation finance. With these measures, we will comprehensively enhance Qianhai's functions as a demonstration zone for piloting national financial industry opening-up and a pilot zone for cross-border RMB business innovation. In fact, when the two documents were still in the pipeline, a considerable part of the opening-up and innovation work has been under way and won applause. For example, we expanded the scope and scale of the pilot program enabling Hong Kong and Macao residents to open mainland settlement accounts remotely; the program of "Swap Connect" kicked off; and the market connectivity plans such as Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect, Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect, Bond Connect, and Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect have been continuously improved. Financial opening-up and innovation in the Greater Bay Area is a systematic project that requires multi-party cooperation and concerted efforts. Moving forward, we will implement the strategic arrangements of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, support the development of the financial industry in the Greater Bay Area together with relevant authorities, and enhance the financial services to better serve the real economy, so as to provide solid financial support for building the Hengqin Guangdong-Macao In-depth Cooperation Zone and the Qianhai Shenzhen- Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone. Relevant branches of the PBOC and the SAFE should take the initiative to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant departments, enhance business guidance for financial institutions, and actively promote innovative financial businesses. Financial institutions should organize more in-house training to get a good command of related policies and ensure sound implementation, so as to continuously facilitate investment and financing activites by market entities. Thank you! Date of last update FEB. 24, 2023

Title: Report on the Financial Work of the State Council at the Sixth Session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National Peoples Congress on October 21, 2023
text: Home News & Events Speeches Report on the Financial Work of the State Council at the Sixth Session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National Peoples Congress on October 21, 2023 a To Read Chinese Version Pan Gongsheng, Governor of the Peoples Bank of China (PBOC) Standing Committee of the National Peoples Congress (NPC), According to the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National Peoples Congress on Strengthening the Supervision of Economic Work, the State Council presented the progress of financial work to the NPC for the first time in October 2022. Now, acting on behalf of the State Council, I am here to report on the advancements made in the financial work since Q4 2022 for your deliberation. Under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the financial system resolutely implements the guidelines of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the first and second plenary sessions of the 20th CPC Central Committee. It remains steadfast in upholding and strengthening the Partys overall leadership over financial work. Furthermore, it conscientiously executes the annual plan and relevant resolutions approved by the first session of the 14th NPC. Upholding the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, the financial system applies the new development philosophy fully, faithfully and comprehensively. It continues to deepen the supply-side structural reform of the financial sector and expedites the establishment of a sound modern financial system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Steadily advancing various tasks related to financial reform, development, and stability, it effectively contributes to the sustained recovery and overall improvement of Chinas economy and provides robust support for the realization of Chinese modernization. 1. Main Progress and Achievements The financial system has resolutely implemented the decisions and arrangements of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council. A sound monetary policy has been implemented in a targeted and effective manner. Efforts have also been made to provide stronger support for the real economy, strengthen and improve modern financial regulation, effectively forestall financial risks, and steadily advance financial reform. Additionally, work has also been done to further promote opening-up and earnestly upgrade financial services. As a result, the financial sector has maintained overall stability, with the financial market operating smoothly and financial risks generally under control. In conclusion, new progress has been made in the financial work. (1) Implementation of Monetary Policy The PBOC has implemented a sound monetary policy in a targeted and effective manner, strengthened the counter-cyclical adjustments, given play to the role of monetary policy in adjusting both aggregate and structure, and kept the growth of broad money supply (M2) and the aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) basically in line with the nominal GDP growth. First, the PBOC has enhanced implementation of the sound monetary policy. A mix of monetary policy tools have been used to keep the liquidity adequate at a reasonable level. Since 2023, the PBOC has lowered the required reserve ratio (RRR) twice for financial institutions by a total of 0.5 percentage points, injecting long-term liquidity of over RMB1 trillion. Financial institutions have been guided to keep the credit aggregates appropriate and maintain a stable pace of credit injection. As of end-September 2023, M2 and outstanding AFRE recorded year-on-year growth of 10.3 percent and 9.0 percent respectively, indicating robust support for economic recovery while maintaining the stability of consumer prices. Second, the role of structural monetary policy instruments has been brought into play. Specifically, the PBOC increased the quota for central bank lending for rural development and micro and small businesses (MSBs) as well as central bank discounts by RMB200 billion. Additionally, we raised the quota for central bank lending to support rural development and MSBs by RMB35 billion for areas severely affected by floods. The PBOC also extended the term of inclusive MSB loan facilities and loan support scheme for rental housing to the end of 2024, and extended the term of the loan support scheme to ensure deliveries of presold housing projects to May 2024. Furthermore, we stepped up support for the financing of sci-tech enterprises and continued to make good use of the carbon emission reduction facility (CERF) and the special central bank lending facility for clean and efficient coal use. As of end-September, outstanding structural monetary policy tools totaled RMB7.0 trillion. Third, we have reduced the financing costs for businesses and the consumer credit costs for individuals. Specifically, the PBOC guided open market operation (OMO) reverse repo rate and medium-term lending facility (MLF) rate to decrease by a total of 20 and 25 basis points respectively, bringing down the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) and the over-five-year LPR by a total of 20 and 10 basis points respectively. From January to September, the weighted average interest rate on newly-issued corporate loans stood at 3.91 percent, 0.32 percentage points lower than that in the same period of 2022. In particular, the weighted average interest rate on corporate loans in September posted 3.82 percent, a historic low. Lowering deposit rates would help stabilize liability costs for banks and thus create favorable conditions for bringing down interest rates on corporate loans. We have given full play to the mechanism that allows dynamic adjustments to first-home mortgage rates. In the first nine months, the interest rate on newly-issued individual housing loans was 4.13 percent, 0.88 percentage points lower than that in the same period last year. We promoted a reduction in the interest rates on existing first-home mortgage loans, and nearly 50 million existing home loans, totaling RMB22 trillion, saw an average decrease of 0.73 percentage points in their interest rates. Fourth, we have kept the RMB exchange rate basically stable at an adaptive and equilibrium level. We raised the macro-prudential adjustment parameter for cross- border financing for enterprises and financial institutions and lowered the foreign exchange RRR for financial institutions in a timely manner. Leveraging the China Foreign Exchange Market Self- Regulatory Framework (SRF), we attached importance to guiding expectations and strengthened counter-cyclical adjustments to ensure that the supply and demand in the foreign exchange market remain in equilibrium. The RMB exchange rate has moved in both directions. Despite its slight slide against the US dollar, the RMB has shown a generally upward movement against a basket of currencies. As of end-September, foreign exchange reserves registered USD3,115.1 billion, which remained basically stable. (2) Operation and Regulation of the Financial Sector Financial institutions in the banking, insurance, and securities sectors have witnessed stable performance, and the financial market operate smoothly. First, the operating and regulatory indicators of financial institutions are within a reasonable range. As of end-June 2023, the total assets of financial institutions reached RMB449.21 trillion. The capital adequacy ratio (CAR) and non-performing loan (NPL) ratio of commercial banks hit 14.66 percent and 1.62 percent respectively, the average comprehensive solvency adequacy ratio of insurance companies was 188 percent, and the average risk coverage ratio and average capital leverage ratio of securities companies were 255.38 percent and 18.78 percent respectively. These figures indicate that the overall credit risk remains under control, and the overall loss-absorbing capacity is sufficient. Second, the financial market continues to demonstrate resilience and vitality. To mobilize the capital market and boost investors confidence, we launched a series of policy measures, including optimizing initial public offering (IPO) and refinancing arrangements, regulating the behaviors of shareholding reduction, and reforming public fund rates. The bond market is operating smoothly, with a steady growth in issuance and a historically low interest rate. At end-September, the yield on 10- year government securities decreased by 16 basis points to 2.68 percent from end-December 2022. Third, the financial regulatory system has been improved. We released the Measures for the Administration of Affiliated Transactions of Financial Holding Companies. Additionally, we established a long-term mechanism for the joint regulation on large payment platform enterprises. As a result, we have rectified prominent issues in the financial businesses of Internet platform enterprises, and shifted our focus to normalized regulation. We organized assessment of domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs), and continuously improved the assessment and regulatory frameworks for both SIBs and insurance companies. The reform of the independent director system for listed companies was advanced. Furthermore, we bolstered regulation on the foreign exchange market and improved the authenticity management mechanism for foreign exchange business. We also proactively leveraged regulatory technology to facilitate the digital and intelligent regulation. Fourth, we have intensified law enforcement efforts in financial regulation. From January to September, the PBOC issued a total of 73 administrative penalty decisions on 10 cases, with a cumulative penalty of RMB6.412 billion. The National Administration of Financial Regulation (NAFR) imposed 2,978 punishments on banking and insurance institutions, penalizing 5,512 relevant individuals, with a total amount of penalties and confiscations registering RMB6.312 billion. The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) handled 559 cases, penalizing 518 relevant individuals or entities and transferring 75 criminal cases to public security organs. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) conducted investigations into 502 cases involving illegal and irregular foreign exchange activities. Furthermore, in collaboration with the public security organs, the SAFE took decisive actions against 95 cases involving underground banks and scrutinized 259 cases related to counterparties of underground banks. The penalties and confiscations imposed by the SAFE reached RMB716 million in total. The PBOC has strengthened its regulation on high-risk industries and institutions to combat money laundering. It accelerated the building of an integrated platform for financial anti-fraud, and strictly cracked down on illegal financial activities such as telecom and online fraud and cross-border gambling. Fifth, we have strengthened the financial legal system. We released the Regulation on the Supervision of Private Investment Funds and submitted the Financial Stability Law to the NPC Standing Committee for its first deliberation. The Financial Stability Law, the Law of the Peoples Republic of China on the Peoples Bank of China, the Law of the Peoples Republic of China on Commercial Banks, the Insurance Law of the Peoples Republic of China, and the Anti-Money Laundering Law of the Peoples Republic of China have been incorporated in the first category of the legislative plan of the NPC. The Law of the Peoples Republic of China on Banking Regulation, the Regulations on Non-Bank Payment Institutions, the Regulations on Local Financial Supervision and Administration, the Regulations of the Peoples Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Administration, and the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Listed Companies have been included in the 2023 legislative work plan of the State Council. A coordination mechanism for regular law amendments in the financial sector has been established to promote the progress of amendments in this field. Sixth, we have continuously and severely cracked down on financial corruption. We have taken strict steps to improve the conduct and enforce the discipline of the financial sector, utilizing real-life examples for in-depth education and awareness raising. We have maintained a vigilant focus on key areas and the critical few by strengthening the regulation on young officials. (3) Financial Support for the Real Economy We have further improved the quality and efficiency of financial services for the real economy to create a sound monetary and financial environment for economic rebound. First, we have kept aggregate financing adequate at a reasonable level. From January to September 2023, RMB loans registered an increase of RMB19.75 trillion, and the increment was RMB1.58 trillion more than that in the same period last year. A total of 204 companies on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and Shenzhen Stock Exchange have raised RMB312.5 billion through their IPOs. The net financing of bonds was RMB7.6 trillion, accounting for 25.9 percent of the AFRE (flow). Second, we have provided further support for key areas. As of end-September, outstanding medium and long-term (MLT) loans to the manufacturing sector posted RMB12.09 trillion, up 38.2 percent year on year; and outstanding loans to technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was RMB2.42 trillion, up 22.6 percent year on year. The role of the Sci-Tech Innovation Board (STAR Market), ChiNext, and the Beijing Stock Exchange has been leveraged to meet the financing needs of key & core technology enterprises, sci-tech innovation enterprises, and specialized, sophisticated, distinctive, and innovative enterprises. We have provided support for the construction of public infrastructure for both normal and contingency use in super-large and mega cities, the rebuilding of run-down urban areas, and the construction of government-subsidized housing. The first batch of infrastructure real estate investment trust (REIT) expansion projects have been successfully listed for transactions, and the scope of assets has been expanded to consumer infrastructure and other fields. We have promoted the establishment of a standard system and an information management system for green finance. Third, we have vigorously developed inclusive finance. We have intensified support for the growth of private enterprises and MSBs. As of end-September, outstanding inclusive MSB loans registered RMB28.74 trillion, with a year-on-year growth of 24.1 percent. The loans supported over 61.07 million MSBs, increasing 13.3 percent year on year. We have improved the financial services for rural revitalization and building up Chinas strength in agriculture. As of end-August, Chinas outstanding agro-related loans registered RMB54.98 trillion, growing 15.4 percent year on year. From January to September, the bond market encouraged banks to issue RMB211.5 billion of special financial bonds for MSBs, and RMB46.7 billion of special financial bonds for the agricultural sector, rural areas, and farmers. The insurance sector played an active role in supporting flood prevention, disaster relief, and post-disaster reconstruction projects. As of end-September, the compensation pay-outs and advance pay-outs for 16 disaster-hit provinces (municipalities), including Hebei, Beijing, and Heilongjiang, amounted to RMB7.947 billion. From January to September, 286 insurance futures projects were launched, covering 12 futures varieties including hogs, eggs, and corn. Fourth, basic financial services have been enhanced. We have conducted big data statistics on important basic data, asset management products, and so on. Solid efforts have been made to protect the security of the critical information infrastructure in the financial sector and prudently advance the research and development of e-CNY.
