Title: Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks
Subtitle: Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the Beijing Finance Expo
text: 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan atthe Beijing Finance Expo September 1, 2005, Beijing Steadyprogress has been achieved in Chinas banking reform under the guidance of the CPC centralcommittee and the State Council. In the transition from the planned economy tomarket economy, the government still intervened a lot in the banks internaloperations and the banks have not established sound credit culture, leading tolarge amount of non-performing loans. The improper management system underwhich decision powers were equally distributed from the head office to thebranches and sub-branches as well as the ineffective internal control andinternal incentive system both contributed to the large nonperforming loans ofthe banks. The government has provided enormous support to the banks, and thebanks themselves have also made tremendous efforts to dispose of thenon-performing loans with their existing capital and the profits accumulated inrecent years. In such a context, strengthening the internal control andinternal incentive systems has become one of the most important reform measures.Priority efforts should be made to improve the internal control system of thebanks, promote a sound credit culture and establish effective loan-grantingprocedures. The banks have started to enhance their internal 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 1/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks control, reformthe decision-making process and strengthen the centralization of decisionpowers. On the other hand, the banks will also need to enhance their credit supportto the small and newly established enterprises. In the past, the banks tendedto compete for a few large enterprises. This is not good for the development ofthe entire economy. The State Council has always stressed that, in pursuing thebanking reform, credit support to the small and newly established enterprisesmust be strengthened. We have to learn from past experiences and try to strikea proper balance between banking reform and credit support to small enterprises. Withtechnological advances and financial product innovation, the risk profilefacing the financial sector has changed. There have been less low-riskbusinesses and more high-risk businesses. For example, the hi-tech enterprisesare generally risky. Some newly established small enterprises may also be veryrisky even if they are not engaged in hi-tech business, as they do not havesufficient capital and stable business operation, thus unable to obtainguaranteed or collateralized loans from the banks. We must fully recognize theimportance of small enterprises in the national economy. Meanwhile, thefinancial sector has become increasingly information-based. An important aspectof financial product innovation is the trading of financial risks based on moretransparent information. In particular, the development of credit derivativeshas enabled the banks to effectively control the risks. This has also posed newchallenges to the banks internal control and internal incentive systems. Sincethe risks can be traded in the financial market, the banks should try toachieve a proper balance between risk and return, instead of simply seekingminimum risk. Insome banks and insurance companies, the joint-stock reform and improvement ofcorporate governance are currently underway or have been completed. One of theincentives is to provide stock options for the senior managers. This is animportant feature in the principal-agent relationship and corporate governance.Its effectiveness depends on whether it is 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 2/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks applied properly. One issue is howto define senior managers. Some companies tend to include many people into thiscategory. That may not be good. Of course, it also depends on the nature of thecompany. For commercial banks, if the performance and NPL ratios of differentbranches differ substantially, the use of stock option as an incentive mayproduce negative effect. Moreover, the credit managers, particularly the seniorcredit managers, are believed to be the lifelines for the banks, but theirperformance may differ a lot, and the use of stock options as an incentive maynot be proper. Therefore, the banks must make good use of the internalevaluation and incentive mechanism to enable the senior manages to effectivelyperform their duties. Theabove are the backgrounds against which the following issues will be discussed. First,from the longer-term point of view, the internal control system of the bankscan be designed as a more flexible arrangement. Past experiences show that somegrass-level bank branches performed poorly in their loan business. Their NPLratios were high. Many loans were extended on the basis of special connectionsbetween the bank officials and the customers, and some credit officers evengranted loans in exchange for personal gains. Of course, some branches did agood job in their loan business. Its desirable for the bank head office totake back some power from the branches of poor performance. However, problemsmay arise if the power is unduly concentrated in the head office, as the creditdemand of the small enterprises at the local level may not be met. Moreover, ifthe bank branches no longer extend loans, but only take deposits and conductother business such as fund transfers, their contacts with the localenterprises will become weaker, and they will know less about theseenterprises. In addition, given that its getting increasingly difficult tocompete for large customers, the banks will need to find new ways to developtheir loan business for the medium- and small-sized enterprises, for example,by setting up relevant departments specializing in credit business to theseenterprises. The banks may then face a 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 3/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks dilemma, since they may not havequalified staff to carry out such business, as the local branches have longlost contacts with their corporate customers. Abank should establish a clear restraint mechanism under which its branches willbe removed of loan-granting power if their performances in the credit businessare too poor. However, it is desirable that the branches be left some room forimprovement. For example, instead of completely taking away loan-granting powerfrom the branches, the bank may allow them to do one or two loan businesses peryear. Of course, for those credit managers with very poor performance, theseone or two loans may also turn into non-performing loans. But generallyspeaking, with strengthened internal control, centralization of power, andgradual improvement of decision process, the banks will be able to controltheir loan losses. Whatis more important is the change in economic situation. The small enterpriseshave been playing an increasingly important role in the economy, particularlywith respect to export and employment. Many large enterprises rely on small andnewly established enterprises for the supply of production components and spareparts. The capital market should play a larger role in supporting thedevelopment of these growing enterprises, but currently it is still unable toprovide sufficient financial services. The commercial banks should and can do abetter job in this area. Thesecond issue is regarding the internal incentive system of the bank. The use ofstock options as an incentive for the senior managers has always been a problemin China. As to who should be includedin the senior management, the listed companies tend to give a very broaddefinition. In fact, a distinction must be made between the incentives forsenior managers linked to the overall economic returns and those linked to thespecific performance. For the commercial banks, these two types of incentiveshave different features and should be differentiated clearly. Some loanofficers performed well, while some do a 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 4/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks poor job, so incentives for the seniorcredit managers should not be linked to the overall economic returns of thebanks, but to their own performances. Of course, in some countries, stockoptions are widely used in some large companies, but the amounts differsubstantially, and in those areas where performance varies significantly,internal incentive systems are mainly used. In China, in the past, the state-ownedcommercial banks gave bonus to the staff based on their ranks. Nevertheless, itshould be recognized that the performance of the banks depends critically on anintegral system linking the credit managers, risk control, asset dispositionand back office oversight. Given that performances of the credit managers varysubstantially, an effective incentive system must be set up. Without such asystem, the credit officers may not properly perform their duties. For example,they may only focus on loans to the large or state-owned enterprises, and donot grant loans to the small or privately owned businesses, in order to avoidrisks and troubles. The credit officers may be largely affected by suchnegative incentives. With one single mistake, they may be punished forviolation of regulations or dereliction of duty, and may even be permanentlyprohibited to engage in such business. In sum, improper internal incentiveswill lead to insufficient financial services and undue competition for a fewlarge customers. This is harmful to economic development. Major changes ineconomic structure, such as sharp fluctuations of oil prices, may posesignificant risks to the banks credit to the main sectors and the largeenterprises, and may even lead to systemic risks. How to establish an effectiveincentive system is a major challenge to the commercial banks in their reformprocess. Domestic banks will also face competition from the foreign financialinstitutions that have gradually entered the Chinese market. Some medium- andsmall-sized commercial banks with strong innovative spirit will make rapidprogress in this area. This is an issue that deserves careful attention by allbanks, particularly the large banks. 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 5/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks Thethird issue is the pricing capability. In the transition from planned economyto market economy, Chinahas found itself lack of some abilities, in particular, the pricing capability,for both domestic products and exports. The pricing capability in the financialmarkets is even weaker. This is partly due to the price control system adoptedin the past under which most prices were set by the government and thefinancial institutions had no pricing power, and partly because of the lack ofpricing training for the staff. Moreover, since the enterprises in the pastwere not responsible for their own profits and losses, they did not have theincentives to set their own prices. Without an effective incentive system and aclear business goal, such as maximizing returns for the shareholders, theenterprises will have no incentive to set their own prices, because no matterat what levels they set the prices, some negative effects, including those fromthe media and the customers, may arise. There are mainly two factors that needto be considered in the pricing of credit products. One is the cost of funds.The other is risk premium. The judgment on risk premium often varies, and thecriteria based on which judgment is made also change as time goes. InChina, many new enterprises do not have sufficient capital and their ability toobtain collateralized or guaranteed loans is weak. So pricing of credit tothese enterprises is a very important issue. Restrained access to credit of themedium- and smallsized enterprises is to a large extent due to the ineffectivepricing by the banks. At the end of October 2004, the central bank removed theinterest rate ceilings for loans. Some banks have already made active effortsto improve their pricing capability, and have enhanced their credit support tothe medium- and small-sized enterprises. We hope that other banks can also makeprogress in this area. The organizational structure and incentive system of thefinancial institutions specializing in credit to small enterprises aredifferent from other financial institutions. Reforms have to be made in theabove two areas in order to enhance credit support to the small enterprises. 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 6/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks InChina, many issues, including the state share reform we currently conduct, arerelated to the pricing problem. One of the major problems behind the stateshare reform is the weakness of pricing capability. Whether the financialinstitutions are more affected by market or by the government in pricing thefinancial products is also an issue that deserves attention. In sum, effortsshould be made to develop the pricing capability of the financial institutions. Thereform of the exchange rate regime also involves the pricing issue. The pricingand trading of foreign exchange forward products are related to foreignexchange risks. Ten years ago when the foreign exchange forward transactionswere first introduced to the market, people hoped that the central bank couldbear all the risks. In the past, participants in the life insurance industryalso thought that their interest losses should be born by the government, asthe interest rates were set by the government. Therefore, they are reluctant todo their own risk analysis and take measures to prevent risks. Thefourth issue is concerning the characteristics of the financial institutions.While seeking to avoid excessively large risks, the financial institutions mustalso take some risks and trade these risks. Risk appetites of differentfinancial institutions vary significantly. To avert risks or sell risksinvolves the consideration of market environment and market depth. Instead ofholding the loans till maturity, the banks can now sell the associated risks.On the liability side, asset securitization has also been widely used. The costof fund has changed significantly. Of course, such changes are cyclical, with thecost varying for different periods. At present, the banks find the interestrates in the inter-bank market more attractive than those for deposits. So thebanks need to adopt new risk management strategies. Many financial institutionshave not yet learned how to profit from moderate risk-taking, and have notactively considered trading in the secondary market. This is also related tothe capital adequacy ratio. To what extent the banks can expand their balancesheets depends on the costs of core capital and supplementary capital. Thebanks have to adapt to market changes. Another issue is the risk managementstrategy of the 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 7/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks banks. Regularly paying interests to the depositors, the bankstake relatively low risks. But low risk does not mean no risk. The banks haveto consider how to reduce risk, avoid risk and sell risk. They also have tounderstand that maximum returns for the shareholders and strengthenedcompetitiveness cannot be achieved without taking some risks. The Chinese banksstill need to make improvement in this area. Thecommercial banks and their incentive systems will change significantly when therisks become tradable. Internal problems related to income distribution andincentive mechanism have emerged, and the problems varied significantly amongdifferent banks. In the past, commercial banks and investment banks adoptedquite different practices in this area. However, in recent years, thecommercial banks have adopted some of the investment banks practices. Thekey to the trading of risks is who are the buyers. Of course, to a certainextent, all institutions and investors may tend to take high risk for highreturns, and may be willing to buy risks. But those more willing to assume highrisks are mainly private investment institutions and funds set up throughprivate placement. These funds did not have sufficient room to develop in thepast. Given that the wealth of households and individual is getting increasinglylarger, we will need to take steps to develop these funds, and from the policypoint of view, consider the due market position of these funds. In China, thereare some confusion about the concepts and business scopes of various funds,such as the funds established through private placement, hedge funds, privateequity funds, etc. The market for trading risks needs a relatively large numberof participants. Thefifth issue is regarding competition. All of the above will bring us tremendouschallenges. In fact, we are confronted with double challenges. We have toresolve the old problems and at the same time address the new issues. We arelike athletes competing on the sports ground. We cannot wait to participate inthe new race until our old wounds have been completely 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 8/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks healed. In particular,we have to pay attention to two issues. One is the attitude of the governmenttoward the financial sector. With large risks and some bad cases arising in thepast, the financial sector may have left a bad impression on the public.However, we have to admit that the economy will not develop soundly without thesupport of the financial sector. Take the rural financial institutions as anexample. The government has to help lift the rural financial institutions outof heavy historical burdens. Otherwise, they will not be able to providesufficient support to the development of the rural economy. It is veryimportant for the government to remove unwarranted controls and encouragefinancial innovation in order to improve financial services to the small andnewly established enterprises and the rural economy. On the other hand, thegovernment should also strengthen its supervision over the market so as totimely identify and resolve problems. We have made substantial progress in thisarea, but will still need to make further efforts. Willthe competition among banks strengthen? Over the past five to seven years, onecommon goal of the commercial banks has been to reduce non-performing loans.When this task has been largely fulfilled, other work will be put onto theagenda, and competition will become increasingly intense. For example, thebanks will focus more on the retail business, the credit card business, themarket for trading risks, as well as on their customers. All these require thebanks to adopt a different operating strategy, and the sensitivity of differentbanks to these changes will be different. Moreover, the businesses of differenttypes of financial institutions have become increasingly overlapped. Forinstance, a commercial bank can arrange a syndicate loan and then sell it toother investors. These investors may be those who are willing to buy creditproducts, asset securitization products or credit derivatives products. Theymay also be investors in the securities market. And they may be either Chineseor foreigners. Another example is life insurance. The insurance companies areundergoing enormous changes, and life insurance 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 9/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks has been bearingcharacteristics similar to those of savings products. Long-term savings are nowbeing invested in a greater variety of products, and have played a greater rolein the market. The insurance companies can also trade risks in the market. Thechallenges brought by strengthened competition require the banks to take a moreactive attitude and set up incentive systems that are adaptable to changes insituation. Under more intense competition, different approaches and practiceswill produce significantly different results. Meanwhile, such competition will enablethe financial sector to better serve the national economy. The areas where wedid not do well in the past, such as rural financial services, credit to smalland newly established enterprises, are expected to see big improvement in thefuture. Thecentral bank and other macroeconomic departments of the government are thusconfronted with many challenges, and will need to deeply consider many issues.We do not want to see excessive concentration of financial services in acertain area or to a certain group of customers, or the so-called herd effect,as it will make the economy vulnerable. We need to be prudent in issuing rulesand regulations. Some of these rules and regulations may lead to excessiveconcentration rather than diversity and flexibility. Some targets or reward andpunishment measures have resulted in distortion and depression of financialproducts and services. We need to seriously consider the issues related to thetransformation of financial services. As information and market structurechange rapidly, the keep-a-distance approach that has long been adopted by thecommercial banks is now being challenged, requiring us to take policy measuresaccordingly. In sum, the challenges and tasks we face at the macro level are asgreat as those at the micro level. 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 10/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks Date of last update SEP. 26, 2005 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 11/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Reform of the internal control and internal incentive systems of the commercial banks 3688110/3688175/3708110/index.html 12/12

Title: Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work
Subtitle: Speech of Mr Zhou Xiaochuan, Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 2nd working session of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML.
text: 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work Speech of Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan, Governor of the Peoples Bank of China at the 2nd working session of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML September 2, 2005 Colleagues: In line with the Agenda of the Joint Ministerial Conference on Anti-money Laundering (AML), we convene today the 2nd working session of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML. Leaders of the State Council have paid high attention to this session and designated Mr. You Quan, Vice Secretary-General of the State Council to attend the meeting and give us a speech. On behalf of the Joint Ministerial Conference, I would like to make a work report as follows. I. Developments of Anti-money Laundering since the inception of the Joint Ministerial Conference 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 1/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work Since the 1st working session of the Joint Ministerial Conference in August 2004, all member agencies, in accordance with the Agenda of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML, have performed their respective functions and made full use of the mechanism of coordination, producing encouraging results in anti-money laundering. I.1. The mechanism of coordination for AML was preliminarily established in line with Chinas actual conditions. In December 2004, the Agenda of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML (hereinafter referred to as the Agenda) was approved by the State Council and distributed to all member agencies. The Agenda clearly defined the organizational system for AML in China and division of responsibilities in AML of all relevant government agencies. The mechanism of coordination for AML took its initial shape in line with Chinas actual conditions. In the past year, inter-agency collaboration proceeded gradually. In December 2004, a high-ranking delegation of FATF (Financial Action Task Force) visited China. During the visit, such member agencies as the Peoples Bank of China (PBC), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Finance (MOF), the Ministry of Justice, China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC), China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), China Insurance Regulatory Commission (CIRC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and the Budgetary Work Committee of the NPC Standing Committee collaborated proactively and completed successfully the talks with the delegation, ensuring that China became an observer of FATF in January 2005. Under the framework of the Joint Ministerial Conference, the Ministry of Public Security, the PBC and the SAFE have established closer collaborative relationship. In March 2005, the Ministry of Public Security and the PBC jointly promulgated the Rules for Cooperation in Cross-investigation on Clues of Suspicious Activities. The Rules instituted the mechanism for contacts, coordination, joint surveillance and intelligence consultations between the economic 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 2/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work investigation departments of the Ministry of Public Security and AML departments of the PBC, effectively spurring investigation and prosecution of money laundering cases. After the Agenda of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML was distributed to all governments at the provincial level, there have formed, with active support of local governments, the coordination mechanism for AML among relevant departments in 12 provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under Central Government and cities with independent budget by June 2005. In some focal regions for AML, the relevant mechanism for AML was also established among agencies at the prefecture level. I.2. Actively promoting construction of the legal system on AML. In March 2004, the Budgetary Work Committee of NPC Standing Committee initiated legislation of the Anti-money Laundering Law, with member agencies of the Joint Ministerial Conference participating in the drafting of the Law. With conscientious and meticulous work, headways have been made in drawing up the Anti-money Laundering Law. In view of too narrow provisions of upstream crimes of money laundering and too strict stipulation of major subjective components of crimes of money laundering in Article 191 of the current Criminal Law, the drafting group of the Anti-money Laundering Law conducted research on revision of stipulations of crimes of money laundering in the Criminal Law. At the start of 2003, the PBC promulgated the Rules for Anti-money Laundering by Financial Institutions, the Administrative Rules for the Reporting of Large-value and Suspicious RMB Payment Transactions and the Administrative Rules for the Reporting by Financial Institutions of Large-value and Suspicious Foreign Exchange Transactions. Their implementation over the 2-plus years has vigorously promoted the anti-money laundering by the banking sector in China. With gradual deepening 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 3/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work of anti-money laundering, however, limitation of the above rules was revealed gradually and it became difficult for them to meet the requirements of developments of anti-money laundering. At present, the PBC is organizing resources to overhaul the rules. The new rules after revision will underline scientific and information-oriented supervision in AML, pay attention to effectively controlling AML costs while implementing prevention and controls against money laundering. In order to actively perform the responsibilities of guiding and deploying AML in the financial industry, the PBC has since 2004 initiated the drafting of AML rules and regulations in the securities and insurance sectors in cooperation with other related financial regulatory bodies. I.3. Organizing in an all-round way the AML examination in the banking sector During April-December 2004, the PBC organized nationwide the first specialized examination on AML in commercial banks. In terms of results of the examination, most commercial banks have established internal control system of AML, performed well their responsibilities in customer identification, record-keeping of transactions and the reporting of large-value and suspicious activities. In view of such problems as inadequate internal control system of AML, non-reporting and un-timely reporting of suspicious activities in some commercial banks, the PBC enforced punishments in conformity with legal provisions. The examination played a positive role in getting a complete picture of implementation of AML rules and regulations in the banking industry, sharpening awareness of commercial banks in attaching importance to AML. The examination also accumulated precious experience in conducting AML supervision in securities and insurance sectors and even in non-financial sectors with high risks of money laundering in future. In 2005, the PBC continued the specialized examinations on AML by commercial banks in separate provincial regions. 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 4/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work I.4. AML funds monitoring played an important role in investigation and prosecution of money laundering cases. In order to perform the role of AML funds monitoring, with the approval of the State Commission Office for Public Sector Reform, the PBC set up the AML Monitoring and Analysis Center in April 2004, responsible for receiving and analyzing reports of large-value and suspicious activities in RMB and foreign currencies. Since the establishment of the Center, it has networked with 17 commercial banks in data reporting. Its cumulative number of suspicious activities reports (SARs) in both RMB and foreign currencies posted 654,400 , amounting to RMB248.023 billion yuan and USD76.92 billion and covering nationwide 30plus provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities. By means of identification, analysis and investigation of SARs, increasingly more money laundering related cases were cleared up through referrals to departments of public security. According to incomplete statistics, since April 2004, the PBC and the SAFE have altogether referred more than 1,500 clues to departments of public security at various levels. In particular, they helped solve 51 cases, involving RMB3.096 billion yuan and USD460 million and relating to various fronts of money laundering activities like underground banks, overseas gambling on ball sports, money laundering through investment, smuggling, illegal purchase and sale of foreign exchange etc. I.5. AML international cooperation made significant progress. Through concerted efforts of the PBC, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Public Security and the MOF, China, together with Russia, founded the Eurasian Group on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (EAG). In January 2005, 33 members of FATF passed a unanimous decision through voting to accept China as an observer, signifying an 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 5/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work important stride in Chinas AML international cooperation. In April 2005, China successfully sponsored the Second Plenum of EAG, enhancing Chinas influence in the field of international anti-money laundering. Over the past year, member agencies of the Joint Ministerial Conference on AML has in succession sent delegations for plenums of FATF and EAG, visited AML organizations in USA and Canada, invited AML experts from such countries and regions as USA, Germany, UK, Luxemburg and Hong Kong for academic exchanges and seminars in China, and conducted productive consultations and cooperation on AML with such international organizations as the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and some related nations and regions. In terms of bilateral cooperation, China has begun AML cooperation with such countries as USA, Russia and Canada, strengthened AML cooperation with Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Regions. International cooperation has shifted its focus from the policy area to practical work area. I.6. Strengthening AML education and training Over the past year, AML education and training was further strengthened. Since August 2004, member agencies have organized various activities of AML education and training. As the leading agency in the Joint Ministerial Conference, the PBC organized over 10 AML workshops and training sessions, compiled and distributed 2004 China AML Report, AML Briefing and Reading Material on AML. The PBC also designated 2005 as the AML Publicity Year, publicizing basic AML knowledge through the media. Such member agencies as the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of State Security added contents of AML into their training. The Budgetary Work Committee of NPC Standing Committee organized two international seminars on laws of AML, effectively sharpening awareness of the general public on harmfulness of money laundering and urgency of cracking down on money laundering. 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 6/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work II. Major work in AML in the coming period Over the past year, effective work in AML by all member agencies has created conditions for in-depth development of AML in future. At present, either government bodies, financial institutions or special non-financial industries have fostered deeper understanding of and higher requirements for deepening AML, laying foundation for further implementing AML. At present, the Central Committee of CPC has put forward the requirements of implementing the scientific development concept, improving the system of socialist market economy, building socialist harmonious society and instituting and perfecting the system for prosecuting and preventing corruption with equal stress on education, institutional buildup and supervision. The requirements provide good opportunities of implementing AML in depth. To this end, we should grasp the opportunities and do our work well in a steady and down-to-earth manner. II.1. Steadily promoting mechanism innovation in AML under the guidance of the scientific development concept We shall research on establishing the long-term mechanism of coordination for AML. AML is a long-term mandate. All member agencies shall further strengthen coordination and synergy on the basis of improvement of the Joint Ministerial Conference. In particular, in terms of international cooperation and case investigation and prosecution, we shall not only solidify existing results but also make breakthroughs in such significant issues as joining the FATF and investigating major illegal cases. The General Office of the Joint Ministerial Conference, in the light of major fronts and prominent issues at present and in the coming period, shall research on instituting the mechanism for regular and ad hoc analyses, discussions and judgments concerning major issues among agencies for AML. It shall research, at the level of concrete AML work, on programs for sharing information and resources of AML supervision, in a bid to raise efficiency and standards of utilizing AML information. 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 7/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work We shall research on establishing AML network system in line with Chinas actual conditions. All member agencies shall, from the perspective of safeguarding state security, combating corruption and advocating honest and clean government and safeguarding the long-term stability of socialist market economic order, speed up research on standardized and scientific organizational setup and functional Agenda for AML. We shall explore ways of extending AML into grass-roots organizations and shall further straighten out and optimize procedures for AML as well as bring out synergy in AML through organizational setup and functional improvement and through full guarantee of personnel, funds and information. II.2. Sharpening awareness of urgency in legal construction on AML to speed up AML legislation We must actively participate in and promote the enactment of the AML Law and speed up revision of relevant articles of the Criminal Law. Enactment of the AML Law and revision of articles concerning crimes of money laundering in the Criminal Law, are not only the objective need of domestic AML but also the urgent requirements by international AML cooperation. The legislation will reflect practical needs of AML in China as well as draw on successful experience of international AML practices, thus developing legal norms of AML in line not only with Chinas actual conditions but also with international standards. We shall beef up developing and improving AML rules and regulations in line with division of responsibilities stipulated in the Agenda of Joint Ministerial Conference on AML. At present, some industries with high risk of money laundering are still not familiar with AML. Related member agencies shall strengthen research on rules for AML supervision, and shall develop and improve AML rules and regulations as soon as possible. II.3. Strengthening AML supervision in an all-round way in line with the principle of laying equal stress on prevention and crackdown 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 8/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work First, we shall bring into play the role of the financial industry as the first line of defense in AML. Financial regulatory bodies shall conscientiously sum up their experience in AML supervision of the banking industry. We shall expand AML supervision into the securities and insurance sectors in a sequenced manner. We shall urge and guide relevant institutions to establish and improve internal control system, improve operational procedures and perform earnestly the duties in AML. We shall explore gradually the effective AML supervision system covering the whole financial field in line with Chinas actual conditions, in an effort to effectively control risks of money laundering confronted by financial institutions and to safeguard reputation of financial institutions. By doing so, we can foster favorable institutional climate to honor the promises for WTO accession of fully opening the financial industry to the outside in 2006. Second, we shall include specific non-financial industries into the scope of AML supervision as soon as possible. Relevant member agencies shall beef up study on establishing the system of AML supervision in such industries with high risk of money laundering as legal counseling, accounting, real estate and auction. By developing industrial rules, regulations and guidance, we shall urge and guide the supervised institutions to improve their operational procedures of AML in line with international standards and to perform their duties in AML in real earnest, in a bid to provide support for preventing and striking various kinds of money laundering. Third, in view of inadequate emphasis on and cooperation for AML by very few financial institutions, financial regulatory bodies shall urge relevant institutions to sharpen their awareness and to improve AML performance. Financial regulatory bodies shall continuously improve their modes of supervision and standardize their procedures. They shall not only perform well communication and education but also uphold the principle that law enforcement must be strict and violators must be punished. 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 9/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work II.4. Speeding up the process of AML by taking advantage of the deepening international cooperation in AML Chinas AML started at a late date and was confronted with the practical pressure of being brought in line with the international standards without experiencing a transition period. Whether or not we could make progress in AML in face of pressure and advance AML to a new level, constitute a major challenge to all member agencies of the Joint Ministerial Conference. All member agencies shall do jobs well in the spirit of researching in an active way, taking initiative in AML work, seeking benefits while avoiding harms and making others experience serve ourselves. We shall enhance our awareness of the importance of deepening international cooperation in AML. AML work is a completely new course. We shall continuously explore and improve in practice. We shall also draw on good foreign experience and practices. Participation in international cooperation in AML will serve to propel Chinas AML work. All member agencies shall enhance awareness of the significance of international cooperation in AML. We shall take consistent measures and continue to deepen international cooperation in terms of legislation, law enforcement, funds monitoring and AML training on a reciprocal basis and implement bilateral cooperation with related countries and regions. By doing so, we can make preparation for tracking down criminals fleeing overseas, recovering funds transferred overseas by criminal means and participating in drawing up international AML rules. We shall do our best for assessment by the FATF. Assessment by and accession to FATF constitutes an important item in terms of international cooperation in AML at present. With FATF assessment evolving in the past several years, its standards have been upgraded continuously and the requirements of the subject applicants become ever stricter. Assessment is a full examination of our achievements in AML, spurring ourselves to rectify our weaknesses and inadequacies in our current AML 3688110/3688175/3708113/index.html 10/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Strengthening Domestic Coordination and Promoting International Cooperation to Improve Anti-money Laundering Work work. All member agencies must attach great importance to the impending assessment, make preparations meticulously and collaborate closely, in a bid to ensure its success. Colleagues, we have attained initial achievements in AML with concerted efforts from all member agencies. All walks of life have continuously enhanced their understanding of AML. The leaders of the Central Committee and the State Council are placing great hopes for the AML work. In January 2005, Vice Premier Huang Ju, when coming to see the delegates attending the annual working conference of the PBC, put forward the requirements that you shall continuously improve the mechanism of AML work, upgrade the level of AML work and further enhance the AML work well from the vantage point of perfecting the system of socialist market economy, building up effective and clean government and ruling the nation in the interest of the people. That immensely encourages and urges us to do the AML work well. Chinas AML is still confronted with myriads of difficulties in the coming period. It presents us with an enormous challenge to grasp the opportunities to improve the AML work in an all-round way. All member agencies shall, from the vantage point of perfecting the system of socialist market economy and ruling the nation in the interest of the people, deepen our understanding of the import of the AML work, continue to strengthen domestic coordination, promote international cooperation, work in a down-to-earth manner and strive to create a new situation of AML in China. Title: Transcript of Speech on the Inauguration Ceremony of Bank of China Co.
text: 26/10/2021, 10:49 Transcript of Mr. Zhou Xiaochuans Speech on the Inauguration Ceremony of Bank of China Co. Transcript of Mr. Zhou Xiaochuans Speech on the Inauguration Ceremony of Bank of China Co. Respectedguests, ladies and gentlemen, GoodMorning. First of all, please allow me, on behalf of the Leading Office of theState Council for Pilot Joint-Stock Reform of the State-Owned Commercial Banks,to congratulate on the incorporation of Bank of China Co. Establishedin 1912, Bank of China has had a history of about 100 years. It is the home ofhistory not only for a commercial bank, but also for Chinas banking industry that has longpursued restructuring to promote national independence and restoration. Afterthe 1911 Revolution, Chinas banking system was almost thoroughly overwhelmed by theforeign banks. Bank of China, however, struggled to strengthen nationalfinancial industry and pioneered in comprehensively introducing into China the advanced experiencesof international banks. Several decades later, Bank of China became a competitivecounterpart of foreign banks and a flagship of Chinas financial industry. Following thefounding of the PRC, Bank of China quickly transformed itself into an importantfinancial force in the course of socialist construction. In particular, Bank ofChina served as a bridge between China and the rest of the world taking advantage of itsrelatively complete international network in the period before reform and openingup when China was almost isolated fromthe international community. Since 3688110/3688175/3708176/index.html 1/4 26/10/2021, 10:49 Transcript of Mr. Zhou Xiaochuans Speech on the Inauguration Ceremony of Bank of China Co. the commencement of the reform and openingup, Bank of China has transformed itself from a bank specialized in foreignexchange and trade related business into a state-owned commercial bank, makinggreat progress in market expansion and financial innovation. Iremember, in the past my colleagues in Bank of China often like to compare itwith Bank of Tokyo in Japan, as both banks used to specialize in foreign exchange andtrade related business. But where is Bank of Tokyo now? In 1996, Bank of Tokyomerged with Mitsubishi Bank, creating the largest bank in Japan then. In August 2004,Mitsubishi Tokyo Financial Group further merged with UFJ, thus establishing thelargest financial group in terms of asset size in the world. The new financialgroup is named Mitsubishi-UFG. The familiar name Bank of Tokyo disappeared.This story indicates that in the fiercely competitive international financialmarket, only those that keep reforming and pioneer in financial innovation can surviveand grow. Today,with the rapid development of economic and financial globalization, China has become an importantpart of the world financial market. In 2006, Chinas financial industry will opencomprehensively to foreign competition and the financial market will, to alarger extent, be integrated with the global financial system. We will facefierce competition from foreign financial institutions with robust financialstrength, sound governance, strong ability of financial innovation and richexperiences in international competition. The Chinese banks, including Bank ofChina, will have to establish competitive advantage by conducting furtherinternal reforms in an effort to assume the historic responsibility of risingup to the challenge of foreign banks, actively taking part in internationalfinancial competition and revitalizing national financial industry. 3688110/3688175/3708176/index.html 2/4 26/10/2021, 10:49 Transcript of Mr. Zhou Xiaochuans Speech on the Inauguration Ceremony of Bank of China Co. Toconduct joint-stock reform of the state-owned commercial banks and establishmodern banking system are an important decision made by the Communist PartyCentral Committee and the State Council. The reform has a profound bearing onthe success of overall financial reform, the future of Chinas national financial industry andeconomic development. Today, we celebrate here the incorporation of Bank ofChina Co. which marks a milestone of the historic reform. However,incorporation is not the ultimate objective of the joint-stock reform of thestate-owned commercial banks. The key is to transform operational mechanism. Inthis regard, Bank of China continues to face daunting tasks of reform anddevelopment. Ihope that Bank of China Co., under the leadership of the Communist PartyCentral Committee and the State Council, can further strengthen its sense ofhistorical responsibility and urgency and seize the opportunity to deepenreform, improve corporate governance and internal control mechanism, transformmanagement perception and operational mechanism, strengthen capital constraint,improve service and enhance efficiency. With these efforts, we expect Bank ofChina to become an internationally competitive modern commercial bank withstandard corporate governance, adequate capital, strong internal control, safemanagement, and sound and efficient service. Inconclusion, I would like to once again, on behalf of the Leading Office of theState Council for Pilot Joint-Stock Reform of the State-Owned Commercial Banks,to send my best wishes for the incorporation and future of Bank of China Co. Thankyou.
