Title: Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform
Subtitle: Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the Conference of Chinese Economists Society
text: 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the Conference of the Chinese Economists Society Beijing, China, June 20, 2004 Inmy mind, the topic of this conference Private Enterprises and SustainableGrowth is of profound significance for the Chinese economic development. Atpresent, though a certain number of banks have been incorporated in the form ofjointstocks, they are not truly privately owned and most of the Chinese banksare still under the control of the state. Future financial institutions in therural areas are the most likely credit organizations to be privatized in China and they constitute animportant factor for the development of the rural economy. Bearing this inmind, I would like to share with you some of my observations on the reform ofthe rural financial system, which are of close relevance to the theme of todaysconference. I. Definitions of rural financial reform Ruralfinancial reform could either be narrowly defined or broadly defined. If broadlydefined, rural financial reform comprises issues ranging from policy andcommercial financial business as well as innovation and development offinancial 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 1/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform intermediation in the rural areas to the building of continuouspositive incentives and exit mechanisms for rural financial institutions,managing agricultural production based on business orders, the cultivation ofagricultural produces futures market and the development of agricultureinsurance. Such a broad rural financial reform has been on the governmentsagenda for a considerable period of time. After the conclusion of the NationalFinancial Work Conference in 2002, the State Council has established a Special Committeeon Deepening Reform of the Rural Financial System and the Rural Credit Cooperatives(the Committee hereinafter) comprising various agencies including the PeoplesBank of China, the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry of Finance, theAgricultural Bank of China and the Agricultural Development Bank of China.Based on numerous discussions and field investigations, the Committee submitteda special report to the State Council in the fourth quarter of 2003, in whichmany proposals and insights on rural financial reform were examined andrecommended for further decisive actions. Anarrowly defined rural financial reform refers to the undergoing reform of therural credit cooperatives (RCCs). According to the Circular on Deepening thePilot Reform of the RCCs promulgated by the State Council on June 27, 2003,the China Banking Regulatory Commission is responsible for the execution of thereform program, the local governments play their role in supervising, guiding,coordinating and assisting the implementation of the reform scheme while thePeoples Bank of China takes the responsibility for the design, review andapproval of the financial support arrangement. RCCs willing to participate inthe pilot reform are selected by the local provincial (municipal) governmentsand reported on a voluntary basis to the China Banking Regulatory Commissionfor deliberation before they are finally approved the State Council. Startingfrom the second half of 2003, reform of the RCCs has been introduced on a pilotbasis in 8 provinces (municipalities), and has since achieved good progress. 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 2/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 II. Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Three factors to be emphasized in the currentround of rural financial reform 1. Relationsbetween the rural economy and the rural finance: commensal, co-existent ormutually supportive? Differentfrom past reform endeavors, the distinction of this round of rural financialreform lies in the new broad consensus reached within the Committee onrelations between the rural economy and the rural finance. In the past, moreemphasis has been placed on pressing credit support by the rural financialinstitutions at a cut-throat price to the development of the agriculturalindustry, the farmers and the rural economy. With the newly emerged consensus,people come to realize that the development of the rural economy and thebusiness of rural finance share a relationship of commensal and coexistence,which could mutually benefit to grow in parallel. If for instance, take therural economy as a human body, rural finance will be an important organ in it,which both lives on and serves the human body. It is definitely not an outsidesupportive instrument grabbed occasionally as needed only for repetitive useand never for maintenance and blood transfusion. In the past, whenever thecredit support line for agricultural industry ran into difficulty, ruralfinancial institutions would be the first to blame and consequently were forcedto increase loan extension, while few paid attention to the health andsustainability of these institutions, which put them in a situation offinancially unviable and waiting for emergency bailout. In such a condition,it would be impossible for the rural financial institutions to grant moresupport to the development of the rural economy. InChinas case, we currentlyhave more than 32,000 RCCs which have long functioned both as the commercialand the policy financial institutions. With the government consistentlystressing the importance of the agricultural industry in the Chinese economy,the RCCs have been loaded with many policy financial tasks usually performedwith the charged lending rates falling 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 3/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform short of the cost-effective level. Thereason behind the failure of the RCCs rests more with the excessiveadministrative intervention and less with mismanagement. Faced with conflictingoperational targets, an institution would find it very difficult to trulyimprove its financial situation by following the commercial principles; ratherit is more likely to see a rise of the NPL ratio and an accumulation of losses.For example, based on the strict loan classification standard, the NPL ratio ofthe RCCs as a whole once reached as high as 50 percent in the two or threeyears immediately following the Asian financial crisis. The net value of theRCCs as a whole was deep down in the negative territory and the amount of losswas two or three times that of their book-value capital. Strapped in such ahigh level of negative net value and NPL ratio, the RCCs simply lacked theability to provide continuous financial service to the agricultural industry. Inthe meantime, unprofitable rural financial business and the undergoingcommercial orientation reform have deterred the Agricultural Bank of Chinagradually away from the rural areas to shift its business focus to the cities,while another important component of the rural financial system, the postalsavings institutions have siphoned massive deposits in the rural areas whichare only to be re-deposited in other financial institutions and not used tosupport the agricultural industry as they are not allowed to issue loans. Whilemost people attribute the competitiveness of the postal savings institutions indeposit taking to preferential policies and institutional advantages, some listthe low efficiency of the RCCs as an important reason for fund outflow from therural areas. In the eyes of many people, postal savings institutions acted likea water pump, exhausting financial resources in the rural areas. Underthese circumstances, the central bank provided financial resources mainlythrough the facility of central bank lending to the RCCs so as to ensure theircredit support to the rural economy. As a matter of fact, financial supportfrom the central bank has enabled the RCCs to even increase aggregate ruralloans after the Asian financial crisis (after 1999 in particular). However, 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 4/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Itis well known that central bank lending cannot be used for the above-mentionedpurpose and whether it can be finally recovered also remains a question.Therefore, supporting rural financial institutions through the facility ofcentral bank lending itself is a kind of exogenous push and not a long-standingand sustainable solution to the embedded problems. Ifpolicy financial support is deemed as an exogenous boost for the rural economy,commercial rural credit business then enters a relationship with the ruraleconomy that could be best described as an endogenous co-existence. Such arelationship demands for quality and sustainable commercial rural creditinstitutions operating in good health. Despite the fact that commercial ruralcredit institutions find it hard to survive in those poverty-stricken areas,which covers about 10 percent of Chinas administrative regions, and needpolicy financial support to fill the credit business gap, the majority of thevast Chinese rural areas has both the ability and the need to cultivate asteady growth of the financially healthy and viable commercial financialinstitutions. 2. Interestrates: deregulation vs. control Thereare two different views on the pricing of loans in the rural areas. The firstconventional wisdom prefers to set the interest rates charged for loans grantedto the agricultural sector, the rural areas and the farmers at a depressedlevel based on the thinking that grain production and the agricultural industryremain a top priority of the Chinese economy that warrants preferential treatment.However, micro credit business in the rural areas usually is scattered andcomes with high cost. As statistics showed there existed a relatively highratio of default in this business. In the case lending rates are set throughadministrative means rather than based on the market principles, ruralfinancial institutions will find themselves unable to use interest rates tocover their risk premium which in turn could cause a damage to the financialsituation and the 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 5/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform viability of the these institutions. The second sort of viewadvocates a gradual break from the conventional wisdom and move towards settinga band for interest rates to float within. In the current round of ruralfinancial reform, one important measure is the introduction of a loan interestrate band for the RCCs which is wider than that set for the commercial banks.By doing this, rural financial institutions could manage to survive andsteadily expand their business to serve the development of the rural economy.Not surprisingly, some people are uncomfortable with this practice, and theyeven turn to accuse the RCCs for not giving enough support to the rural economyby charging excessively high interest rates. 3. Cooperativemechanism Cooperativemechanism has long been adopted in the organization of Chinas rural economic activities.Agricultural production was coordinated by production cooperatives, procurementand marketing of agricultural produces were conducted through the supply and marketingcooperatives and financial service was provided through the creditcooperatives. Thanks to economic development, price liberalization andinstitutional changes over the past many years, farmers across China have increasinglyselected to withdraw from this kind of cooperative arrangement and no longerregarded those RCCs burdened with large net losses and high NPL ratios aspartnership organizations in which they could take shares to enjoy qualityfinancial services. Ina considerable period of time, the government also takes the RCCs as the quasistate-owned financial institutions and always stands ready to provide bailoutsupport to any such institutions facing severe payment risks. Not a singlerural credit cooperative has been allowed to go bust and all depositors areassured to get their principals and interests 100 percent paid. Lack of bankruptcyarrangement, the last resort of market exit, usually leads to adverse selectionand moral hazard. 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 6/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Despitethe fact that RCCs have performed differently across the country and there havebeen some success stories, the current round of reform will not emphasize as inthe past on the cooperative structure of the RCCs, but rather shift to stressthe importance of learning the successful experience in enterprises reform andintroducing the joint-stock or cooperative share- holding system to restructurethe RCCs. Inthe past, people tended to see credit cooperatives as a kind of community-basedfinancial institutions which should not be necessarily subject to the capitaladequacy ratio requirements applicable to the commercial banks. However, as animportant barometer measuring the health and sustainability of the financialinstitutions, capital adequacy ratio is not only a selfimposed discipline butalso a reflection of a financial institutions capability to deter risks. Ifincorporated as a joint-stock institution, a rural credit cooperative mush haveadequate capital in place to fend off risks. While few has challenged thecooperative institutional arrangement of the rural financial institutions sincethere are also successful experiences associated with credit cooperatives insome other countries, what is worthy particular attention is that, in thecurrent round of reform, the same criteria should be laid for the RCCs in termsof capital adequacy ratio, risk control set-up and NPL disposal, whether theyare incorporated in line with the joint-stock or the cooperative structure . Onsuch a count, exploration and innovation should be encouraged to introduce morediversity to the institutional arrangement of the rural financial institutions,not focusing only on the uniform model adopted across the whole country in thepast. III. Some directions for the central banks financialsupport to the reform of the RCCs Basedon above deliberations, initiatives have been taken on two tiers to reform therural financial services in China. The first initiative related to the pilot reform of theRCCs introduced in 8 provinces in the second half of 2003, which was laterexpanded 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 7/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform to cover most of the provinces in the summer of 2004. In this reformprocess, I could summarize the role played by the central bank as recognizingand relieving historical burdens of the RCCs, providing positive incentives ona continuous basis, and preventing downside risks and moral hazards. The secondinitiative associated with the broad reform of the rural financial system,including determining the role of policy financial institutions in the ruralareas, restructuring the postal savings system, developing order-basedagricultural production, and introducing insurance and futures trading foragricultural produces, etc. These measures on various reform fronts have yet tobe gradually transformed into concrete policies to be carried out in differentphases. 1. Recognizingand relieving historical burdens Aspreviously stated, the accumulation of non-performing loans in the RCCs couldbe attributed to the administrative intervention by the governments, overdraftby the fiscal authorities at the grass-root levels as well as mismanagement ofthe RCCs themselves and the deficiencies of the loan pricing mechanisms. Loansissued by the RCCs are widespread and mostly concentrated in the grass-rooteconomy, thus very difficult to supervise and monitor though the bankingregulatory authority did maintain limited presence in there. In principle, theRCCs should be urged in the first place to dispose of the risks caused byself-mismanagement so as to lay a solid moral foundation for future reform, anddisciplinary penalties should be imposed on those accountable for theirrecoverable losses. But in practice, accountability for these losses is hardto establish and also there are no effective mechanisms to supervise lossrecovery. In these circumstances, losses have become historical burdens thathave to be disposed of by the state through different channels, in the hopethat the rehabilitated RCCs can assume their role in providing qualityfinancial services to the rural economy and can steadily grow financiallystrong. Rural financial reform can only be advanced after giving a fairrecognition to the fact that the historical burdens of the RCCs are the resultsof 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 8/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform economic transition in the early period of reform when the demarcation linebetween the enterprises and the government was blurred and the price mechanism distorted. Whyemphasizing on this issue? Because some people nowadays still turn a blind eyeto this like an ostrich. In their view, great progress has been made in thereform of the RCCs over the recent years and the micro credit has been provedquite an effective support to the farmers. If the central bank can sustain its financialsupport for a period of 20, 30 or 50 years, the RCCs will probably be able togradually dispose of their historical burdens. In my view, a timeframe of 20-50years is simply too long. Thereare two ways to get rid of the historical losses. The first way is to let thecentral bank continue to provide concessionary loans to the RCCs which wouldenable them to benefit from the interest spreads so that they could graduallydispose of the historical losses. The other way is to use the central bankbills, as designed by the monetary policy department of the Peoples Bank ofChina, under which the state will bear half of the net losses with the otherhalf to be absorbed by the RCCs themselves. At the same time, the RCCs will beallowed to keep any recovered assets so that they will have the incentives tofurther pursue bad assets disposal. After receiving financial support from thecentral bank, the RCCs will be urged to rely on themselves to increase capitaland improve corporate governance and internal control through joint-stock restructuring. 2. Providingpositive incentives on a continuous basis Ina teachers view, it may be a bit more easy to establish incentives for astudent performing above the average level, but much more difficult to do sofor a student least attentive to his or her performance. This example may notfit well with the reform of RCCs, but we hope positive incentives could beextensively provided on a continuous basis to cover more RCCs with differentperformance. In the process of financial restructuring, the RCCs should beencouraged to ascend the ladder of 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 9/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform incentives step by step. The first step isthat the RCCs which have opted to participate in the reform process and thelocal governments at different levels must make a commitment to the reformprogram, only with that will the state provide them with financial support and preferentialpolicies in NPL disposal. The second step will be for the RCCs to work had todispose of non-performing loans while at the same time try to increase capitalso as to bring the capital adequacy ratio from in the negative territory up tozero. You may find it hard to believe when I mention zero capital adequacyratio. But just as I said before the aggregate net value of the RCCs is deepdown on the negative side, so it will even not be easy for it to move up to thezero level. After that, the Peoples Bank of China may use specially issuedcentral bank bills to buy non-performing loans of the RCCs and at the same timepay interests for these special bills. For those RCCs which have received the specialbills, their balance sheet will improve. However, since the central bank billsare not cash and can not be traded in the market either, the loan extensioncapacity of the RCCs will be contained, thus partly off-setting the shocks ofcentral bank lending to the monetary policy. The third step will be for theRCCs to raise their capital adequacy ratio to 2 percent after two years when thecentral bank bills become mature (Basle Capital Accord I published in 1988 setthe core capital adequacy ratio at 4 percent and the general capital adequacyratio at 8 percent). Once fulfillment of criteria set on capital adequacyratio, corporate governance and NPL disposal is confirmed, the central bankwill redeem the special bills for the RCCs so as to enable them to expandfinancial services and loan business. Since lending rates of the RCCs havealready been liberalized to float within the range of 0.9-2.0 times of thebenchmark lending rates, the RCCs will be able to make profits in their loanbusiness. Apart from the above-mentioned three steps of incentives, there areother performance criteria to be met by the RCCs in the coming years so that theycould finally comply with the same regulatory ratios in capital adequacy, riskcontrol and NPLs imposed generally on financial institutions. 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 10/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Constrainedby staff quality and business environment, financial institutions in rural China will find it extremelydifficult to bring their corporate governance and management performance up tothe same level as their counterparts in the cities. That said, above reformmeasures could broadly help to push the RCCs towards the right developmentdirection. All in all, we hope extensive positive incentives could beestablished on a continuous basis to encourage the RCCs to grow in the rightdirection. 3. Preventingmoral hazards Despitethe above reform efforts, problems of various kinds in the RCCs are likely toreemerge in the future, taking into account of the low staff quality,relatively high market risk, possible intervention by the local governments andunderdeveloped credit culture in the rural areas. In this round of ruralfinancial reform, the State has absorbed the historical burdens of the RCCs. Ifin the future there are RCCs caught in payment crisis as a result of hittingthe skids or mismanagement and once again go to the State for help, huge risksof moral hazard and adverse selection will be created. Therefore, in the designof institutional arrangement for this round of reform, we need to take theserisks into consideration. Oneeffective instrument we can rely on to prevent a hitting of the skids isstrict supervision. The key is to adopt prompt corrective action (PCA). Inparticular, when capital adequacy ratios of the RCCs display a trend offalling, regulatory authorities should step in to take timely actions torestrain their business expansion and dividend distribution, thus making themfeel like putting a straightjacket. If the capital adequacy ratios continue tofall, the regulatory authorities should initiate a merger and acquisitionprocess and even demand a closure of these RCCs before their net value fallinto the negative territory. Countries across the world differ in theirexperiences in taking the prompt corrective actions, and we need to put inplace a similar arrangement to prevent a resurgence of loss making by the RCCs.In this regard, the US Federal Deposit Insurance Company 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 11/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Improvement Act standsas a good example. Under this Act, depository institutions are required tosatisfy a capital adequacy ratio of 10 percent. If the ratio falls to 8percent, the regulatory authority will first issue a warning and will takefurther restrictive actions like restrictions imposed on introduction of newbusiness and wholesale deposit taking if it continues to fall to 6 percent. Adepository institution will be put on the track of merger and acquisition ifits capital adequacy ratio slides to 4 percent and then will be closed when theratio further dips to 2 percent. That is to shut it down before the depositorslose their savings. Indesigning PCA for the RCCs in China, we need to stress three important considerations. First,the RCCs are widely dispersed in the grass-root rural areas and they need an accommodativeregulatory arrangement. Second, taking the Chinese situation intoconsideration, an effective market exit system must be put in place to forcethose RCCs with their net value falling to approach the zero level to closedown. If these RCCs are left attended and finally go bust, you may find more hiddenproblems dictating a negative net value, thus encroaching the interests of thedepositors. The key factor to be incorporated in the exit system is theprotection and compensation scheme for the small and medium-sized depositors,thus we need to establish a deposit insurance system in a timely manner. In thecourse of closing down problem RCCs, the determination to enforce such aprocess is vital. You are bound to come across strong resistance when planningto close down a RCC for it will in the short term affect the local financialservices and the economy. If there appears any hesitation to press ahead withsuch a move, risks of moral hazards and adverse selection will certainly arise.Third, in the process of closing down bad-performing RCCs, new licenses shouldbe granted to create innovative financial institutions in the rural areas toprovide financial services to the rural economy. In Chinas case, almost every township has aRCC. Closure of a RCC usually means absence of financial services in aparticular township. That said, we should not compromise the criteria set forlicensing new institutions. I should say, 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 12/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform feasibility studies on theincorporation of community banks or new financial institutions in the ruralareas have been underway for a considerable period of time. There was a periodof rectification of financial institutions when new licenses were relativelyrestricted in the rural areas. Now situation has changed and financial reformhas entered a new era in which considerations should be given to replacingproblem institutions with new institutions. Otherwise, risks of moral hazardsand adverse selection will arise, as problem institutions could not be timelyresolved while at the same time new institutions are not allowed to beestablished to enhance financial services. Of course, there is also noguarantee for the sound performance of the newly established institutions whichdepends not only on themselves but also on the effective supervision by theauthorities on a continuous basis. IV. Guiding credit support to the rural economy First,postal savings institutions should be brought to compete with the RCCs on equalfooting in terms of price policies. For example, on August 1, 2003, the Peoples Bank ofChina cut interest rates paid on incremental deposits held by the postalsavings institutions in the central bank, and green lights were given to thepostal savings institutions to use these deposits at their own discretion.Besides, efforts will be made to dispose of the stock deposits of the postalsavings institutions in the central bank within five years. In particular,interest rates of such deposits will be brought down in five years from thecurrent level to that paid on the required reserves; the postal savingsinstitutions will be authorized to use these deposits at their full discretionin five years time; and scope of fund use will be gradually expanded for thepostal savings institutions. Besides, a fiscal subsidy scheme will beestablished to provide support for general postal services. 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 13/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Second,successful experiences in the implementation of the US Community ReinvestmentAct should be learned to urge depository financial institutions in China to resume a kind ofpay-back obligations by offering services in the local community. According tothis Act, federal banks and depository institutions that participate in the depositinsurance scheme shall have an obligation to help with the credit and servicefacilities required by the local communities where they take deposits. In orderto encourage active enforcement of this Act, two important measures have beenadopted. One is to have the records of the financial institutions in fulfillingcredit requirements of their respective local communities disclosed by theregulatory authorities. Another one is make the approval of application forfederal license, deposit insurance, change of address of the headquarters orbranches or incorporation of new branch offices by the concerning financialinstitutions subject to their performance in observing the Act. Inspired bythis Act, many financial institutions and depository institutions, inparticular those financial institutions that highly value their marketreputation or intend to buy other financial institutions, have shown strongwillingness to carry out this law by reaching mutually cooperative frameworkwith the local communities. For example, many of them have set up new businessoutlets in the local communities to improve credit and other financialservices; and flexibility of loan guarantee has been improved to expand creditaccess to the middle and low-income households. By following this Act, communitybanks have re-invested the locally taken deposits in the markets where theycommand good understanding, thus making contribution to economic prosperity inthe less developed communities and the relief of pressures on financialresources flowing from the developed areas to the underdeveloped regions.Though preparations both on the legislative and the technical fronts need to bemade first to introduce this kind of community-based financial services inChina, we could pioneer in related research and feasibility studies on thisimportant subject. 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 14/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform Third,interest rates should play a more important role. In particular, lending ratesfor financial institutions at and below the county level should be graduallyliberalized. Based on field investigations, the interest rate band for loansextended by the RCCs was widened to 0.9-2.0 times of the benchmark lending ratein 2003. In the coming periods, we need to make efforts to ensure lending ratescharged by the financial institutions in the rural areas could cover their loanrisks in a sustainable way. In the meantime, these institutions must maintainan interest margin sufficient to compensate for business cost and risks. On theother hand, excessive competition on deposits taking through offering highinterest rates should also be prevented. Interest rate remain quite aneffective instrument for guiding both the capital and the business flows. Thisis more evidenced in the current round of reform, as higher interest marginshave constituted great incentives to attract capital flow to the RCCs. Commercialorientation must be resolutely promoted and upheld if a financial institutionhopes to rely on its quality services, not the fiscal support, to guarantee itsfinancial viability. The basic commercial principle for a financialinstitution, a company involved in money business, to bear in mind is the rightto price the financial products offered to the customers. The RCCs is noexception in this regard, and market-based interest rate reform holds the keyto the business success of the rural financial institutions. Dueto time limit, I will not further elaborate on other important subjects whichare also closely relevant to the fin Date of last update SEP. 17, 2004 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 15/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 16/17 26/10/2021, 10:49 Some Reflections on Rural Financial Reform 3688110/3688175/3708182/index.html 17/17

Title: Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank
text: 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank May 12, 2004, Trinidad and Tobago Mr.Chairman, Mr. President, Fellow Governors, ladies and gentlemen: Itake it as a great pleasure to lead the Chinese delegation to attend the 34thAnnual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank.First of all, please kindly allow me to express my heart-felt thanks to thesupport rendered by the government and people of Trinidad and Tobago to theannual meeting and the warm hospitality extended to the Chinese delegation. Myappreciation also goes to the management and staff of the Caribbean DevelopmentBank for the considerate arrangement made for the annual meeting. 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 1/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank Mr.Chairman, Caribbean economy witnessed synchronized recovery with the globaleconomy in 2003 as evidenced by the continuous strengthening of the pillarindustries including tourism and construction, and the overall improvement ofpublic finance experienced by all regional economies. Inflation and exchangerates remained stable across the region, with economic growth of somecountries, such as in Trinidad and Tobago and Belize, reaching over 4 percent,while growth in other countries of the region also outperformed last year. Despitethe remarkable progress, daunting challenges including a decrease ofconcessionary trade arrangement, drop of major agricultural produces, lowcompetitiveness of the manufacturing industry, snail-paced development of theregional capital and money markets and instability of fiscal situation continueto obstruct development of the regional economy. Mr.Chairman, operational performance of the Caribbean Development Bank continuedto improve in 2003, with the number of approved projects and the volume ofloans both largely increased. And fund disbursement rate and amount alsoovergrew the previous year, resulting in a net fund transfer to the borrowingcountries for six years in a row. At the same time, business profits generatedfrom operations of the general fund further expanded and non-performing loansremained at low level. Over the past year, the Caribbean Development Bank hasupheld its commitment to poverty reduction and provided valuable support toprivate sector development, making great contribution to the process ofregional integration. Apart from that, the Caribbean Development Bank has alsoconducted internal reform of its organizational and staff structure. All thesecommendable efforts have greatly benefited the regional economic and socialdevelopment. However, we should not be 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 2/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank overwhelmed by a sense of complacency,and instead should be mindful of the existing deficiencies that need to be improvedin the coming periods. First, redundant procedures of projects review and funddisbursement must be streamlined to improve work efficiency. Second,professional knowledge and skills of the bank need to be sharpened to cope withthe increasingly complex economic environment. Third, response to justifieddemand of the borrowing countries needs to be speeded up. Fourth, breakthroughremains to be achieved in absorbing non-borrowing members from outside theregion. Mr.Chairman, the world economy is currently marching towards full recovery, providinga favorable environment for economic development in the Caribbean region. Facedwith such a good opportunity, the Caribbean Development Bank should take activemeasures to foster closer cooperation with other financial institutions in theregion and the international organizations and more forcefully mobilizefinancing resources from various sectors to support regional economicdevelopment while at the same time making full use of its unique role in such aprocess. As the most important development institution in the region, theCaribbean Development Bank should provide not only financial support but alsopolicy advice based on its local knowledge to economic development of theborrowing countries in the region. In the process of policy making, the CaribbeanDevelopment Bank should strengthen bilateral cooperation, communication andcoordination with other regional institutions to reach policy consensus andharmonization. Basedon analysis of local situation, we can see future economic development of theregion depends more on successful resolution of some of the internal problemsrather than on external factors such as strong world economic growth. One ofthe 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 3/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank key problems remaining to be tackled is the strengthening of regionaleconomic integration. Constrained by limited size, poor natural resources, lessdiversified economic structure and heavy external reliance, not a singlecountry in the region is blessed with strong competitiveness in the worldeconomy. Under such a circumstance, economies in the Caribbean region have noother choice but to strengthen economic integration and complementaryadvantages of each other to ensure a long-term economic success. We certainlydo not expect an encouraging economic prospect for the region if countries in theregion only care about their own development and are reluctant to take thewelfare of the whole region into consideration. In this respect, problemsexisting in the tourism industry such as man-caused degradation of naturalenvironment, insufficient investment and human resources, oversimplified travelproducts and low capability in policy and market analysis must be firstresolved to lay a solid foundation for a sustained and steady development ofthe industry. Second, quality of traditional agricultural produces must beimproved, export of non-traditional products should be further increased andgood working relations must be fostered with other regional trade and economicorganizations. Third, more effective policy measures need to be formulated toencourage private sector participation in the process of economic development.Fourth, taxation system must be reformed to expand the service industry so asto broaden tax base and increase government revenues. Mr.Chairman, remarkable achievements have been made by the Chinese government inrecent years in terms of both economic growth and social progress, and I wouldlike to take this opportunity to share with the distinguished audience some ofthe experiences we have obtained in the process. First, we are always consciousof striking a balance between reform, development and stability. In our view,stability constitutes the prerequisite for reform and development. Therefore,in the process of economic and social development, we have always made theharmony between the strength of reform, the speed 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 4/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank of development and theendurance of the general public a top priority, and targeted a persistentimprovement of the people's living standard as the lock-point for handlingrelationship among the three factors. Such a consensus has contributed to the mutuallyre-enforcement of reform, development and social stability. Second, China'snational situation has mandated the importance of the agricultural industry inthe economy. In our view, the agricultural industry constitutes the basis forthe national economy. Without a sound development of the agricultural sector,there would be no real economic growth and social stability in China. On such acount, the Chinese government has strengthened investment in the agricultural industryover the recent years through promoting technological progress, speeding uprural infrastructure construction and prioritizing rural economic developmentover growth of other industrial sectors. Third, in the process of povertyreduction, the Chinese government has always centered its efforts on capacitybuilding in the poor areas. Under such guidance, poor areas are encouraged toincrease productivity, make use of local resources and cultivate a sense of commodityeconomy. Poverty reduction has been gradually shifted from the "reliefassistance" model to the "development support" model. That is to say, theprinciple of "blood transfusion"has been replaced with one featuring "self blood generation". In particular,infrastructure of the poor regions has been strengthened to help them deal withnatural disasters, and the government has appropriated relevant funds for thedevelopment of farmland, water conservancy projects, highways, electricitynetworks and communication facilities to improve the production and livingconditions in these regions. Besides, earmarked interest- subsidy loans, budgetsupport and preferential policies have been provided to the poor regions tohelp them develop market- oriented industries and projects. With improvedproductivity and incomes, these poor regions will have greaterself- accumulation capability. In addition, relevant trainings have beenarranged to help people in the poor regions learn the advanced and practicaltechnologies so that they could become increasingly self-reliant in the processof development. Apart 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 5/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank from that, efforts in poverty reduction have been complementedby water and soil conservation, environmental protection and ecologicalmanagement to enhance the poor regions' potential to develop in the long run.Lastly, with a comprehensive development approach, emphasis has been placed onthe development of science and technology, education, public health and cultureto promote coordinated economic and social development of the poor regions. Mr.Chairman, as the largest developing country in the world, China fullyunderstands the difficulties and challenges facing the Caribbean region in itseconomic and social development. China has always attached great importance tothe exchange and cooperation with the Caribbean region, and has always beenconcerned with the development and progress in this region. China wishes tobecome a permanent friend and cooperation partner of countries in the Caribbeanregion, and will support the work of the Caribbean Development Band and thedevelopment of the Caribbean region as always. Wewish the Caribbean Development Bank success in carrying out this year's workagenda. Thankyou, Mr. Chairman. 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 6/7 26/10/2021, 10:46 Statement of Mr. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China at the 34th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Caribbean Development Bank Date of last update MAY 12, 2004 3688110/3688175/3708215/index.html 7/7

Title: Statement at the Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee
text: 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee Statement by Mr. ZHOU Xiaochuan Governor of the People's Bank of China Eighth Meeting of the International Monetary and Financial Committee Dubai September 21, 2003 1. World Economic Outlook: Fragilities, Risks, and Policy Response The world economic recovery has further strengthened since our discussion this past spring. However, the many risks facing the global economy have not completely disappeared. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 1/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee Economic momentum in the United States has been fairly strong, and the Japanese economy has shown signs of improvement. Despite the absence of a real economic upturn, market expectations have improved in the euro area. Following the temporary setback caused by the outbreak of the SARS epidemic, rapid growth momentum has returned to Asia's economies since the beginning of the third quarter. Emerging market economies in Latin America have resumed growth after the turbulent debt situation was brought under control, and the economies in transition and countries in the Middle East and Africa have demonstrated varying degrees of improved performance. With the continued stimulus provided by the easing of geopolitical tensions and the accommodative policies adopted by the major economies, the prospect of an upsurge in the latter half of 2003 is becoming brighter for the global economy. However, short- and medium-term factors still affect global prospects. First, there is less room for the advanced economies to implement supportive macroeconomic policies aimed at stimulating demand. Interest rate levels have hit record lows in many countries and fiscal deficits have soared in major industrial countries, severely limiting their capacity for further rate cuts or deficit expansion. Second, the negative impacts of equity bubbles may prove stronger and last longer than initially expected, and the threat of a property bubble burst should not be overlooked. A major decline in housing prices would inevitably deal a new blow to investment and consumption, and drag down global growth. Third, the global economy still relies heavily on U.S. performance, intensifying the risk of world economic fluctuations. Fourth, the possibility of extremely volatile exchange rate movements among the major currencies cannot be ruled out, posing a threat to recovery and restructuring in the affected regions. Fifth, with deflationary momentum in some countries yet to be effectively contained, the risk of its exacerbation and spread still hovers. Sixth, though geopolitical tensions have relaxed, to some extent, for the time being, destabilizing factors still exist which constitute a major threat to the world economy in the period ahead. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 2/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee In view of the above risks, I believe that the major industrial countriesthe United States, the EU, and Japan, in particular should assume major responsibility for the global recovery and restructuring by introducing structural reforms, raising savings rates, boosting domestic demand, reforming labor markets, adjusting trade policies, giving developing countries greater market access, and gradually addressing the problem of fiscal imbalances. 2. Strengthening Surveillance, and Preventing and Resolving Crises In recent years, the Fund has carried out a great deal of research and made exerted efforts to strengthen surveillance and prevent and resolve crises, thereby contributing to the stability of the international financial system and the development of the world economy. We welcome these efforts. In an increasingly globalized world, the economic and financial crises experienced by a number of countries are more and more related to turbulence in international financial markets, exchange rate movements in major countries, and changes in the international trade environment. Therefore Fund surveillance must focus on systemically important economies and financial markets. In particular, surveillance of the economic and financial policies of the major industrial countries should be enhanced while assistance and support should be provided to the developing countries to promote structural changes and eliminate poverty. To a large extent, the effectiveness of Fund surveillance depends on the support and cooperation of member countries. I wish to emphasize that while the Fund is working to intensify its surveillance, it should also continue to enhance the capacity building of its members. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 3/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee In my view, the purpose of formulating and implementing standards and codes is to promote the global economy and preserve the stability of the international financial system. Therefore, there must be sufficient developing country participation in the formulation of standards and codes and consideration should be adequately given to differences in development levels and institution building. The implementation of standards and codes should be conducted on a voluntary and step-by-step basis and focused on actual results. Moreover, I appreciate the Fund's efforts to promote the Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) and financial soundness indicators (FSIs). The financial stability analysis framework and FSIs are helpful in analyzing financial sector vulnerabilities in a given country, and in the world at large. In light of the enormous influence that the major advanced countries have on global financial stability, the Fund should first intensify its surveillance and assessment of these countries' financial sectors and markets, and timely summarize the lessons and experiences to further improve the methodology and indicator system. Then, as part of improving capacity building in the developing world, the Fund can gradually promote the implementation of a methodology and indicator system in a broader context. The Fund's search in recent years for a sovereign debt restructuring mechanism has been positive and meaningful. I hope that with the broad participation of the international community, the Fund will continue its pursuit of a mechanism acceptable to all parties. At present, the use of collective action clauses should be decided by a sovereign country in light of its economic situation and market environment. The proposed code of conduct should be practical, and should serve as a useful reference for members. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 4/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee 3. Development of Low-Income Countries: Debt Relief Initiatives, the Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility (PRGF), and the Doha Round The sluggish global economy in the past two years has caused greater difficulties for low-income countries in terms of exports, capital inflows, poverty reduction and economic restructuring. I would like to call on the international community to pay more attention to development in these countries, support the Fund in enhancing cooperation with other international organizations, expand the scale of assistance, and make the assistance more effective. I also hope that a growing number of developed countries can implement the Monterrey Consensus with concrete action, and achieve the objective of devoting 0.7 percent of GNP to official development assistance. Trade is an important tool for developing countries, enabling them to use their comparative advantage for the purpose of increasing revenue, promoting social and economic progress, and integrating into the world economy. The WTO Ministerial Meeting in Cancun failed to reach agreement on major issues in the new round of multilateral trade negotiations. This shows that there is still a long way to go before the objectives set by the Doha Ministerial Meeting can be realized. At this critical juncture, it is necessary for the two institutions to support the Doha Round more strongly, facilitate the reduction of distortions and unfairness in the multilateral trade system, promote greater market access, especially access for goods in which developing countries have comparative advantages, and make a substantive contribution to the cause of global development and poverty reduction. The Chinese Government has consistently supported the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries' Debt Initiative (HIPC Initiative) and the PRGF. Though our per capita income remains fairly low, we have done our best to provide debt relief to the HIPC countries. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 5/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee It is gratifying to note that, under the HIPC Initiative, the debt burdens of a number of countries have been reduced significantly, thereby providing a basis for sustainable growth in the future. Nevertheless, the economic base of these countries remains relatively weak, requiring the support and assistance of the international community. Moreover, a number of countries are not able to begin the HIPC debt relief procedure for various reasons. We wish to express our concern and hope that they will soon achieve economic stability, be able to implement a poverty reduction strategy effectively with the help of the international community, and qualify for HIPC debt relief at an early date. Drafting a country-owned Poverty Reduction Strategy Paper (PRSP) with the help of the international community is essential for poverty-stricken countries to implement a long-term sustainable development strategy and eliminate poverty on the basis of broad consensus. We are pleased to see increased ownership of relevant countries in drafting a PRSP and that progress has been made in producing better quality papers. We hope that the international community will take full account of the actual conditions of poor countries with regard to the inadequacy of their legal frameworks, institution building and human resource development, refrain from setting unrealistic or difficult objectives, and make a greater contribution to debt relief in these countries. 4. Quota and Governance Structure Deepening economic globalization has not eliminated the root cause of global monetary and financial turbulence, but has instead added to the possibility of its exacerbation under certain conditions. Therefore, I think that the Fund needs to carefully assess the adequacy of its resources and formulate a contingency plan to ensure an effective fulfillment of its central mandate 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 6/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee in safeguarding the stability of the international monetary system. We support the establishment of a Committee of the Whole for the 13th General Review of Quotas, when necessary. At the same time, the Fund should further explore ways to revise quota formulas and to address the out-lineness, thus fairly reflecting the rapid economic growth of the developing countries over the years. We welcome Executive Board discussion on the developing countries' voice and representation in the two institutions. The representation of African countries in the Fund should be enhanced. We have noted that rational quota formulas are interrelated with greater voice and representation. In the absence of quota formula reform, there would be little improvement in developing countries' voice and representation. Therefore, we welcome the staff's package solution for reforming quota formulas, addressing out-of-lineness, and increasing basic votes. 5. Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) The Chinese government attaches great importance to the work on AML/CFT, and continues to support and actively participate in the cooperative efforts of the international community in this area. We highly value the role of international and regional AML/CFT bodies, including the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), and appeal for increased representation of developing countries in the FATF to enhance the appropriateness and authority of its recommendations. We are paying close attention to FATF implementation of ROSC procedures, because this has a major impact on the success of the pilot program. We hope that the Fund can review the experience gained from this program in a timely manner in order to target future assessments more clearly. We support the provision of the follow-up technical assistance by the Fund in the area of AML/CFT. Given its limited technical assistance resources, however, the Fund should continue to focus on its core and 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 7/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee traditional areas. In addition, when participating in AML/CFT work, the Fund should respect the sovereignty and specific conditions of individual countries and allow them to exercise their own initiative. 6. Independent Evaluation Office (IEO) We would like to express our satisfaction with the work of the IEO. Projects completed in 2003 and those scheduled for 2004 and 2005 are closely related to the role of the Fund and the focus of its current work. Suggestions for enhancing the Fund's role and improving the effectiveness of its policies contained in the three reports drafted by the IEO provide good guidance for the Fund to further strengthen its performance and realize its ultimate mandate. We hope that the Fund will value these suggestions and take steps to translate them into action. We hope that in its future work, it will be possible for the IEO to listen to comments and suggestions from all sides, provide more objective and systematic evaluations of work that relates to the Fund's purposes, and offer constructive and feasible suggestions. 7. China's Economy Up to now, the Chinese economy has performed much better than anticipated in 2003. The outbreak of the SARS epidemic earlier this year had a much smaller impact on the economy than previously estimated. GDP grew by 8.2 percent in the first half of the yeara relatively high rate compared with the same periods in recent years. The consumer price index rose 0.6 percent over the same period last year. Growth for the whole year is projected to be above 8 percent, and the consumer price index is expected to rise 1 percent. The economic structure has further improved. Steady progress has been made in the 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 8/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee employment and re-employment programs. There has been a further strengthening of the social safety net, and various reforms have progressed in an orderly manner. In sum, there has been continued improvement in the institutional environment for economic development. Despite the severe impact of SARS, China's economy has maintained rapid growth, owing to the following factors. First, China has maintained a stable domestic political and economic environment. Second, China has resolutely pursued policies that boost domestic demand. Over the past five years, China has persistently implemented a proactive fiscal policy and sound monetary policy, laying a solid foundation for economic growth. Third, even deeper reforms have stimulated economic growth. The joint development of different economic sectors under different types of ownership has continued to strengthen, investment growth has become more market-oriented, and enterprises have increased their capacity for selfdevelopment. Fourth, pursuit of the opening-up policy has entered a new phase, leaving greater room for economic growth. The immense market and favorable investment climate have made China increasingly attractive to foreign investors. While it had an adverse impact on China's economy, the SARS outbreak also created new sources of growth. In particular, the medical, automobile, and health care sectors enjoyed strong growth, which partly offset the losses of other economic sectors. Although China has achieved rapid economic growth, a number of problems remain that deserve attentionan increase in unemployment pressures, the slow growth of rural income, the reappearance of duplicate investments in some regions, the launch of new projects by some industries with obvious excess capacity, an unduly large number of luxury houses with rising vacancy ratesexacerbating economic structural imbalances. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 9/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee We will make continued efforts to expand domestic demand, readjust the economic structure, deepen reforms, promote further opening up, increase job opportunities, and improve people's living standards. We will adopt an approach of comprehensive planning and consideration of all factors to achieve harmonized development. We will strive to achieve sustained, rapid, and steady economic growth by maintaining consistent, stable macroeconomic policies and by the continued pursuit of proactive fiscal policy and sound monetary policy. Development remains the central theme over the medium term. Improving the standard of living for the people is our ultimate goal. We will actively undertake structural adjustment and reform measures, further open up to the outside world, and make progress in science and technology. Guided by the principle of harmonious economic and social development, we will effectively implement the strategies of "Developing the West," "Relying on Science and Education to Invigorate the Nation," urbanization, and sustainable development. We will accelerate the transformation of the old industrial bases and ensure achievement of the targets set in the Tenth Five-Year Plan. We have noticed the international community's recent interest in the exchange rate of China's currency, the renminbi (RMB). The Chinese government has always adopted an attitude of the utmost prudence and responsibility on this issue. During the Asian financial crisis, a stable RMB not only fostered economic and financial stability in China, but also helped contain the further spread of the crisis, thus contributing substantially to economic and financial stability in Asia and around the world. At present, with its economy still facing various challenges, China needs to maintain the stability of its various policies. If China can maintain healthy, rapid economic growth, this will create huge market demand and stimulate imports. During the period from 1998-2002, China's average annual imports growth was 3.5 percentage points higher than the growth of exports. In 2002, China's imports from the countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Japan, Russia, and Australia grew 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 10/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee by 34 percent, 25 percent, 6 percent and 8 percent, respectively, over the previous year. In the first half of this year, China's imports from the United States, Japan, Korea, the EU, and ASEAN countries increased by 36.1 percent, 46.1 percent, 53.7 percent, 39.3 percent and 55.5 percent, respectively, over the same period last year. We will continue to push ahead with market-based institutional reforms, and let the market play an essential role in resource allocation. While maintaining a basically stable RMB, we will continue to examine and improve the mechanism for determining the RMB exchange rate. We believe that exchange rate reforms and other institutional reforms are integral parts of the overall reform endeavor, and thus it is important to identify priorities and proper sequencing to carry out these reforms. At the same time, we will relax control over the capital account in a prudent manner, and seek to achieve balance of payments equilibrium. The economy of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) weathered the severe impact of SARS in the first half of this year. On the sixth anniversary of the resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong SAR, China's central government signed the Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) with the Hong Kong SAR government. Recently, Guangdong, Beijing, and Shanghai have begun to liberalize "individual travel" to Hong Kong SAR, which will significantly boost Hong Kong's tourism industry. With confidence strengthening, Hong Kong SAR's economy has shown some positive signs. The Hong Kong SAR government has revised upward its growth projection for the whole year. In the first quarter of this year, the GDP of Macao SAR grew by 16.5 percent. The tourism and entertainment sectors performed well, and consumption increased significantly, contributing to the entire economic upturn. We will further strengthen economic and financial cooperation between the Mainland and Hong Kong and Macao SARs through the CEPA. 3688110/3688175/3708236/index.html 11/13 26/10/2021, 10:49 Statement By Mr. Zhou Xiaochuan Governor Of The People's Bank Of China Eighth Meeting Of The International Monetary And Financial Committee We are confident that the strengthening global recovery, the sustained strong growth expected in the Mainland and, particularly, the full support from the central government, will contribute to a brighter outlook for the economies of Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR.
