Title: Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China
Subtitle: Delivered by Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the HKMA's sixth distinguished lecture
text: 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China Delivered by Governor Zhou Xiaochuan, People's Bank ofChina at the HKMA's Sixth Distinguished Lecture 18 September, 2003 Ladiesand gentlemen, good evening. It ismy great honour to have this opportunity to give a lecture here in HongKong. I appreciate very muchJoseph's kind introduction about me and his words on the relationship betweenthe People's Bank of China and the HKMA. I am very pleased that theHKMA has organised this activity and that Joseph has contributed for so manyyears to the Hong Kong monetary system. I am also very glad that Gerry can discuss my lecture today. As very good friends, we have for quitea long time had discussions on the financial sectors and economic policies. 2. I haveconsidered what topic would be appropriate for today's occasion. I have some advantages because China isalways having new changes in economic reform and economic transition, so peoplemay have an expectation of hearing about the new changes that have recentlyhappened! But I also realise Ihave a disadvantage as the Chinese economy is 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 1/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China transiting into a market economy,and Hong Kong is a very typical example of the free market economy. So I should say that my colleagues andI should learn from the experience of Hong Kong, rather than I should talkabout the economic changes. 3. I should alsomention that the English language is a very foreign language for me. But I will try my best to do my job. 4. Finally Ichose reform gradualism and evolution of the exchange rate regime in MainlandChina as the topic of today's occasion. But from now on I will not repeat "Mainland". I will just say China for simplicity. 5. First, I willtalk about the concept of reform gradualism. There are official concepts andalso academic concepts, and the concept on the opposite side. That is what Icall the contrast concept. Talkingabout reform gradualism, the purpose is to talk about the evolution of the exchangerate regime. I think in China the exchange rate regime is undergoing a reformprocess, and it is a typical case of reform gradualism. 6. First of all,let us look at the official concept, so I put the Chinese word and the Englishword, as the official language to mention the concept, to emphasise the balancebetween reform, development and stability. Mr Deng Xiaoping emphasised that development is afundamental principle, so it is also the highest priority in economicpolicy-making. 7. The relateddescription of this concept is to solve the problems cropping up on our wayforward through development. So ifwe turn it into an economic concept we may see that gradualism is related topragmatism, which is 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 2/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China different from idealism. Because there is no theory oneconomic transition, transition is very often a matter of trial and error. Reform requires continuous accumulationof momentum to generate energy to move forward in development. I think it is related to the Paretoimprovement, a concept to which I will come back later on. 8. Gradualismemphasises the time characteristics of infrastructure building, including law,regulations, the banking system, accounting systems, the building ofprofessions and the institutions. This requires quite a long period of time. There is no possibility of changing these overnight. Related to the concept is the pathdependency. In 1993 the NobelLaureate, Douglas North, received the Nobel Prize for his theory on pathdependency, so we have to emphasise that if you go through reform it mustdepend on the historical path. 9. Next, I wouldlike to compare this with the opposite concept, which many people know veryclearly. One is the shocktherapy. Later on some peoplecommented that there was only shock, but no therapy. The big bang was used for the financial reform in the UK,but actually what happened in the former Soviet Union and the Eastern Europeancountries was also a kind of big bang. 10. Because thereis no theoretical or empirical experience on the process of economictransition, some people have tried all sorts of methods at the beginning of thereform, and this has become a theoretical belief. 11. The last wordI use is a Russian one. That is "troika", which means a three-horse cart. Inthe late 1980s and beginning of the 1990s, the troika meant to do three thingsall together: One was marketisation; the second was mass privatisation; and the third was democratization. 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 3/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China 12. Let us reviewthe results of the transition in the former Soviet Union and the EasternEuropean countries. I should mention that from the beginning of economictransition, GDP dropped down by 10 to 20 per cent, and production declined by50 per cent. So actually the shocktherapy was not so encouraging. 13. This chart[see slide 7] illustrates that the output of the economy and the growth ratewas negative: during the beginning of shock therapy, these three linesrepresent the Central European countries, southern European countries and theBaltic countries, and the blue one is the former Soviet Union, or theCommonwealth of Independent States, and the line in between is the average forCentral Europe and CIS. 14. We can alsosee the GDP growth rates [slide 8]. At the top is the Chinese growth rate, and below that is Vietnam, andfollowed by Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Hungary and Poland. In the beginning of 1990, a lot ofpeople suggested going for shock therapy, but actually the performance was notso encouraging, and the competitiveness and time was lost for economic reformtransition. 15. Let us explainthe different concepts by using the concept in economics which is known as thePareto optimality. In thebeginning of the last century, Walras and Pareto were very famous economists.They developed the school of general equilibrium. General equilibrium theory discussed resource allocation,and later on Pareto defined the concept on how resource allocation could reachoptimality. According to his definition, the free market economy can reach thisoptimality. He named this thePareto Optimality. It also meansthe highest efficiency of resource allocation. 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 4/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China 16. But in thecentrally planned economies, such as Russia, China and many other EasternEuropean countries, they tried very hard to use the computer to calculate thisoptimality, and used this optimality to put the resource allocation into stateplanning. Then they decomposed the plan into micro economy and gave thecommands for implementation. 17. The centrallyplanned economies experienced a very obvious mistake  that is there was notenough information for them to compute this optimality. And even if you could computethis optimality, you would still lack the incentive to implement it. You therefore have to do it bycommands. Later on, the centrallyplanned economies realised the problem, and they wanted to introduce a newsystem and reach the best situation of resource allocation. Finding optimality was quite likepeople climbing a mountain. If youcan see the peak of the mountain, and if you know where you are located, thenyou can draw a direct line to the peak. However, the direct line is not that easy to climb, so there is anotherconcept called Pareto Improvement. You do not need to see very clearly what is the best way to go to thepeak, but you try to use each of your steps to make an improvement. That meanseach step anyway is going up. Itmight be a spiral up or it might be a zigzag. It does not matter too much which way you go, but you try tomake sure that each step is going up, that with each step you take the economyis benefited, and that meanwhile you also gain momentum to take the next step. 18. I think thisis a relevant explanation of China's reform gradualism. But Pareto Optimalityand Pareto Improvement have some hypotheses. One of the hypotheses is the convex hypothesis. This meansthat when you move, you know that the way to go up is convex. It is notconcave. So if you have anon-convex hypothesis, all the measures may not work. For example, you know that a product price is higher thanthe cost, so you would like to put more resources -- human resources or capital-- into the production. Then bygoing in this direction you are able to earn more money. But the concavehypothesis implies that you may get a negative result in a concave situation. I think this is also relevant to thetransition economies: with all theefforts in shock therapy they made to improve the economy towards theoptimality, what they actually got was a fall of GDP and foreign trade. 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 5/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China 19. I have also tomention the recognition issue. Sometimes when you climb up the mountain,actually you do not see the peak of the mountain because it is verycloudy. As you do not know exactlywhere the peak is, very often you feel lost and you do not know where you arelocated. 20. I would liketo provide some case studies, the first of which is the collapse of CMEA. CMEA is a word people have alreadyforgotten. It is the Conference ofMutual Economic Assistance which started after World War II. I think itsparallel is the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (that is the GATT), theformer organisation of WTO. 21. CMEA was thesystem between former socialist countries, the Soviet Union and the EasternEuropean countries. Fortunately, China was not officially in the CMEA. After the shock therapy there was a bigproblem when the transition economies preferred to transit into a free marketsystem. However, their product standards were not high enough. So if they developed trade with Westerncountries, they had to change their product standards, and they found that theyhad to reduce or to shut down on-going production. Then workers lost theirincomes, and their purchasing power was reduced. They had a desire to import more from Western countries butthey did not have the foreign exchange to pay. They did not like the trade pattern between CMEA countries,that is, the barter trade, or counter-trade system. They had the Swiss Francfor trade settlement, although this was only for booking, not for realpayment. 22. As we havefound out, due to the sudden changes and the rapid shift to the new system, theoutputs of these countries were actually down about 30 to 50 per cent. It wasbecause of the changes in trade. The CMEA countries emphasised very much thedivision of labour. So suddenly they could not trade. There was also the bordertrade between China and Russia. At that time, the Chinese side supposed that wecould carry on having barter trade and counter trade. The Chinese said they 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 6/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China didnot lack foreign exchange while Russia said they did not have enough hardcurrency. Because of the mentality of shock therapy, however, they refused todo barter trade, and I think this was not very encouraging. We can see from this chart that thereal output declined very substantially, by around 30 to 50 per cent [slide11]. 23. These tables[slide 12] showed the imports and exports of Russia, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Poland and Romania.. You may note that trade of thesecountries was substantially reduced in 1991. 24. Wecan proceed to study the second case, that is, the financial discipline.Centrally planned economies had a problem, the so-called soft budgetconstraint. The famous Hungarian economist, Janos Kornai, wrote a book on softbudget constraint. Later on he went to Harvard University and wrote anotherfamous book, "From Marx to Market". 25. According tohis theory, if a centrally planned economy undertakes economic reform and massprivatisation, it can resolve the problem of public ownership, and can thenshift from soft budget constraint into hard constraint. Some of these countries really had avery radical shock therapy in this area, so they issued new laws, regulations,rules, and launched a restructuring of their banking systems. They set upcapital markets and foreign exchange markets. They changed their exchangerates, and they had a voucher-type privatisation. However, as I understand, because this involved theinfrastructure of the economic system, it has taken much longer to reallyimplement the essential changes. 26. So if we lookat Russia in 1990s, there were no hard constraints. We can see enterprises didnot pay wages to the workers. Workers did not pay taxes to the state. The statedid not pay pension and the other welfare, including education, to the people,so actually what happened was a much worse situation in the financialdiscipline, or say, in the budget constraint. 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 7/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China 27. In Hungary thesituation was better but it was still a very gradual, slow-paced change. JanosKornai later on mentioned that he made a mistake and he found out it actuallyhad to be a gradual way to set up the financial discipline as part of theinfrastructure of financial transition. 28. Later on, in1998, there was financial crisis in Russia. I think maybe the Russian crisis was a lucky thing for HongKong because the focus at that time shifted to Russia, and later on to Braziltogether with LTCM problems. We see the stock market fell substantially inRussia. The exchange rate was very much depreciated. There was a serious problem in servicing external debt. Theinteresting thing is the banking system in Russia at that time. As the financial discipline was so bad,a very large percentage of banks absorbed deposits from the people withoutlending the money to enterprises. Without the financial discipline, the depositmoney was used to buy government bonds. Later on, in 1998, the governmentannounced that it would not be able to pay back the government bonds. It could only pay 40 per cent of them.This became a very big disaster for the Russian banking system, and also, Ithink, a disaster for the Russian people. 29. The third caseI would like to consider is what China was doing. I would like to think back to the time around 1979. That wasthe starting year of economic reform. Because it was long ago, many peoplemight think that China started its economic reform from the agriculturalsector, and only in the agricultural sector, and to say that agriculturalreform was a kind of privatisation. But I would like to say that there was also a kind of troika, of threehorses. One was agriculturalreform, the second one was industrial reform while the third was the open doorpolicy. 30. In the area ofagricultural reform, I would like to mention three aspects. One is related tothe concept of privatisation, which was known as the family responsibilitysystem. The second was the marketisation and the price 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 8/9 26/10/2021, 10:50 Reform gradualism and evolution of exchange rate regime in Mainland China liberalisation ofagri-byproducts. I think it was very important to produce more products to meetdemands at that time. The third one was to diminish or eliminate the plan ofcrop growing areas. Prior to the reform, the Central Planning Commissiondefined how much area should be used to grow various kinds of crop. 31. I think thefirst reform in the industrial area happened in 1978. That was the discussion of the production objective.It was to set the productionobjective to meet demand of consumers in the society rather than to meet theproduction plan. The second was toallow a material incentive. Beforethat there was no incentive at all, as the workers were paid exactly the sameno matter how much they contributed, or if they worked overtime or not. Thethird one was the liberalisation of the consumer goods industry and theirprices. As a result, in fiveyears' time, we already saw improvement in the consumer goods supply in China. 3688110/3688175/3708239/index.html 9/9

Title: Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy
Subtitle: Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the lunching in honour of Mr Horst Kohler, Managing Director of the IMF
text: 26/10/2021, 10:44 Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy Speech of Governor Zhou Xiaochuan at the Lunching in Honor of Mr. Horst Kohler, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) September 1, 2003, Beijing, China 3688110/3688175/3708242/index.html 1/5 26/10/2021, 10:44 Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy Good morning,ladies and gentlemen, It is a greatpleasure to have Mr. Kohler join me today to discuss with you on issues of theworld economy and China's reform and development. This is Mr. Kohler's fourthvisit to China since he took the office of the Managing Director of the IMF.Such a frequent exchange of visits between the Chinese authorities and the IMFtop management highlights a persistent strengthening of bilateral cooperationbetween the two sides. China hasenjoyed a close and cordial working relationship with the IMF ever since itresumed its membership in the IMF in 1980. In early 1980's, temporary economicdifficulties led China to have borrowed on three occasions from the IMF,altogether involving an amount of about USD1.6 billion, and these loans had allbeen paid up by the end of 1991. Over the past 20 years, the IMF has providedvaluable policy advice to the Chinese government on a variety of challenges wehave confronted in the process of establishing a socialist market economy inChina, including through the Article VI consultations, technical assistance andvarious training programs. At the same time, the IMF's positive and objectiveassessment of China's economic development and policies has greatly helped theinternational community to gain a full and correct understanding of China. In2000, China signed a joint-training program with the IMF. With the completionof the construction of the joint-training center in Dalian, we are expecting strengthenedbilateral cooperation in the areas of personnel training. With all this inmind, Mr. Managing Director, please allow me to take this opportunity toexpress our heart-felt gratitude to you, and through you, to all 3688110/3688175/3708242/index.html 2/5 26/10/2021, 10:44 Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy the staff ofthe IMF, including those retired staff who had so generously contributed toChina's economic reform and opening up. As a member ofthe IMF, China is also actively involved in and supporting various activitiesof the IMF, and evenly fulfilling its obligations, including participating inthe concessionary financial programs to support poor countries. Blessed withstrong position of the balance of international payments and sufficient foreignexchange reserves, China has for many years projected itself as a netcontributor of resources to the IMF. More than twodecades of cooperation with the IMF is accompanied with profound achievementsmade by China in the process of economic reform and opening up. During such aperiod, China's overall GDP has quadrupled, with economic structure markedlyimproved, a market economic system preliminarily established, economic openingup entered new phases, the financial industry realized frog-leap development,and macroeconomic management remarkably strengthened. At the same time, Chinahas seen its international status risen to certain extent. In 2001, the rankingof China's quota in the IMF rose from the 11th place to the 8thplace, equivalent of that of Canada. In this regard, I would like once again toexpress my gratitude to Mr. Kohler and his colleagues in the IMF for theirgenerous support. 3688110/3688175/3708242/index.html 3/5 26/10/2021, 10:44 Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy In the yearsto come, China will continue to push forward reform and economic opening up inan active and steady way, and we would continue to welcome and look forward tothe most valuable policy advice and technical assistance from the IMF inadvancing the reform courses. As one of the three most important internationaleconomic organizations in today's world, the IMF with a global membership isplaying an increasingly important role in safeguarding international financialstability, in promoting steady and balanced growth of the world trade, and inencouraging orderly cross-border capital flows. Particularly in recent years,the IMF's broad involvement in a wide range of activities, including the launchingof FSAP, promoting global implementation of various international standards andcodes of good practice, combating money laundering and terrorism- relatedfinancing activities, has helped to build a new framework for global financialstability and balanced growth of the world economy. Ladies andgentlemen, I am confident that with the superb leadership by Mr. Kohler, thehard work of all the Fund staff as well as the joint efforts of all the Fundmembers, we are destined to see strengthened bilateral cooperation andunderstanding between the IMF and its member countries, and the Fund itselfwill surely be able to gradually realize its sublime mandate, which is topromote a balanced and sustainable growth of the world economy. 3688110/3688175/3708242/index.html 4/5 26/10/2021, 10:44 Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation and Mutual Understanding to Promote Common Prosperity of the Chinese and World Economy Date of last update SEP. 03, 2003 3688110/3688175/3708242/index.html 5/5

Title: Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision
text: 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision MR. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China Seminar on Financial Stability and Central Bank Governance Beijing, August 26, 2003 In order tostrengthen financial supervision as well as to enhance the independence of theCentral Bank in formulating and implementing the monetary policy, Chinaestablished the China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC) in April this year asa special watchdog for the banking industry. Such an event is of profoundsignificance for strengthening financial supervision. It, 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 1/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision however, does notmean that the Central Bank is no longer responsible for and involved in financialsupervision in China. To the contrary, the Central Bank, after the birth of theCBRC, still needs to bring into full play its unique role in financialsupervision that goes beyond other financialsupervisory authorities. The reason isthat the target of banking supervision is closely related to that of monetarypolicy. The major target of banking supervision rests in ensuring the safetyand soundness of the banking system and the legal interests of depositors whilethat of the monetary policy resides in maintaining stability of the currencyand in turn promoting economic development. The decision-maker of the monetarypolicy should pay attention to the safety and stability of the banking system.Instability of the commercial banking system constitutes a threat to the safe operationof the payment system, and in turn influences monetary policy transmission,affects the allocation of credit resources and increases the cost of monetarypolicy. Bankingsupervision exerts significant influence on the effectiveness of the monetarypolicy. Risk control measures taken by the banking supervisory authorities willproduce its effects on the monetary policy. The stipulation of a minimumcapital adequacy ratio will prevent banks from expanding their assets, and thusbecomes a curb to the expansionary monetary policy. When the economy is fallinginto recession and the banking industry is likely to see a rise of itsnon-performing assets, the banking supervisory authorities under such acircumstance may call the banks to take prudential measures such as increasingloan loss provisioning and improving asset quality. These measures in turncould invalidate the expansionary 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 2/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision monetary policy adopted to lift the economyout of recession. Preservation of liquidity as a prudential requirement would alsolimit banks' ability to lend. The monetarypolicy would also have its influence on the effectiveness of bankingsupervision. The implementation of a tight monetary policy would weaken banks' solvencywhile that of an over-expansionary monetary policy would inflame bubbles in theeconomy and hence result in great potential risks for banks. The Central Bank'sadjustment of money supply as well as liquidity and capitalization ofsecurities by employing such monetary policy instruments as central banklending, re-discount, required reserve ratio and open market operations andwill produce direct influence on liquidity and profitability of banks. Besides,the People's Bank of China (PBC) also acts as the lender of last resort andhence need to know about the performance of the banks. Therefore,after the PBC has released its functions of licensing the entry of market by banks,asset management companies (AMCs), trust and investment companies (TICs) andother depository institutions and supervising their operations, it needs togreatly strengthen its functions in monetary policy, in monitoring of thefinancial market, in formulation of operational rules for financialinstitutions, in safeguarding the overall financial stability, as well as inprevention and mitigation of systemic risks. It also needs continue to carryout the functions in foreign exchange administration, in currency issuance, inacting as the fiscal agent, in payments and clearing, in legal framework constructionas well as in representing the Chinese government in 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 3/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision international financialcooperation and in collecting and conducting analysis of financial statisticaldata. From now on, the biggest change of the functions of the PBC is likely totake place mainly as follows: I. Strengtheningthe function of formulating and implementing monetary policy, enhancingmonitoring, analysis, and research on economic and financial situation at homeand abroad as well as improving financial management through employment ofvarious monetary policy instruments With the establishment and improvement of the socialistmarket economy, the role of the Central Bank becomes ever more prominent in theoverall economic management. Development of economic globalization has alsoushered in many new problems and challenges for the world economy. They willcertainly have substantial impact on the external environment of the Chineseeconomy. For instance, the world three major economies are currently alltrapped in economic contraction and very low level of price and interest rate,which is producing repercussions on the Chinese economy. On such a count, weneed to closely follow and make comprehensive analysis of such developments soas to ensure a standy-by and proper response to the negative effects theyimpose on the Chinese economy. To meet such a challenge, the PBC needs toexercise its role in maintaining financial stability by bringing into flexibleplay of various monetary policy instruments such as interest rate and exchangerate, reinforce the surveillance and monitoring of the financial markets suchas the money market, the foreign exchange market and the gold market, payattention to and coordinate links between the money market and markets of realestate, securities and insurance as well as related policies and risk controlarrangement, promote standardized operation 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 4/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision and overall balanced development ofthe financial market, improve monetary policy transmission, and vigorously enhancemonetary policy-making process. Strategic research on optimizing allocation of financial resources willalso be strengthened. Particularly under the circumstances that the financialsector continuously widens its opening up after China's accession to the WTO,the PBC needs to, from the vantage point of national interests, conductcomprehensive research on and draw up a development program for the overallfinancial sector, promote a synchronized and coordinated development of thethree industries of banking, securities and insurance, and foster a harmoniousdevelopment of the money market, the capital market and the insurance market.Moreover, development of the financial market demands strengthened constructionof financial legal framework and continuous improvement of the operationalrules for financial institutions. The PBC also needs to promulgate and improvelaws, regulations and rules related to monetary policy and those for maintainingoverall financial stability and payment security. II.Transforming the mode of financial management to deter and defuse systemicfinancial risks In early 2003, we completed the institutional restructuringof the supervisory system. After the separation of the supervisory function,the PBC needs to transform its mode of financial management and the way to maintainstability of the financial system. As the lender of the last resort, theCentral Bank should monitor the capital adequacy ratio and liquidity ofrelevant financial institutions, forestall and mitigate systemic financialrisks as well as monitor and assess the overall and cross-sector risks of thefinancial industry. Policy coordination with other regulators should beenhanced to step up surveillance over 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 5/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision financial holding companies and transactionsof cross-sector financial instruments. Since the central bank is responsiblefor the overall financial stability, it needs to strengthen stabilityassessment of the financial sector, so as to ring the first alarm bell for anypotential risks with a systemic nature. With globalization and continuousintegration of the world economy, China will become more than ever before apart of the process. On such a consideration, studies and analysis of worldeconomic developments and the possible fallouts they might bring on the Chineseeconomy should be adequately conducted in a timely manner. Besides, greatattention should be paid to safeguard sound equilibrium of the balance of paymentsas well as the security and profitability of foreign exchange reserves. Studiesshould also be conducted on gradual and sequenced liberalization of the capitalaccount and free convertibility of the Renminbi. III Strengthening the function of anti-money-laundering In the recentyears, the international community has attached ever more importance toanti-money-laundering and China has actively participated in internationalcooperation in this area. The Central Bank, as the provider of the clearingservices for fund transactions, can detect clues for suspicious fund flow bymonitoring large amount fund movement. From now on, the Central Bank willvigorously strengthen the institutional construction and practical guidance onanti-money laundering in the financial sector and enhance analysis of andsurveillance over suspicious flows of large amount funds. 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 6/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision IV Strengthening administration of credit information system Theconstruction of credit information system constitutes an important element in anda pressing task for the establishment of the socialist market economy in China.The Central Committee of the CPC attaches great importance to such an endeavor.Following the National Financial Work Conference at the beginning of 2002, theState Council instructed the PBC to take the lead in forming "the task forcefor developing enterprise and individual credit information system" The taskforce has so far completed a draft regulation governing administration ofcredit information system and put forward technical standards and the programof constructing a nationwide credit registration and inquiry system. As credit informationcollection and related service are still in its infantry in China and noexperience in this regard has ever been obtained before, the Central Banktherefor should pioneer in the construction and unify management of the credit informationsystem, so as to guide the industry develop in a rapid and healthy manner. From now on,the PBC will mainly perform the following functions as the Central Bank inChina: 1. Continue to implement the soundmonetary policy to preserve the sound momentum of economic and financial development 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 7/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision In the firsthalf of this year, performance of the financial industry was broadly stable.Money supply accelerated, loans by financial institutions grew enormously,liquidity of financial institutions maintained normal, foreign reserves soared,and exchange rate of Renminbi remained stable. At the end of June, broad moneyM2 reached RMB20.5 trillion yuan, representing an increase of 20.8 percent froma year earlier. Narrow money M1 grew by 20.2 percent to RMB7.6 trillion yuan.Total loans in renminbi and foreign currencies by all financial institutionsgrew to RMB15.9 trillion yuan, up 22.9 percent over a year earlier or RMB1.9trillion yuan more than that recorded at the end of 2002. Foreign exchange reservesgrew to US346.5 billion, increasing by 42.7 percent year-on-year or US60.1billion over the end of 2002. Generally speaking, the sound monetary policy wasproved effective in supporting economic growth and preserving overall financialstability at the same time. 2. Strengthen guidance on and speed upreform of the state-owned commercial banks In line withthe principles to be followed in banking reform, i.e., commercialization,stock-holding and modernization, comprehensive reform will be carried out onwholly state-owned commercial banks. The strategy is to build the whollystateowned commercial banks into large internationally competitive modernbanks within a certain period of time. Meanwhile, structure of corporategovernance and mechanism of capital replenishment in joint-stock commercialbanks will be studied and improved and those qualified commercial banks will beencouraged to go public to enhance their competitiveness in the 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 8/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision market. City commercialbanks will be urged to form business alliance in accordance with marketprinciples and to shift their business emphasis to financial services to small-and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. In addition, reform of ruralcredit cooperatives will be accelerated to beef up credit support toagriculture, the rural economy and the farmers. 3. Speedup market-based interest rate reform For the pastfew years, China has proceeded in an active while steady manner themarket-based interest rate reform. Restrictions on inter-bank lending interestrate, issuance interest rate of treasury bonds, inter-bank interest rate forbond repo, and issuance interest rate for policy financial bonds have beengradually removed. Bank lending rates were made more flexible as the floating rangefor interest rates charged to SMEs were twice widened. Commercial banks havebeen allowed to take large-amount deposits at negotiated rates and a pilot programintroduced for market-based interest rate reform by RCCs to accumulateexperience for rural financial reform. Interest rates of loans and large amountdeposits in foreign currencies were liberalized and policies of administrationon the interest rates for foreign currency deposits and loans by both domesticand foreign- funded financial institutions unified. In particular, the Renminbiinterest rate was cut eight times in a row to support economic growth.Meanwhile, management of interest rate in the market was strengthened and OpenMarket Operations were flexibly used to guide the movements of the market interestrate. 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 9/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision The 16thCongress of the CPC and the 10th National People's Congress (NPC)put forward clearly the requirement that market- based interest rate reform bespeeded up. The target for the market-based interest rate reform is toestablish the mechanism of interest rate formation where the interest rate fordeposits and loans by financial institutions is decided by the supply anddemand of financial resources in the market and where the Central Bank caneffectively adjust and guide the movements of the interest rate by flexiblyemploying monetary policy instruments to bring into full play the role of theinterest rate in optimizing allocation of financial resources. The interest ratereform is a gradual process. In the several years to come, we will proceed themarket-based interest rate reform in a steady manner in line with the sequenceof "foreign currency ahead of Renminbi, loans ahead of deposits, large amountand long term ahead of small amount and short term". In particular, interestrate of loans will be liberalized gradually to finally allow commercial banks chargeinterest rates at their own judgement for different tranche of loans while thecentral bank is only responsible for setting the floor for the base rate. In thetransitional period, commercial banks will be required to charge loan interestrates within the approved range in line with conditions of different borrowers,regardless of the size or ownership structure of the borrower. Measures willalso be taken to guide commercial banks to establish and improve interest ratepricing mechanism and to become interest rate risk averse. 4. Strengthenguidance on and deepen the reform of the rural credit cooperatives and improvefinancial services in the rural area 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 10/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision The reform ofRCCs matters not only to the steady and healthy development of the RCCs themselvesbut also to the overall agricultural development, income increase of farmersand the stability in the rural area. In line with the overall plan andrequirements on the reform of the RCCs set by the Central Committee of the CPCand the State Council, the reform of RCCs should aim "to clarify ownership,strengthen disciplinary mechanism, reinforce functions in financial services, seekappropriate government support and hold local governments accountable". In linewith these principles, RCCs will be turned into local community financialinstitutions where farmers, rural businesses and other various economicentities jointly hold the stock, thus becoming a financial institutionspecializing in providing services to farmers, agriculture and the ruraleconomy. Internal control and operational mechanism of the RCCs will be furtherstrengthened to prevent and mitigate financial risks confronting the RCCs.Besides, the RCCs should be encouraged to act as the main financial force to supporteconomic structural adjustment in the rural area, help farmers to increaseincome and promote the harmonious development of urban and rural economy.Government policy support to theRCCs will be enhanced, with the local provincial governments to be heldaccountable for the management of the RCCs and for the prevention andresolution of the confronted financial risks. 5. Strengthenand improve foreign exchange administration 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 11/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision Severalregulations on foreign exchange administration have been promulgated to expandsupply of foreign exchange. A series of policies have been formulated andimplemented to facilitate use of foreign exchange by both enterprises andindividuals, to encourage enterprises to invest abroad and to preserve theequilibrium of balance of payments and stability of the exchange rate. In thedays to come, restrictions on capital account transactions will be graduallyremoved so as to pave the way for full convertibility of the Renminbi. 6. Speedup the construction of the payment system and modernization of financialservice The largeamount real-time payment system has been completed on time in 13 provincialcapitals and put into operation. The acceptance ofbankcards across banks and regions nationwide has been markedly improved.A series of rules and regulations have been promulgated and put into effect onanti-money-laundering in the financial institutions. Training and publicitycampaign has also been intensified to increase public understanding ofanti-money-laundering efforts. Allin all, the construction of the payment system, improvement of bankcardacceptance and efforts combating money-laundering activities will constitutethe main tasks for the PBC in strengthening its financial services in the yearsto come. 7. Strengthenmanagement of currency issue and state treasury functions 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 12/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision Currencydistribution fund will be properly appropriated to ensure a reasonable supplyof cash in the economy. Enforcement of rules on cash management will be furtherstrengthened to regulate cash transactions. Meanwhile, great efforts will bemade to continuously crack down unlawful activities and financial crimes suchas the production and trafficking of counterfeit currencies so as to protectthe integrity of the Renminbi. Modified accounting system for state treasurywill be applied to improve statistical analysis of revenues and expendituresincurred in state treasury. Moreover, pilot reform to introduce a unified statetreasury account will be expanded and advanced to ensure a timely completion ofsuch a project, and surveillance of the state treasury accounts will be furtherenhanced to safeguard the security and integrity of the state treasury funds. Date of last update AUG. 26, 2003 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 13/14 26/10/2021, 10:50 Role of the Central Bank in Financial Supervision 3688110/3688175/3708245/index.html 14/14

Title: Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China
text: 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China --Written statement of Mr. ZHOU Xiaochuan, Governor of the People's Bank of China 12th International Banking Congress St. Petersburg, Russia June 5, 2003 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 1/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China It is a great pleasure for me to take this opportunity to elaborate on the role of monetary policy and financial system reform on promoting a sustained high economic growth in China. I. Three major functions of monetary policy in China's economic growth process In reviewing China's experience of reform and opening up to the rest of the world, and its well-recognized achievement of rapid economic growth since 1978, it is not too difficult to draw the conclusion that monetary policy has played a critical role in safeguarding macroeconomic stability, promoting economic reform and development, supporting reforms in specific areas during particular periods of time to achieve Pareto-improvement (PI), and supporting economic structural adjustment. (1) Providing a stable financial environment. In the early stage of reform and opening up to the rest of the world, the People's Bank of China reformed the exchange rate system in 1980, supporting the reform and opening up to take its first step. Later in 1985 and 1988, in response to the economic over-heating and high inflation caused by the exorbitant investment and consumption, the People's Bank of China timely tightened money supply through its monetary and credit policy operations and restored the price stability. Monetary policy at that period was aimed at the aggregate control and structural adjustment through a mixture of direct control and indirect adjustment with measures including reserve requirement, interest rates for deposits and loans, and the introduction of special deposits, etc. During 1991-92, the People's Bank of China increased money supply to counter the slow down of economic growth. The economy was quick back on track. As the transition from the central planning economy to the market economy speeds up, the People's Bank of China has been resilient in adjusting its monetary and credit policy in line with the actual economic performance, aiming at price stability, maintaining macroeconomic stability, and supporting development and reform and opening up to the rest of the world. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 2/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China (2) Supporting reforms in specific areas to achieve PI. In 1994, China successfully reformed its foreign exchange system by adopting a system of buying and selling foreign exchange through designated banks and setting up a nationwide unified interbank foreign exchange market. A unified, managed floating exchange rate regime based on market demand and supply was set up, the basis for achieving full convertibility of RMB was then established. On December 1, 1996, China officially informed the International Monetary Fund of its acceptance of the obligations under the Article 8 (2), (3) and (4), removing all exchange controls over current account transactions, and realized the current account convertibility. This marked another major breakthrough in China's foreign exchange system reform in response to the external sector development, the needs of attracting FDI and facilitating the integration of the Chinese economy with the world economy. During 1993-96, the fast growth in localities, overheating in setting up development zones, excess investment in real estate and speculation in equity market resulted in early signs of economic bubble. Against this background, the People's Bank of China, followed the strategic decision of the State Council, adopted an appropriate tight monetary policy and employed administrative and legal means to restore the financial order, control base money and credit aggregates. As a result, the monetary and credit aggregates were effectively brought under control and RMB value was preserved. In three years of rectification, adjustment and absorption, a soft landing of the economy was successfully achieved. When the Asian financial crisis burst out in 1997, the currencies of China's neighboring countries depreciated by large margins, financial markets in the region as well as elsewhere were in turbulence. At that juncture, China decided to maintain RMB value stable in line with its own reality and the overall interest of the international community. The stability of RMB acted as an anchor in stabilizing regional financial markets and gained applause from the world. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 3/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China Because of the increase in supply capacity in China, the excess supply of agriculture products and the decline in prices of agriculture goods has curbed the increase of farmers' income. As a result, a slight deflationary phenomenon appeared in China during 2001-02. The CPI was 0.4% in 2002. With the adoption of the pro-active fiscal policy and sound monetary policy together with policies of developing the western regions of China, China was able not only to get rid of the impact of Asian financial crisis by increasing domestic demand in a relatively short period of time but also decrease deflationary pressure. In the second half of 2002, the price level in China increased month by month. The CPI in early 2003 became positive. During the 20 years of reform and opening up to the rest of the world, the People's Bank of China also supported the development of capital market in China, the re-capitalization of the state owned commercial banks, and encouraged them to move forward to be share-holding commercial banks and to be publicly listed. The individual housing ownership reform also enjoyed the support of the housing credit policy of the People's Bank of China. These monetary policy measures have promoted the economic development and achieved significant PI result. At the same time, the financial system reform and monetary policy operations have also made a giant leap forward through the process of reforms and opening up to the rest of world. (3) Supporting structural adjustment. Given the unique features of China's economic transition, the People's Bank of China also rendered its firm support to the economic structural adjustment through its monetary and credit policy. Since 2000, the monetary and credit policy has, in cooperation with fiscal policy, been very supportive to the state strategy of developing the western regions of China; alleviating the difficulties of the state owned enterprise and helping restructuring of military enterprises; and reforming the grain distribution system in the later part of 1990s through the measures of re-lending, 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 4/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China debt/equity swap, bad debts written off, etc. The timely adjusting the real estate credit policy supported the housing system reform and curtailed real estate over-heating. These policy measures have fulfilled their targets while the effectiveness of some policy measures may need to be reviewed further. II. Key financial system reforms in the coming years China's financial system has registered a historical leap forward. Financial market system is being full fledged day by day, and the efficiency of resource mobilization and utilization has been steadily improving. There are, however, many difficulties and challenges ahead for the further deepening of the financial sector reform and development. For instance, the NPL ratio is still relatively high, financial institutions particularly the state owned commercial banks are yet to be reformed to meet the challenges brought by the economic development. As the economic development and globalization further advances, and in accordance with China's WTO commitments, China has to confront new challenges by speeding up and further deepening financial reforms. The key points of reforms in the coming years include: --systematic reform of the banking sector, including dealing with NPLs, re-capitalizing banks, improving corporate governance and encouraging banks to become share holding banks and be publicly listed. --taking effective measures to promote capital market development, including increase in direct financing to improve savings pattern. --formulating a package of policy measures to improve pension and medical care system. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 5/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China --pursuing market-based interest rate reform, RMB convertibility and financial service reform in line with trade liberalization, maintaining the stability of RMB exchange rate. The experience of reform and opening up to the rest of the world in China have proved that reforms must be carried out in line with PI, step by step, well coordinated and backed by strong determination. Reforms are a long-term process, each step must be taken in line with the PI in order to increase resource allocation efficiency and improve microeconomic environment. The success of each step of reform could then become the driving force for the next step of reform, including generating political support and economic interest and enhancing public confidence. The endurance and confidence of the public to the reform would otherwise be compromised if the reforms were carried out differently. During the periods of systematic transition and economic structural adjustment, in order to achieve PI, monetary policy has to coordinate with other governmental policies while maintaining relative independence. Moreover, as the reform deepened and economic institution improved, monetary policy should gradually fade out from the reforms in specific fields as well as structural adjustment and focus on macroeconomic regulation. III. Recent economic and financial performance in China China's reform and opening up to the rest of the world has achieved great success well recognized by the world. As a result, China's overall strength has significantly increased. In the past decades, China's annual average GDP growth rate has been kept at above 9%, surpassing the world averaged growth rate by large margins. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 6/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 7/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China Under the circumstances of the 1997 Asian financial crisis and the recent uncertainty of the world economic prospect, China has been able to smooth out fluctuations in economic performance and maintained a good momentum of sound economic development by stimulating domestic demand through the pro-active fiscal policy and sound monetary policy. Since the beginning of 2003, the good momentum of sound economic development has continued as the GDP growth in the first quarter increased by 9.9%. A slight deflationary phenomenon emerged in China during 2001-02. The CPI was 0.4% in 2002. Starting from the beginning of 2003, CPI registered its first positive since November 2001. In the first five months, CPI increased by 0.6% over the same period of last year, representing a turning point after 13 months of decline in price levels. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 8/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 9/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China With regard to the financial sector performance, the first five months of 2003 has shown the following features: money supply (M2) continued its fast growth; total deposits and lending by financial institutions increased by large margins and RMB remained stable. By the end of May, M2 increased by 20.2% over the same period of last year, higher by 6.2 percentage points; M1 increased by 18.8% over the same period of last year, higher by 4.2 percentage points; M0 increased by 12.3%. The growth of M2 has been higher than the sum of GDP growth rate and CPI by 9.8 percentage points, needless to say the increase has been fast. Total outstanding lending by financial institutions (including foreign financial institutions) amounted to RMB15.33 trillion yuan, up by 21.4% over the same period of last year. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 10/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 11/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 12/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China In the first five-month, China's total import and export amounted to US 309 billion, up by 39.6%, of which the exports totaled US 156 billion, up by 34.3%, imports totaled US 153 billion, up by 45.5%. Total trade surplus was US 2.38 billion. The total amount of FDI contract was US 38 billion, increased by 42.22%, actual utilization of foreign funds amounted to US 23 billion, increasing by 48%. By the end of May 2003, the total state foreign exchange reserves amounted to US 340 billion, and the RMB exchange rate stood at RMB 8.277 per US dollar. RMB exchange rate remained stable. In sum, China has maintained its good economic momentum of high growth and low inflation since 1998. At the same time, China also faces pressures of employment, deflation and potential financial risks. We will continue the current sound monetary policy to maintain price stability while supporting economic growth, job creation and mitigating financial risks. Thank you all. 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 13/14 26/10/2021, 10:42 Monetary Policy, Financial System Reform and Sustainable Economic Growth in China Date of last update JUN. 05, 2003 3688110/3688175/3708248/index.html 14/14

Title: Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World
text: 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World MR. Li Ruogu Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China Montreal, Canada, May 8, 2003 It is a greatpleasure to be invited to present my views at the forum about China's economicdevelopment and investment environment. Thanks to more than two decades ofreform and opening up,remarkable progress has been made in developing China's economy. Along with thesustained, rapid and healthy economic growth, market infrastructure andinvestment environment also steadily improved, which has boosted businessconfidence and inflow of foreign capital. In recent years, China has become thelargest emerging market destination of foreign direct investment. The reformand opening-up policy pursued by the Chinese government has helped China securesubstantial financial resources in a dramatically changing global environment,thus making great contribution to the take-off of the Chinese economy. 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 1/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World I. Evolution of China's reform and opening-up to the outsideworld The Third Plenary Session of the Eleventh CPC NationalCongress held in 1978 launched China's reform and opening-up to the outsideworld. The strategy we followed in the past 24 years in carrying out the reformwas specifically tailored to China's own characteristics. That is to say,reform in the rural areas and on the microeconomic fronts preceded that in thecities and the macroeconomic fields. Reform is usually first conduced on apilot basis and then gradually expanded based on the attained experience. Apartfrom that, we have also adopted a reform strategy called "walking on two legs",which means a new arrangement must be set up before the old one is abolished.Although our economic system reform is market-oriented, we have not blindlyforsaken the power of the government in regulating and managing themacroeconomic development. Broadly speaking, reform and opening-up of theChinese economy can be divided into three stages. Between 1978 and 1984: reform of the micro-economicoperational mechanism. In this stage, the household responsibility system wasintroduced in the rural areas to promote agricultural production, while in thecities incentives of various forms such as increasing the decision-making andprofit-sharing of the enterprises in industrial production were adopted toencourage both the workers and managers to improve performance. 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 2/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World Between 1984 and 1991: In this second stage of economicreform, focus was fixed on improving the macroeconomic management system tostrengthen the vitality of the enterprises. Based on such a consideration, aseries of reform was conducted to improve the taxation, foreign trade,financial and the price system with a view to upgrade resource allocation. Between 1992 and thepresent: building upand improving the socialist market economic system. In this stage, efforts weremade both on the micro and macro economic fronts. On the micro front, reform ofthe ownership structure mainly featuring the introduction of joint-stockincorporation was pursued across the country with an aim to establish amodernized corporate system in China. While on the macro front, reform wascarried out to improve the investment, foreign exchange administration andfinancial regulatory system so as to establish more indirect instruments formacroeconomic management. With the deepening of reform, China's economic opening-uphas also been gradually advanced. We first selected four coastal citiesincluding Shenzhen as the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in July 1979 to serveas the pilot windows for attracting foreign investment. In 1984, the SEZs werefurther expanded to include other 14 coastal cities such as Qingdao and Dalian.At the same time, the Yangze River Delta, Pearl River Delta and south FujianProvince were also opened as economic zones for foreign investment. Economicopening up entered a new stage in 1992 when almost all sectors were liberalizedfor foreign investment except those very few special industries of strategicsignificance to national security. On December 11, 2001, China joined the 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 3/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World WTO,an event of profound significance which has highlighted not only China'sdetermination and confidence to further integrate into the process of economicglobalization, but also a leap forward of its economic reform and opening up. The reform and opening up efforts made in the past twodecades have produced eye-catching achievements for China's economicdevelopment. China's GDP rose from RMB362.4 billion yuan in 1978 to RMB10.2trillion yuan in 2002, turning China from the 11th [1] tothe 6 th largest economy in the world. At the same period of time,foreign trade expanded from US20.64 billion, 32 nd place in theworld, to US620.77 billion, ranking the 5 th in the world, whileforeign exchange reserves increased from US840 million in 1979 to US286.4billion in 2002. Inflow of foreign capital totaled more than US600 billion,and China also maintained a pool of overseas assets exceeding US400 billion.All these figures indicated a substantial improvement of China's economicstrength and the living standard of the Chinese people, which has helped tostrengthen China's position in the global economic and political arena. In terms ofreform and opening up of the financial sector, the achievements can besummarized into four aspects. First of all, a financial organizational frameworkhas been established, in which various financial institutions including banks,securities companies and insurance companies compete and coordinate with eachother. Second, financial market is being gradually improved and money markethas developed to a certain degree. Third, regulation over the financial markethas been shifted from direct control to indirect oversight. Fourth, a financialregulatory system has been established in line with the realities in 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 4/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World China.China's financial industry has been growing steadily over the past two decades.At the end of 2002, outstanding balance of loans in all financial institutionsreached RMB18.3 trillion yuan while total capitalization in the stock marketamounted to RMB3.8 trillion yuan. Meanwhile, a total of 180 operationalestablishments were set up by foreign financial institutions in China, including146 foreign bank branches, joint-equity banks or wholly foreign-funded banks. Besides,foreign banks also established 221 representative offices in China. Theseinstitutions altogether have US39.2 billion worth of assets. Though theirshare in China's total financial assets is merely 2% or so, as an importantpart of the financial industry in China, their role in the development of theentire industry is significant. II.Securing financial resources in an uncertain world: China's experience The reform path we covered in the past 20 years reminds usthat the following factors have to be taken into consideration in the processof securing financial resources in a changing world. 1. Preserving political and social stability by taking agradual approach to reform constitutes an important precondition for securingfinancial resources 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 5/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World China'sexperience shows political and social stability could provide effective supportto economic growth and secure the efficient operation of the whole economicsystem. International experience also proves that political instability andsocial unrest could easily trigger economic or financial crisis, thus harming oreven stagnating the economic growth. For us, practice is the only criteria totest truth and our reform has been unprecedented on any measurement. On such acount, whenever we introduce a policy measure, it must be preceded with pilotprojects and experience of the pilot will then be reviewed and improved beforebeing introduced nationwide. The establishment of SEZs in Shenzhen and othercoastal cities is an important element of this experience. The advantage ofthis approach is that reform measures are formulated more closely based oneconomic situation in different localities. And tested measures are easilyacceptable to the people and can help maintain political, economic and socialstability. Anotherexperience we have learned is that two preconditions must be satisfied forgradual and sequenced reform to succeed. First of all, a well and pragmaticallydefined development strategy must be put into place. We initiated a "three-stepstrategy" to develop China's economy at the very beginning of reform in accordancewith China's own characteristics at that time. Secondly, we need strongleadership and consistent policies. The current Chinese political systemfeatured with a multi-party cooperative arrangement under the leadership of theChinese Communist Party has ensured smooth steering of China's economicconstruction and consistent advancement of the government policy. 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 6/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World 2. Changing the government's function and improvinginvestment environment In the commandeconomy before reform and opening up, the government played a critical role inthe function of the economy. Theabsence of a market mechanism meant that enterprises did not have autonomy indecision making and business operation; governments at various levelsintervened in the operation of enterprises and financial institutions. Sincethe initiation of reform and opening up, China has taken a series of measuresto transform the government's function and nurture market mechanism in order tostrengthen the market's role in resource allocation and investment for thepurpose of creating a favorable investment environment for sustainable economicdevelopment and boosting the confidence of market participants at home andabroad in the long-term prospect of the Chinese economy. Governmentsupport to economic growth should not take the form of intervention inenterprises' day-to-day business operation and decision making and should notbe measured by the proportion of share holding by government. Rather, to support economic growth, thegovernment needs to create a market mechanism, investment environment and legalframework conducive to economic growth and the government should engage inbuilding market infrastructure and provide a favorable environment for marketplayers. 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 7/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World Thetransformation of government function is conducive to the growth of marketmechanism and it enhances market's role in resource allocation and investmentdecision. Consequently, it reducesthe chance of human error and improves the efficiency of resource allocation.The massive capital inflow that has continued for many years in China isattributable to the improvement of investment environment. 3. Improving the legal framework and the market mechanism Theestablishment of legal framework is an important part of market infrastructurebuilding. Compared with administrative measures and administrative penalty,regulating economic behavior with legislation is more effective. For more than two decades, China hasbeen working actively to improve legislation, promulgating and amending lawsand regulations in accordance with international practice. As a result, a legalframework has been put in place in line with market economy, facilitating theimprovement of market mechanism and transformation of government function. 4. Building a credit culture and ensure market confidence 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 8/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World For markets tooperate smoothly, an economy needs to build a credit culture and all economicagents must act in good faith. Credibility of the government, of enterprisesand of individuals is essential to sound economic development. In recent years,the Chinese government has made tremendous efforts and a lot of measures havebeen introduced to establish a credit culture. In the financial sector, we arebuilding a credit information system to help build a credit culture in theentire Chinese society. It must berecognized that whether the momentum of sustained and rapid economic growthwitnessed in the past two decades and more can be carried into future depends,to a very large extent, on the development of credit culture in China. A nationthat acts in good faith and accumulates wealth through hard work can give moreconfidence to foreign investors and attract more capital inflow. 5. Participating in economic and financial globalization As economicand financial globalization continues, geographic boundaries give way to thefree flow of resources, especially financial resources. For a developingcountry like China, timely participation in globalization helps us not only toattract capital inflow, but also to learn valuable technology and expertisefrom advanced countries for the benefit of improving the efficiency and qualityof the economic growth at home. For this reason, the Chinese government and people engaged in 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 9/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 Securing Financial Resources in An Uncertain World difficultnegotiations for 15 long years before finally becoming a member of the WTO.Although WTO membership may bring some challenges in the short term, but in thelong run, this is an inevitable outcome of economic opening-up and integrationwith the world economy and China will benefit from the membership. Whathappened in the first year after WTO accession has proved it. On the otherhand, the Chinese government has realized that economic globalization hasnegative impact too. China is a country in transition. How to make full use ofits positive impact, manage its negative impact and reduce risks to the largestextent is a major task of ours and an important reason in our gradual andsequenced approach to reform and openingup. Therefore, we have never advocatedcopying other countries' approach and experience. When learning from other countries' experience, we haveemphasized that the specificity in China must be taken into consideration.Practice has proved the effectiveness of our policies and measures. In conclusion,developing countries need to improve government functions, nurture marketmechanism, improve investment climate and preserve political and socialstability in order to secure financial resources in an uncertain and rapidlychanging environment. It is gratifying to see that China has successfullyopened up and reformed its economy and sustained rapid growth in the process ofimproving market mechanism and transforming government functions. We areconfident that as the economic globalization continues, the Chinese economywill grow in a sound, rapid and sustained manner. 3688110/3688175/3708251/index.html 10/12 26/10/2021, 10:48 [1] World Bank, 1980.
