Title: Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China
text: 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China Dr. Guo Shuqing Deputy Governor, People's Bank of China Director-General, State Administration of Foreign Exchange China's rapid economic growth in the past 20 years largely benefited from huge volume of cross-border capital flows, particularly capital flows in the corporate sector. Chinese government has always been targeting the management of the capital flows in corporate sector as a top priority in its overall foreign exchange administration. . Existing management of Capital Flows in Corporate Sector As the statistics of international balance of payment shows, in 2001, China's capital inflow was USD99.5 billion and capital outflow was USD64.7 billion; and in the first half of year 2002, China's capital inflow and outflow was USD57.3 billion and USD45.1 billion respectively. From 1994 to the end of June 2002, China's cumulative capital inflow amounted to USD723.0 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 1/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China billion, and its cumulative capital outflow amounted to USD542.6 billion (Table 1). On today's occasion, I would like to briefly introduce China's management of the capital flows in corporate sector. Table 1 :China's capital inflows and outflows in the capital and financial account of BOP in 1994-2001 (in billions of USD) 1994 1995 1996 1997 1998 1999 2000 2001 2002.1-6 2002 Capital inflow 61.8 67.7 71.0 92.6 89.3 91.8 92.0 99.5 57.3 120.0 Capital 29.1 29.0 31.0 71.6 95.6 86.5 90.0 64.7 45.1 100.0 outflow Data sources: Balance of Payments Annual Report 2002, China's Foreign Exchange Administration Annual Report 2001. The data of 2002 are estimations. 1. Foreign Direct Investment With approval of relevant regulatory authorities, foreign investors can establish or expand wholly-funded enterprises and affiliated corporations, set up joint ventures and cooperative enterprises, or invest in an enterprise already in operation, provided that their investments are in conformity with the national guiding catalog of industries. After getting the approval, the investing enterprises should go through necessary procedures such as registering with the government agency in charge of foreign exchange administration (SAFE and its branches), which is responsible for the approval, registration and foreign 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 2/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China exchange account surveillance (including supervision over the enterprises' sale and purchase of foreign exchanges) related to transactions and exchanges under investment account. Foreign direct investment can be liquidated upon approval by the regulatory authorities. Generally speaking, such an application will be approved. By the end of 2001, China had altogether approved 390,484 foreign-funded enterprises with total foreign direct investment reaching USD395.2 billion. Currently, 189,000 foreign-funded enterprises still remain in operation. In recent years, China has paid more attention to the investment from multinational corporations, permitting them to merge and acquire domestic enterprises. In July of 2000, the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (MOFTEC) and the State Administration of Industry and Commerce (SAIC) promulgated Provisional Regulation on Domestic Investment of Foreign-funded Enterprises, which authorizes investment in the middle and west of China by FFEs exceeding 25% of their total investment to be treated as FFEs. In 2001, MOFTEC promulgated Circular on Some Issues Concerning Foreign-funded Joint-stock Companies, in which it is stipulated that qualified joint ventures, cooperative enterprises and wholly foreign-funded enterprises can be listed and issue A share in China. Relevant government agencies also issued some policies to attract venture capital investment in 2001. After its accession to the WTO at the end of 2001, China not only removed prohibitions or restrictions on foreign investment in industries such as civil aviation and telecommunication, but also committed to raising equities permitted to be held by foreign investors in some other industries. 2. Portfolio Investment In China, residents must apply for approval by the State Council and other regulatory authorities before they buy stocks and other securities abroad. With approval, domestic enterprises can issue stocks abroad. And with approval, corporations that 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 3/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China issued H shares abroad can repurchase their shares. The funds raised abroad must be repatriated to China, and the enterprises can keep the funds either in foreign exchange or in RMB by selling foreign exchanges to designated banks. As for enterprises to open foreign exchange accounts at home or abroad, prior approval is required. By the end of August of 2002, 67 domestic enterprises had issued shares in overseas market, raising 18.5 billion USD of funds. Furthermore, there are about 70 so-called red-chip corporations that had registered in Hong Kong and raised 43.7 billion USD. Non-residents are not allowed to invest in A share market in China. They are not allowed to sell or issue any stock or other securities in China, but they can buy B shares. At the end of 1992, the B share market was founded in China to meet particular needs of foreign investors. Foreign investors are not allowed to deposit cash into their B-share margin accounts. The inflow and outflow of B-share investment funds over 50,000 USD or other equivalent foreign exchanges must be reported for the sake of BOP statistics. In February of 2001, domestic investors were allowed to buy B shares using foreign exchanges, but they are not allowed to remit B share investment funds abroad without permission. At present, there are 110 companies issuing B shares in China (3 companies withdrew from the market this year), with a total of 4.96 billion USD funds raised. Now there are 1197 listed companies in China, among which, companies issuing A shares total 1173 and 86 companies are listed in both the A share and B share market. Since 1991, RMB 645 billion have been raised in the A-share market, plus USD 67.16 billion or RMB 550 billion raised in the H-share, B-share and red-chip markets. Residents must acquire approval of regulatory authorities before they purchase, sell or issue bonds and money market instruments abroad. Domestic institutions (including financial institutions and non-financial enterprises) are allowed to issue bonds abroad. Non-financial enterprises are not allowed to purchase or sell foreign bonds and money market instruments. 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 4/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China Only when having passed the inspection of qualification and exposures of foreign exchange position, and with the motivation of avoiding risk or hedging,can financial institutions buy foreign financial derivatives and other instruments. State-owned enterprises should acquire the approval in advance for overseas commodity future transactions. As for the Chinese-funded enterprises to hedge their external debts, if the transactions are entrusted to foreign banks, they should be approved by SAFE (including its branches). If such hedging transactions are to be undertaken by foreign-funded enterprises, they need not get approval in advance, but the transactions should be reported to SAFE (including its branches) afterwards. 3. External Debt External debt is a sensitive component of capital flow in the corporate sector, which includes financial credit provided between residents and non-residents, and the guarantee provided by residents to non-residents. China has been practicing strict quantitative control on external debt for a long time. Recently it turns to rely more on indirect control measures. The state decides on the amount of long and medium-term external debt and the annual quota of external debt, and tries to arrange the structures of industry, region, maturity and currency reasonably, so as to ensure adequate reimbursement. When borrowing abroad (including project financing), enterprises should first acquire approval for the projects and financing terms from regulatory authorities, and then accomplish financing directly or through banks. Afterwards, enterprises must finish such procedures as external debt registration, account management, principal and interest payment, and foreign exchange sale or purchase. The state practices control over balances of short-term external debt. Non-resident deposits are compiled into statistics of short-term external debt, and are reconciled in the short-term loan quotas of banks. 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 5/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China Both Chinese-funded enterprises and foreign-funded enterprises should get prior approval of the State Council when they tend to issue bonds abroad. The long and medium-term external debt borrowed by any foreign-funded enterprise should not exceed the balance between its total investment and registered capital. When a foreign-funded enterprise borrows foreign exchange from the Chinese-funded financial institutions, the Chinese-funded financial institutions should register with SAFE (including its branches) about such loans. External guarantee is also a very important part of external debt administration. External guarantee provided by Chinese-funded enterprises, joint ventures, cooperative enterprises, non-banking financial institutions, together with external guarantee under financing by Chinese-funded designated foreign exchange banks, should be first examined and then be registered, approved and inspected by the regulatory authorities. Wholly foreign-funded enterprises can provide external guarantee on the basis of self-determination, but should register with SAFE (including its branches) afterwards. Except for on-lending of sovereign debt, government agencies and institutions should not provide external guarantee. At the end of June 2002, calculated according to the latest guidelines of IMF on external debt statistics, China's gross external debt was 169.11 billion USD, with a decrease of 1 billion USD over the end of the previous year. 4. China's Direct Investment Abroad When domestic enterprises invest abroad, they should first acquire the approval of the proposed investment project from the regulatory authorities, and then go through examinations of foreign exchange sources and investment risks. There are some limits on enterprises' purchase of foreign exchanges to invest abroad. For any enterprise that invests abroad, it should register with the regulatory authorities, repatriate home its profits earned abroad, and report its financial and statistical information 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 6/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China as required. By the end of June of 2002, China had approved 6758 enterprises to invest abroad, with a total contractual Chinese investment of USD 8.88 billion. To be frank, most people believe that it has been underreported. 5. Other Capital Flows Non-residents should have effective certificates when they remit foreign exchange deposits or bring foreign currency out of China. As for commercial credits under current account transactions provided by residents to non-residents, there is nearly no control over such transactions and exchanges. From the part of foreign exchange administration, the only procedure is to verify the authenticity of the transactions. For such transactions as non-residents' purchase and sale of real estates within China, provision of guarantee by non-residents to residents (excluding Chinese-funded enterprises), and provision of commercial credit under current account transactions by non-residents to residents, there are mainly such administrative procedures as registration, verification, recording and account management that should be gone through during the process of transaction and exchange. And from the perspective of investment policies, the above capital flows are encouraged in China. Presently, the following transactions are subject to strict prohibition: purchase, sale or issue of bonds in domestic market by non-residents; purchase, sale or issue of money market instruments in domestic market by non-residents; purchase, sale or issue of collective investment securities in domestic market by non-residents; purchase, sale or issue of financial derivatives in domestic market by non-residents; issue of collective investment securities abroad by residents; issue of financial derivatives abroad by residents; and purchase of real estates abroad by residents. . problems in the MANAGEMENT of capital flowS in corporatE sector 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 7/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China China has been encouraging inward foreign direct investment and non-residents' investment in B shares while discouraging domestic issue of bonds either in RMB or foreign exchanges by the Chinese or foreign-funded enterprises and direct investment abroad by residents. China encourages domestic enterprises to be listed in domestic or overseas capital markets while strictly prohibiting the inflow of short-term capital. Such policies are broadly successful. They have insulated the Chinese economy from external shocks, reduced fluctuations in financial markets and maintained the stability and development of the domestic financial system. Proper control over capital inflow has produced favorable environment for the healthy development of China's economy. But at the same time, such kinds of control have also caused some problems or disadvantages. Table 2 :Price comparison between A share and B share of some enterprises (on September 23, 2002) Shenzhongguan ShenshenbaoShennanbo Feiyada Shenshenfang Fangda Chenming Yuedianli Gujinggong Zhangyu A 13.90 share(RMB) 13.02 15.38 16.52 9.56 11.39 15.42 12.72 15.42 17.62 B 5.82 share(RMB) 6.89 4.79 5.90 3.87 4.93 6.41 5.25 6.92 8.12 B 5.48 6.49 4.51 5.56 3.65 4.65 6.04 4.95 6.52 7.64 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 8/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 share(HKD) Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China B/A 0.419 0.529 0.311 0.357 0.404 0.433 0.416 0.413 0.449 0.461 For example, the A-share issuing price of Shanghai Petroleum and Chemical Corp. is 10.07 yuan, while its H-share issuing price is 0.97 yuan in Hong Kong. Such a large difference in issuing prices leads to great discrepancy in fund-raising costs. And the high price of A-share will likely to cause financial foams and speculation. Table 3 :Price comparison between A share and H share of some enterprises (on September 23, 2002) Zhongguoshihua Shanghaishihua HuanengguojiDongfanghangkong A 3.46 10.07 12.65 5.67 share(RMB) H 1.73 0.97 6.58 0.98 share(RMB) H 1.63 0.91 6.2 0.92 share(HKD) 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 9/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 H/A Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China 0.5 0.096 0.520 0.173 The difference between negotiable shares and non-negotiable shares causes fragmentation in the capital market. The stocks of the state-owned enterprises are divided into state-owned shares, legal entity shares and negotiable shares. The rights enjoyed by the same shares are actually different, which results in the discrepancy between negotiable shares and nonnegotiable shares. At the end of August, 2002, the total market capitalization of listed companies in China was 4650 billion yuan in RMB and the negotiable market capitalization was 1530 billion yuan in RMB, or 32.9% of the total market capitalization. The high proportion of state-owned stocks did not mean effective maintenance of state equities. On the contrary, it worsened inside control of the enterprises. Medium-and-small-sized investors' rights are impaired, which is neither beneficial to the improvement of corporate governance, nor helpful for small shareholders to invest in large-sized stocks. And such a problem is an impediment to the healthy and standardized development of the stock market, as indicated by the turbulent stock prices that are susceptible to be manipulated for speculation. That stocks issued by the same enterprise are priced and transacted in both RMB and foreign exchanges aggravate the fragmentation of the capital market. Allowing enterprises to be listed in the capital market to improve corporate governance is undoubtedly very important for enterprises to raise their competitiveness. But the artificial separation of A share and B share in a uniform capital market cut the linkage between the same capital market instruments. The same enterprise issues different stocks, which has in fact engendered a situation of same stocks with different prices and same stocks with different rights. At present, the price difference of A share and B share and of A share and H share issued by the same enterprise are enormous (Table 2 and Table 3). Restrictions on bond issue by enterprises at home increase their dependence on banks, which circumscribed the development of the capital market. At the end of 2001, China's total value of bonds only accounted for 29% of the Gross Domestic Production (GDP), and the value of corporate bonds accounted for less than 5% of the total value of bonds. All these 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 10/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China led to enterprises' excessive dependence on bank loans, and a high proportion of non-performing loans in the banking sector. A capital market without corporate bonds is actually a "one-leg" giant. The stock market in disequilibrium is also vulnerable to instability. Supervision over short-term capital flow is far from adequate. Because of the partial convertibility of RMB under capital account, the flow of short-term capital has not generated as many market fluctuations as in other countries so far. However, we realize that the government faces great challenges in their administration of capital flow, especially the supervisory loopholes or vacuums could possibly become channels for illegitimate capital flow and allow destructive funds to escape supervision and produce potential risks. For instance, some transactions under capital account could be disguised as current account transactions, and some overseas investment funds could illegally enter into the A share market. Some policies need to be changed after China's accession to the WTO. For example, as in the administration of external debt, we used to treat the loans provided by domestic foreign banks as external debt, and now we could not do this any longer. For another example, we used to place too much control over residents' overseas investment, such as demanding residents go through the examination by relevant authorities of the investment risks and set aside 5% of the investment as deposits to guarantee the repatriation of profits earned abroad, which are actually obstacles to China's economic development. For the moment, we're busy cleaning up and revising such outdated controls. III. Tentative policies to improve the management of capital flow in corporate sector China's reform and opening-up has entered a brand-new stage. The Chinese government has made it very clear that, utilizing foreign capital should be combined with economic restructuring, upgrading and optimizing industrial structure, and improving the enterprises' efficiency. Utilizing foreign capital should also be proceeded in combination with establishing and perfecting the socialist market economy, enhancing enterprises 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 11/12 26/10/2021, 10:44 Management Of Capital Flows In Corporate Sector:Current Situation And Outlook In China Date of last update OCT. 11, 2002 3688110/3688175/3708257/index.html 12/12

Title: China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform
text: 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform Dai Xianglong Governor of the People's Bank of China "The financial industry is very important and is the core component of modern economy", Mr. Deng Xiaoping put it during his visit to Shanghai in 1991. At the National Financial Work Conference in February 2002, President Jiang Zemin pointed out that finance played an essential role in resource allocation and was an important leverage in macroeconomic adjustment and that soundness of the financial industry was essential for national economic stability. This important remark further elaborated and developed the thesis that finance is the core of modern economy. The financial system consists of money, financial institutions, financial markets, financial supervision and financial liberalization. Its efficient operation is of paramount importance in modern economy. In order to bring its essential role into full play in the socialist market economy with Chinese characteristics, we need stable currency, financial institutions with reasonable division of labor, efficient financial markets, sound 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 1/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform financial policy, well sequenced financial liberalization and a regulatory system consistent with the development level of the financial industry. Since the 4th plenary session of the 13th Congress of the CPC, the third generation of the Chinese leaders has paid paramount attention to the development of the financial sector. They crystallized the goal of financial reform and developed and carried out the right policies to proceed with the financial reform in a timely manner. In 1993 the central government issued the "Opinions on Current Economic Development and Strengthening Macroeconomic Management". In addressing the overheating economy and the disorder in the financial sector at the time, this document initiated 16 measures to strengthen macroeconomic and financial regulation. The important document "Resolution on Certain Issues Pertaining to Developing the Socialist Market Economy" further clarified the goal of financial system reform and development. At the outburst of the Asian financial crisis in November 1997, the central government timely convened the National Financial Work Conference and made strategic plans to deepen the financial reform, rectify the financial order and contain financial risks. In January 1999, the central government sponsored a seminar for provincial governors and government ministers on financial issues, which greatly improved the participants' knowledge on financial industry and their competence in taking the lead in promoting financial work. In February 2002, in the context of the initiation of China's third strategic phase of modernization and WTO entry, the central government again held another National Financial Work Conference, which further confirmed the principles, goals and policy measures during the tenth five-year Plan period. These important decisions ensured that the financial industry developed in the right direction. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 2/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform The financial industry was on its fastest development and best performance over the past 13 years after the 4th plenary session of the 13th CPC Congress. After more than a decade's efforts, China established a new financial system consistent with the socialist market economy, in which the organizational structure of the financial industry, the financial markets and the financial supervisory system have further improved. The financial system has also played an important role in strengthening macroeconomic control, fighting against inflation, preventing deflation, promoting economic growth, and safeguarding social stability. In general, great achievements have been made in financial reform and development. . Improvement of the organizational structure of the financial industry has strongly supported the fast and sustainable economic growth Money supply is defined as currency in circulation, corporate and household deposits. At the end June 2002, the money supply amounted to around RMB16 trillion in China. Financial policies should be tailored to increase the money supply in an appropriate manner so as to sustain the internal and external value of the currency. Various financial institutions including the commercial banks, securities firms and insurance companies need to be established to manage and operate the monetary funds so as to optimize the allocation of the financial resources and the factors of production to further improve productivity. On a micro basis, the most important indicator ensuring finance to play its essential role in a modern economy is a system of financial organizations with complete functions and reasonable division of labor based on fair competition. According to the "Resolution on Certain Issues Pertaining to the Development of Socialist Market 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 3/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform Economy", China has established a relatively sound and healthy financial organizational system with a variety of commercial banks, securities firms and insurance companies as the mainstream institutions. At the end of June 2002, the total assets of financial institutions amounted to RMB23.2 trillion, among which RMB 22 trillion belonged to financial organizations under the supervision of the People's Bank of China (PBC), accounting for 95 percent of the total. The securities sector accounted for RMB651 billion yuan or 3 percent and the insurance industry RMB560 billion yuan or 2 percent. 1. Steady structural improvement of the banking industry In a modern economy, the function of commercial banks is to take in deposits, provide working capital loans, offer settlement and payment services and create money. Between 1979 and 1984, China established four state- owned specialized banks. In 1994, three policy banks were established, specializing in financing for policy- oriented projects. Correspondingly, the state-owned specialized banks were transformed to wholly state-owned commercial banks. The National Financial Work Conference of 1997 adopted a resolution to transform the state- owned banks into commercial banks truly operating on commercial basis. In this spirit, the wholly state-owned commercial banks accelerated their reform, improved their management and operational mechanism, emphasized the centralized legal person control system, and streamlined their branches and staff. Marked achievements have been made along these lines. From 1998 to 2001, the wholly state-owned commercial banks reduced the number of branches by 45,000 through either closure or merger, cut staff by 240,000. At the same time, they paid more than RMB500 billion yuan in tax to the state revenue and wrote off RMB250 billion yuan loan losses to support the reform of the state-owned enterprises. In 2001, the four wholly state-owned commercial 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 4/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform banks registered a profit of RMB23 billion yuan while successfully disposing of RMB61.7 billion yuan historic bad debts. In order to better support the small and medium-sized enterprises and encourage fair competition in the banking industry, China has established 10 joint stock commercial banks. On the basis of rectification and regulation, more than 2,200 urban credit cooperatives have been reorganized into 109 city commercial banks. The rural credit cooperatives have been de-linked from the Agricultural Bank of China. At the same time, three rural commercial banks have been established. The more than 30,000 rural credit cooperatives and credit cooperative unions at the county level have become the mainstream in providing financial services in the rural area and played an increasingly important role in supporting rural economic development, in improving the living standard of the rural population and in promoting the agricultural production. The introduction of foreign financial institutions also promoted financial reform and development. In the past decade, the banking industry has made great efforts to improve financial services, and to support the economic reform, opening-up and development. Total credit increased continuously with improved structure, turnover and quality. By the end of 2001, the outstanding credit in domestic and foreign currencies had reached RMB11.2 trillion, RMB 10.2 trillion more than that of the end of 1990, representing an annual growth of 19.4 percent. From 1998 to 2001, banks lent RMB 608.3 billion yuan for infrastructure and technical renovation projects financed with government debt and RMB 559.8 billion yuan for housing and consumption. In the first half of 2002, credit increased by RMB 868.3 billion yuan, of which 49 percent was made by wholly state-owned banks. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 5/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform It is estimated that non-state controlled borrowers accounted for 63 percent of the total balance of bank loans at end-June 2002. Development of the securities institutions in the improving regulatory environment The major function of securities institutions is to provide long-term capital financing. According to the decision of the central government to "gradually increase the channels and proportion of direct financing", the securities companies in China developed very fast along with improvement in market regulation. At the end of June 2002, there were 109 securities firms and 15 fund management companies. The net asset value of the funds had surpassed RMB 100 billion yuan. With the great potential of the capital market, securities companies have broad prospects of development. In the future, the business function of the securities companies will be broadened and fully developed. Institutional investors, securities investment funds in particular will be encouraged to develop with increased varieties of investment instrument. Continuous improvement of insurance institutions The basic function of the insurance industry is to diversify risks, reduce losses and to provide assurance for each and every stage of reproduction. Since the 90s of the last century, insurance industry had accelerated its reform. Life, non-life and re-insurance have been separated and the insurance institutions improved. At the end of June 2002, there were 5 state-owned insurance companies, 15 joint stock insurance companies, 19 Chinese-foreign joint-ventures and 14 wholly foreign-funded insurance companies. Meanwhile, a number of insurance intermediaries such as insurance brokers, agencies and assessors were established. Along with the reform of the 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 6/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform social security system, the demand for insurance services will grow. Commercial insurance will play an increasingly important role and the insurance companies will develop faster. . financial markets have consolidated with steady improvement of efficiency in fund allocation and utilization Financial market is the trading place for supplier and user of funds. Its main function is to mobilize and allocate financial resources and channel savings into investment projects. Through market competition, interest rate, exchange rate and rate of commission are determined by the market. The financial markets also promote the flow of the factors of production and resource allocation. A healthy and efficient financial market enables the central bank to better conduct its monetary policy and adjust the money supply in a timely manner. The "Resolution on Certain Issues Pertaining to the Developments of the Socialist Market Economy" adopted in 1993 by the central government decided to develop the financial markets with bank credit as the mainstream financing source. The National Financial Work Conference of 1997 decided to develop the financial market system consistent with the socialist market economy. Remarkable achievements have been made with regard to development of the financial markets. 1. A well-functioning money market has been developed. Money market is the trading place for short-term funds. It includes inter-bank money market, inter-bank securities market, exchange market and commercial paper. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 7/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform In the first half of 1993, irregularities emerged in the financial sector. Some credits were made against the regulations. In the spirit of the decision made by the central government, the People's Bank of China strengthened its regulation over the inter-bank money market. In January 1996, a centralized inter-bank market was established and the China Inter-bank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) was initiated. Since then the inter-bank market developed healthily and the trading volume increased. By the end of June 2002, the accumulative turnover had reached RMB3.4 trillion yuan. The inter-bank market has become the major trading place for financial institutions to manage their liquidity positions. In June 1997, China established inter-bank bond market, allowing commercial banks and some other financial institutions to involve in repo and spot transactions of government securities and financial bonds issued by policy banks. By now, the inter-bank bond market has become the largest and fastest-growing fund market. It has also become the important platform for the open market operation of the central bank. By the end of June 2002, its accumulated volume of repo transaction had reached RMB10.7 trillion yuan. In April 1994, the first nationwide inter-bank foreign exchange market was set up in Shanghai, centralizing the foreign exchange tradings. It laid the important foundation for the foreign exchange regime reform later and the adoption of a unified managed floating exchange rate. In the eight years since then, the efficiency of the interbank foreign exchange market has been improving with growing turnover. By the end of June, the cumulative turnover had reached USD478.24 billion yuan. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 8/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform With the approval of the State Council, the gold exchange has been established in Shanghai and is getting ready to start trading. Capital market developed with improved regulation Capital market is the trading place for funds of more than one-year maturity. The development of the capital market has been a gradual process. More than a decade ago, Mr. Deng Xiaoping resolutely advocated setting up securities and equity markets. In addressing the problems in the development of the securities market, President Jiang Zemin remarked, "securities markets constitute important part of the socialist market economy. It is of great importance to develop a healthy, orderly and soundly operating securities market to optimize resource allocation, adjust economic structure, mobilize saving and promote the economic growth". The Shanghai Securities Exchange and Shenzhen Securities Exchange were established in October 1990 and July 1991 respectively. The securities markets in China developed in terms of both their business size and market functions in the last 12 years of reform and development. At the end of August 2002, there were 1,197 listed companies with a total marketization of RMB4.65 trillion yuan and negotiable equity value of RMB1.53 trillion yuan. Since 1991, RMB827 billion yuan have been raised on both domestic and overseas securities markets. The securities markets played an important role in the reform of financing and investment systems, in the adjustment of industrial structure, in the transformation of management mechanism of the enterprises, and in the improvement of corporate governance of the enterprises. By the end of 2001, the state-owned enterprises and enterprises with controlling majority shares held by the state had a leverage ratio of 65 percent (excluding land), 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 9/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform one percentage point lower than that of 1995. The listed companies represent the best enterprises in China. The securities markets have become an important engine for China's economic growth. Insurance market developed in both depth and width The insurance market in China developed very fast with increasing variety of products, business, and rapid growth in premium income. Annual premium in 1989 registered RMB14.24 billion yuan whereas in 2001 it reached RMB210.94 billion yuan, representing an annual growth of 25.2 percent. In 2001, the insurance companies in China provided insurance for the property of the value of RMB19.3 trillion yuan. The annual premium income accounted for 2.2 percent of GDP, an annual growth of 0.4 percentage point. Per capita premium or insurance density was RMB168.8 yuan, indicating an annual growth of RMB41.1 yuan. Insurance companies settled claims of RMB59.83 billion yuan, RMB7.09 billion yuan more than the previous year. Commercial insurance has become one important aspect of the social security system. The development of the insurance market played an important role in safeguarding the economic development, social stability and benefiting the public. . Macroeconomic management improved markedly and the RMB remained stable The major goal of macroeconomic management is to realize the equilibrium between supply and demand, and promote the national economic development. At the 3rd plenary session of the 14th CPC Congress, President Jiang Zemin pointed out that it was an important reform to strengthen role of monetary policy and supervisory functions of the central bank. The "Resolution on Certain Issues Pertaining to Developing the Socialist Market Economy" passed by this congress also stated that it was necessary to transform the functions of the government 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 10/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform and to establish the macro-economic management consisting of development planning, fiscal and monetary policies. The major function of the central bank is to strengthen its monetary policy and financial supervision, sustain the stability of the value of RMB and the international balance of payments. After more than a decade's efforts, capacity for macro-economic management has been more skilful and the value of RMB has remained stable. 1. Fundamentally shift from direct to indirect policy instruments Monetary policy consists of the principles and strategies of the central bank to use monetary policy measures to realize the goal of macroeconomic adjustment by adjusting the money demand and supply. It is part of the national macroeconomic policy. The objective of monetary policy is to stabilize the value of RMB and thereby promote economic growth. For a long time, China had been practicing the mandatory planning on the lending of state-owned banks. In order to realize the industrial and regional development plans, not only the aggregate amounts but also the amounts of each category of credits were regulated. In order to adapt to the increasing number and variety of financial institutions and financing channels, the quota control on credit, which had been in practice in decades, was abolished in 1998. Meanwhile, a number of indirect instruments such as interest rates, open market operation, reserve requirements, central bank lending, and rediscount were adopted to adjust money supply. This indicated the significant transition from direct control to indirect adjustment. Therefore, the monetary policy has become more consistent with the development of the market economy. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 11/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform 2. An appropriately tight monetary policy successfully reigned in inflation In 1993, retail price, consumer price and other price indices surged, indicating a serious inflation. In October 1994, retail price index was as high as 21.7 percent. In June 1993, the Government took 16 policy measures to address inflation and overheating of the economy. The financial authorities adopted an appropriately tight monetary policy in line with the central government policy by raising lending and deposit rates on two occasions. The money supply was adjusted effectively. At the same time, credit policy was employed to guide the direction of fund allocation to ensure sufficient fund for State-owned enterprises, key projects and agricultural development, and to encourage effective supply. The appropriately tight monetary policy produced remarkable results, as reflected in the decline of economic growth rate to 9.7 percent and retail price index falling to 6.1 percent in 1996. 3. The implementation of a sound monetary policy effectively reversed deflationary trend In the second half of 1997, especially after the outbreak of financial crisis in Asia, the Chinese economy slowed down as investment and consumption growth lost strength, export plummeted, and lack of effective demand dragged down price level. The Chinese Government responded with a combination of proactive fiscal policy and sound monetary policy to boost domestic demand and prevent deflation. On the monetary front, we adopted a sound rather than accommodative or expansionary policy due to the following considerations. First of all, money supply was already excessive both in terms of stock and growth. Further loosening money supply will exacerbate potential financial risks and harm the soundness of financial sector. Secondly, enterprises, the state-owned ones in particular, were highly indebted and did not have much 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 12/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform demand for bank loan. Expansionary monetary policy and the subsequent relaxing of lending standard would create more bad loans and add to the pressures of dissolving financial risks. Thirdly, structural imbalances in the economy, rather than insufficient money supply, were the root cause of continued price decline. The sound monetary policy has proved to suit the Chinese realities and thus, was a wise policy decision. The sound monetary policy is not a passive policy. It contains the following proactive measures. First, money supply has increased by a reasonable degree to intensify support for economic growth. Between 1997 and 2001, M2 and M1 grew at an annual rate of 14.8 percent and 14.5 percent respectively. At end July 2002, the balance of M2 stood at 17.1 trillion RMB yuan, 14.4 percent higher than that of one year earlier; M1 stood at 6.4 trillion yuan, 17 percent higher than that of a year earlier. The growth of money supply was more than 5 percentage points higher than the sum of the growth of economy and price. Secondly, the central bank has used its policy, regulations and window guidance to guide the direction of commercial bank lending in order to improve efficiency of credit. Between 1997 and 2001, total lending increased by 6 trillion RMB yuan, focusing on the credit support to agriculture, small and medium-sized enterprises, science, technology and education. Farmer household micro credit and consumer credit for housing and education have been provided. Thirdly, the exchange rate stability of RMB has been maintained. Fourthly, efforts have been made to smooth the transmission of monetary policy. The implementation of a wide spectrum of macro-economic policies, including sound monetary policy, has enabled China to overcome the impact of Asian financial crisis and the shock of synchronized slowdown in US, Japan and Europe. The economy has been on a sound track, growing by 7.8 percent, 7.1percent, 8.9 percent and 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 13/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform 7.3 percent with an inflation rate of -0.8 percent, -1.4 percent, 0.4 percent, and 0.7 percent respectively between 1998 and 2001. The steady economic growth momentum has been kept in the first half of this year, reflected in the 7.8 percent growth rate. In order to consolidate the development momentum, the sound monetary policy will continue into the coming years to provide adequate financial support to the economy. Interest rate control has been relaxed in the process of gradual liberalization Interest rate, as the price of fund, is an important tool of financial regulation and monetary policy. In 1993, the PBC raised deposit and lending rates on two occasions, contributing significantly to reigning in inflation. Since 1996, against the background of price slide and effective macroeconomic adjustment, the central bank has cut the deposit and lending rates on eight occasions, reducing the interest payment of enterprises, especially that of big and medium sized state-owned enterprises, and promoting steady economic growth. In accordance with the government policy of gradually introducing a market determined interest rate system on the basis of central bank rate, we have taken important steps for interest rate liberalization. At present, inter-bank rate, treasury bond repo rate, discount rate are all liberalized. Interest rates of foreign currencies follow movements of international market. Urban financial institutions enjoy a 30% upward floating band, on their lending rates to small and medium-sized enterprises while rural credit cooperatives have a 50% band. Experiment of rural credit cooperatives deposit rate floating is underway in eight counties and cities. Interest rate has become an important instrument for liquidity and macro-economic management. Financial Supervision has been strengthened and financial system has functioned soundly 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 14/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform The central government has always placed importance on financial regulation and supervision. President Jiang Zemin, when addressing the 1997 National Financial Work Conference, stressed the need to improve financial legislation and supervision for the purpose of rectifying and preserving financial order. In the 2002 National Financial Work Conference, he once again stressed that intensifying financial supervision should be the top priority for the financial authorities. With the deepening of financial reform and improving financial and economic environment since the 4th Plenum of 13th CPC Congress, financial regulation and supervision has improved significantly. As a result, financial order has been restored and risks in a number of financial institutions have been dissolved. A financial regulatory and supervisory framework has been set up in line with the actual situations in China, enabling the financial sector to function smoothly. Legal framework has been developed A complete set of rules and regulations is the basis for business operation of financial institutions and the basis for effective supervision of regulatory authorities. At present, a framework of financial regulatory legislation has been set up with Law on the People's Bank of China, Securities Law, and Insurance Law at the core, and administrative rules, regulations and regulatory documents supporting these laws. Order of the financial market has improved remarkably 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 15/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform In 1993, measures were taken to address irregularities in violation of regulations on bank lending, inter-bank borrowing and interest rates. In 1995, the securities repurchase business was rectified, balance of repurchase being reduced from RMB70 billion yuan in August 1995 to the current RMB8 billion yuan. In 1996, a 4-Item Correction Program was applied to financial institutions. After the outbreak of financial crisis in Asia in 1997, the government came up with a strategic plan to strengthen financial regulation, rectify financial order, and to prevent and dissolve risks, and set up task forces to deal with concealed accounts of banks, non-compliance in business activities, illegal stock and future transactions and other irregularities in the financial sector. In four years, a total of 5,200 bank staff involved in concealed accounts non-compliance activities were penalized; more than 4,000 cases of illegal fund raising were dealt with, involving a total of 50 billion yuan, 15 billion yuan of which were recovered. Securities and future markets were consolidated; all the illegal stock exchanges in the country, totaling 41, were closed down; the number of futures exchange was reduced from 14 to 3, and transaction items reduced from 35 to 12; vicious competitive behavior of insurance companies in terms of unrealistic charges, and premium was dealt with in a strict manner, underground insurance brokerage was banned. These measures averted the chaos in the financial market and provided a favorable external environment for financial reform and economic development. Financial risks accumulated over the years are being dissolved First of all, NPLs in the wholly state-owned commercial banks are on the decline continuously. For many years, wholly state-owned commercial banks made important contributions to government revenue and to supporting 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 16/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform economic development, improving services to enterprises and households. However, due to various reasons, risks built up in the wholly state-owned commercial banks, the most acute one being excessive NPL ratio. A number of measures were taken to reduce NPLs and eliminate financial risks. In 1994, commercial banks adopted asset liability ratio management focusing on risk management and put in place a system for identifying and assessing NPLs. After the National Conference on Bank Management in June 1995, the rules of seeking profit and ensuring safety and liquidity were established for commercial bank operation. In 1998, special treasury bonds worth of RMB270 billion yuan was issued for re-capitalization of wholly state-owned commercial banks. In 1999, four asset management companies were created to take over from the four big banks problem assets worth almost RMB1.3 trillion yuan in book value. At the same time, wholly state-owned commercial banks streamlined their branches. At the beginning of 2002, commercial banks adopted the five-category loan classification standard, prudential accounting practice and operational information disclosure system. Good outcome has been produced. In 2000, the four wholly state-owned commercial banks saw their NPL growth drop for the first time and in the last quarter of 2000, the net value of NPLs began to decline. At the end of 2001, both the NPL outstanding and the ratio began to drop, by 90.7 billion yuan and 3.81 percentage points respectively. This trend continued into this year. In the first six months, the NPL outstanding decreased by RMB36.9 billion yuan, NPL ratio decreased by 1.96 percentage points to 23.39 percent. The NPL ratio of the four wholly state-owned commercial banks is expected to come down by 2 to 3 percentage points every year during the 10th Five-Year Plan period. 3688110/3688175/3708260/index.html 17/19 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Industry Progresses in Reform Secondly, the risks in non-bank financial institutions have been contained effectively. Title: Governor Expounded on China's Position in the Spring Meeting of the IMFC
text: 26/10/2021, 10:51 Governor Dai Xianglong Expounded on China's Position in the Spring Meeting of the IMFC Governor Dai Xianglong Expounded on China's Position in the Spring Meeting of the IMFC The International Monetary and Financial Committee(IMFC) held its spring meeting on 20 April in Washington D.C. Governor Dai Xianglong of the People's Bank of China led the Chinese delegation to the Meeting in the capacity of Governor for China in the International Monetary Fund. Members of this Committee and the deputies attended this meeting against a background of signs of recovery after the short-lived and mild recession in the global economy. Members of the IMFC discussed world economic outlook, prevention and dissolution of financial crisis, poverty reduction and development, anti-money laundering and suppression of terrorism financing. Governor Dai expounded on the Chinese position with regard to major issues in the international economic and financial arena. He pointed out that there were still risks and uncertainties despite emerging signs of recovery. Therefore, the international community should remain alert, take effective measures to secure a stable recovery. Governor Dai also talked about the necessity to promote multi-polarity in the world economy for a harmonized development in the world economy and for the establishment of a new international economic and political order that is fair and equitable. The IMF should place more importance to the reform of international monetary system, address the imbalance in world 3688110/3688175/3708263/index.html 1/4 26/10/2021, 10:51 Governor Dai Xianglong Expounded on China's Position in the Spring Meeting of the IMFC economic growth, support regional economic development and prevent big fluctuation in exchange rates among major currencies. Governor Dai said that the international community should pay sufficient attention to the growing imbalance in the world economic growth, work in all seriousness to promote growth in poverty-stricken countries and remove the root cause of threat to world peace and stability. Dai welcomed the Monterrey Consensus and expressed the hope that concrete actions would be taken to realize the Consensus and achieve the objective of 0.7% of GNP as official development assistance; he called on the developed countries to give full market access to the developing world, increase import from the developing countries to achieve poverty reduction objectives. The international community should promote capital flow and technology transfer to developing countries and the rational allocation of factors of production worldwide and thus boost economic growth and efficiency of the growth. On anti-money laundering and terrorism financing, Dai once again made it clear that the Chinese Government firmly supported and implemented the relevant UN Security Council resolutions, and that this work should be led by the UN and implemented by national governments. The IMF is only to provide cooperation within the mandates provided for by its Articles of Agreement. The relevant international anti-money laundering organization should enlarge its representation by having more developing country members. On the representation of developing countries in the IMF, Dai believed that the many changes in international economy in the five decades after World War II made it necessary for the IMF to work out new methods to reflect the position and requirements of developing countries, especially in quota and voting rights. 3688110/3688175/3708263/index.html 2/4 26/10/2021, 10:51 Governor Dai Xianglong Expounded on China's Position in the Spring Meeting of the IMFC Dai gave the members a briefing on the recent economic developments in China. China will continue the proactive fiscal policy and sound monetary policy, speed up reform of the state owned enterprises and banks, create conditions to improve RMB exchange rate regime and deliver WTO commitments on financial market opening. China has joined in the General Data Dissemination System as of 19 April and will disclose economic and financial statistics according to the relevant IMF standards and scope. Before the IMFC meeting, the G24 Ministers coordinated their positions on major policy issues in a meeting. The Alternate Governor of China at the IMF, Assistant Governor Li Ruogu of the People's Bank of China attended the meeting as an observer and delivered a speech. Title: China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia
text: 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia Ladies and Gentlemen, Let me take this opportunity to share with you my observations on the opening-up of China's financial sector and financial cooperation in Asia. Through reform over the years, China has by and large put in place a financial system in line with the socialist market economy with the financial sector growing steadily in the process of reform. The value of RMB has remained stable both at home and abroad and China's external debt is kept within a comfortable range. Foreign exchange reserves reached US 227.6 billion in the end of March, US15.4 billion more than the beginning of this year. The NPLs in the wholly state-owned commercial banks are in decline both in terms of its ratio and in the total lending portfolio absolute number. However, many problems need to be addressed urgently if the financial sector is to grow further. First of all, the financial institutions, especially the wholly state-owned financial institutions have yet to establish an operational mechanism and corporate governance compatible with the international standards. Secondly, financial assets, especially those of the wholly state-owned commercial banks, are of low quality. Thirdly, financing structure, characterized by low proportion of direct 3688110/3688175/3708266/index.html 1/6 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia financing and high proportion of indirect financing, remains to be rationalized to reduce excessive dependence of the corporate sector on bank loans. Similar problems are found in many emerging market economies in Asia. China became a full WTO member last December. Gradual opening-up of the financial market is part of our WTO commitments. By December 2006, foreign banks will have been granted national treatment. Faced with grave challenges posed by the WTO membership, China will speed up reform in the financial sector and gradually open it up in a bid to achieve sustainable and sound development. First of all, the overhauling of the wholly state-owned commercial banks will escalate to transform them to be modern financial institutions. The objectives of this reform is to transform the four wholly state-owned commercial banks into large modern banks fully competitive in the international market within five years or a longer time frame. Those qualified wholly state-owned banks will be reorganized into joint-equity banks with the state holding the majority stake. The major tasks at the moment include improving corporate governance, reducing the NPLs ratio, dissolving financial burdens left over from history, and bringing CAR up to international standard. The domestic banks should become fully competitive when foreign banks receive national treatment in December 2006. Secondly, improve decision-making and conduct of the monetary policy. At the moment, the central bank is pursuing a sound monetary policy to support economic growth and prevent deflation. The objective of monetary policy is to maintain stability of the currency value. At the same time, the central bank should support the development of capital market. RMB interest rates liberalization will proceed steadily with expanding fluctuation band. 3688110/3688175/3708266/index.html 2/6 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia Thirdly, we will continue to implement the managed floating exchange rate regime with the exchange rate determined by market demand and supply of foreign exchange. Under the precondition of maintaining exchange rate stability, we will further improve the exchange rate regime. China's current account was liberalized in December 1996. The capital account remains under control with varying degree for different items. Foreign direct investment is subject to registration; external borrowing requires application and approval; foreign capital investment in RMB denominated securities is not allowed for the time being. The use of foreign capital in China has reached a new level as Chinese overseas investment is growing while massive capital flows into China. As the foreign exchange reserves continue to grow, we will gradually relax restrictions on transactions under capital account and promote capital account convertibility. Fourthly, financial supervision will be further strengthened. The current arrangement of segregation among banking, insurance and securities industries under different regulatory authorities is not likely to be changed in a fairly long time to come. Now that China has joined the World Trade Organization, foreign financial institutions operating in China should also conduct their business within this legal framework. Since the beginning of this year, all the commercial banks have been required to adopt five-category loan classification system, provide provision for NPLs and write off bad loans in accordance with international practice. In June this year, the four wholly state owned commercial banks will disclose their performance information of the last year. Ladies and Gentlemen, 3688110/3688175/3708266/index.html 3/6 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia Asian financial crisis has taught us the lesson that if Asian economies could not work more vigorously to set up a mechanism for regional monetary cooperation, it would be difficult to avoid speculative attacks. According to WTO statistics, the commodity export of Asia amounted to US1.65 trillion in 2000, out which more than US800 billion, or 49%, were intra- exports among Asian countries. In 2001, the foreign exchange reserves of 12 Asian economies exceeded US1.12 trillion, accounting for almost 60% of the world total. Growing economic and trade links among the Asian countries provide a solid basis for regional financial cooperation while the abundant foreign exchange reserves will serve as a reliable funding source for the region itself, and increase its capacity to cushion impact of external shocks. At the current stage, central banks in Asia should further build up regional financial cooperation among each other. First, financial sector opening up should intensify to support regional trade expansion. By March 2002, 185 operational offices have been established by foreign banks in Mainland China, with a total assets amounting to US38.6 billion, 60 percent of which are held by banks from other Asian countries. China will further open up its financial sector to the Asian economies in accordance with its WTO commitments. At the same time, China's commercial banks will gradually expand their operational network in other countries. Commercial banks in Asia should work together to create a favorable environment for regional trade development. Second, Asian financial market needs to be further developed. As important international financial centers in the Far East, Tokyo, Hong Kong and Singapore, each boasting of unique advantages in trading certain financial products, should increase coordination and grow together in competition. While efforts should be continuously made to promote money market development, joint research should also be conducted on developing capital market, in particular the bond market. EMEAP 3688110/3688175/3708266/index.html 4/6 26/10/2021, 10:51 China's Financial Opening-Up and Financial Cooperation in Asia (Executive Meeting of East Asian and Pacific Central Banks) should play a stronger role in promoting regional bond market development and in establishing regional payment and settlement system. Thirdly, central bank cooperation within Asia should be strengthened. Within the framework of Chingmai Initiative based on the solid financial cooperation under "103" mechanism the signing of bilateral swap agreement should speed up. For the time being, China has already signed swap agreements with Japan and Thailand and Japan has completed signing agreements with China, ROK, Thailand, the Philippines and Malaysia; these arrangements involve a total value of US17 billion. China and Japan are currently working with other Asian countries in order to finalize their respective swap agreements. Exploration in more in-depth monetary cooperation should begin on this basis. At the same time, we think it is necessary for central banks of the Asian countries to coordinate in interest rate and exchange rate policies to maintain exchange rate stability in Asia. Fourthly, financial regulatory authorities in Asia should have more cooperation to prevent and mitigate financial risks and resist external shocks together. It is desirable for them to exchange experiences in the areas of financial legislation, NPLs reduction and disposing of high-risk financial institutions, work together to set up an early warning system for monitoring financial risks in Asia, and strengthen cooperation in fighting against money laundering and counterfeiting activities. Thank you.
