Title: Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability
text: 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability To Read Chinese Version The State Council Information Office held a press conference at 10:00 a.m. on March 22, 2020 (Sunday). Chen Yulu, Deputy Governor of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC), Zhou Liang, Vice Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC), Li Chao, Vice Chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) and Xuan Changneng, Deputy Administrator of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) were invited to brief on the governments response to global COVID-19 outbreak and the progress made in maintaining the stability of the financial market. Press questions were also answered. The transcript is as follows. Chen Yulu: Dear friends from the press, good morning! Under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee with General Secretary Xi Jinping at its core, now the situation in China is moving steadily in a positive direction, the resumption of work and production quickens, and life and work are gradually returning to normal. Targeting the needs in epidemic control and treatment, as well as the resumption of work and production, the financial system resolutely implements the decisions 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 1/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability and arrangements of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council by swiftly introducing a mix of effective and targeted policy measures. The PBC employs appropriate open market operations and targeted required reserve ratio (RRR) cuts to provide short, and medium and long-term liquidity to the banking system, so as to keep the liquidity reasonably sufficient and to ensure the stable operation of the financial market after its scheduled reopening. The PBC has promptly launched RMB300 billion worth of special central bank lending and RMB500 billion quotas of central bank lending and central bank discounts to render accurate support for epidemic containment and the resumption of work and production. The PBC worked with the CBIRC to roll out policies of loan extension and renewal to heavily hit micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and private enterprises to help them maintain stable cash flows and pull through the tough times. Meanwhile, the PBC actively guides cuts on market rates to substantially reduce the financing cost of the real economy. The above policy mix is producing remarkable results: Chinas financial system is generally sound with stable market expectations. Money and credit grow steadily fast. The national economy has weathered the epidemic while making notable contributions to global economic and financial stability. A great deal of financial services are provided on the front line of the fight against the outbreak, and employees in the financial sector have worked very hard and even made relatively large sacrifices. Up to now, a total of 1,137 employees in the financial sector have got infected, and 42 of them passed away. In the whole process, the financial system has upheld the CPCs leadership, followed relevant work arrangements, and gave full play to the CPCs guiding principles on the front line. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 2/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability Within the whole sector, we saw many excellent CPC members, outstanding individuals and exemplary models living up to their vow of remaining true to our original aspiration and keeping our mission firmly in mind. Recently, as the COVID-19 outbreak is spreading overseas, the international financial market experienced increased fluctuations, and the risks of global economic downturn rise. In this context, China faces new challenges in economic growth as the international situation develops. At present, the big picture of Chinas epidemic containment is stable. Chinas real economy is picking up gradually, and the fundamentals for sound economic growth over the long run remain unchanged. With high spirit, the financial system will resolutely implement the decisions and arrangements of the CPC Central Committee, and follow established policy frameworks and market-oriented and law-based principles to accurately grasp changes of epidemic control and treatment as well as economic situations at each stage and timely readjust policy intensity, pace and priority. We will build on the actual situations of Chinas epidemic control and treatment and economic growth to actively participate in international cooperation and to cope with the challenges arising from the complicated situations. Thank you. Journalist with China National Radio, China Media Group: My question goes to Deputy Governor Chen. Consumer price has been rising since H2 2019, and the latest statistics unveiled in February seem to be relatively high. I would like to know, what are the PBCs opinions on the trend of CPI? How to balance efforts to both maintain growth momentum and control inflation with the monetary policies? Thank you. Chen Yulu: The Law of the Peoples Republic of China on the Peoples Bank of China provides that the ultimate goal of Chinas monetary policy is to maintain the stability of the value of the currency and thereby promote economic growth. On that account, the chief goal of the monetary policy is to maintain currency stability, i.e. stabilize domestic prices and at the same 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 3/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability time keep the RMB exchange rate basically stable at an adaptive and equilibrium level. Since price stability is vital to peoples basic necessities, it has been a long-time priority of the PBC in policy formulation and implementation. Chinas CPI rose 2.9 percent year on year in 2019, which was largely driven by structural factors, namely the widely recognized soaring prices resulting from the short supply of pork and other foods. As relevant departments have introduced a set of measures to keep the supply sufficient, maintain prices stable, and guide market expectations, inflation expectations for the year of 2019 stabilized rather than further diverging. As you mentioned just now, CPI rose by 5.3 percent year on year in January and February. Structural factors and impact of the epidemic on supply are the main reasons. Therefore, it possesses the features of both a structural rise and a temporary increase. Strictly speaking, the impact of the epidemic on supply and inflation is likely to stay for a while. As the situation in China is moving steadily in a positive direction, and the resumption of work and production proceeds in an orderly manner, production will pick up over time, and product supply will rise step by step. Therefore, prices will be gradually stabilized overall, and are expected to decline on a quarterly basis in the next three quarters. Price stability depends on economic fundamentals. As Chinas macro economy remains stable, and the overall supply and demand remains broadly balanced, there is no basis for long-term inflation or deflation in China. In 2020, we will make the sound monetary policy more flexible and appropriate, ensure that policy intensity, pace and priority are in line with the development of the epidemic, and keep the growth of broad money supply (M2) and aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) generally in line with nominal GDP growth. To that end, we should keep prices basically stable and guard against the combined impact of the risks of shrinking social credit and downward economic pressure. In other words, we will properly balance efforts to stabilize growth, fend off risks and control inflation. Thank you. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 4/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability Journalist with Market News International: I have two questions. First, six major central banks have lately promised to support USD liquidity via liquidity swap lines. Will Chinas central bank join the pack or other similar international collaboration? Chen Yulu: Thank you for your question. President Xi has repeatedly emphasized that mankind is a community with a shared future. The spread of the virus has led to increased volatility in the international financial market and a sharp fall in the stock markets of Europe and the US, as well as many emerging economies. The global economic and financial growth was hit by the growing outbreak. Both the international outbreak and its impact on the global economy pose common challenges to countries across the globe. Even though we are yet to end our combat against the outbreak at home, we still try our best to overcome challenges to support the international community for the global fight against the outbreak. Currently, as COVID-19 outbreak is spreading rapidly worldwide with wider coverage and greater impact, it is imperative for all countries to enhance international coordination of public health, trade, fiscal, monetary policies and other macro-policies, so as to jointly and comprehensively enhance the synergy and effectiveness of international response. As to whether the PBC will participate in the coordination of international polices, the PBC has been actively employing multilateral, regional and bilateral channels to step up policy coordination with international organizations and central banks of major countries since the outbreak. Governor Yi Gang has for several times communicated and exchanged views with Ms. Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Mr. Agustin Carstens, General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and Mr. Jerome H. Powell, Chair of the Federal Reserve on how to effectively respond to the outbreak with monetary and financial policies. The PBC has also taken the initiative to inform the central 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 5/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability banks of G20 members and major international financial institutions of the epidemics impact and effective countermeasures. These efforts have been well received by the international community. We notice that, facing the global spread of the virus, many countries have adopted similar policy measures to counter the epidemics impact and maintain the stability of domestic financial markets. As a major international platform for macroeconomic policy coordination, G20 has made historic contributions to coordinating and driving global economic recovery since the financial crisis in 2008. The IMF, as the cornerstone of the global financial security net, shoulders the responsibility to maintain a stable global financial market. We support the G20, the IMF and other multilateral international platforms and institutions to play an active role in policy coordination and crisis relief, effectively prevent and control the impact of the global outbreak and maintain the stability of global economy and financial markets. Thank you. Journalist with CNBC: When it comes to the engagement of Chinese financial institutions in global finance, are there any other considerations and measures the PBC plan to take to stabilize the global financial market, apart from communications? Thank you. Chen Yulu: The recent growing spread of the outbreak worldwide has intensified international financial market fluctuations. The stock markets of Europe and the US, as well as many emerging economies have fallen by around 30% on average, which raises great concerns in the international community. It is still too early to say that a global financial crisis has set in for now. To determine whether there is an international financial crisis, often we need to answer three basic questions. First, is there a cross-market and persistent panic selling in the international financial market? Second, is there a massive shutdown of financial institutions, particularly systemically important financial institutions (SIFI)? Third, is the real economy worldwide 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 6/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability severely disrupted? Currently, many countries have introduced a series of countermeasures to mitigate the intensified fluctuations in the international financial market. The effects remain to be seen. Just as Vice Chairman Li Chao mentioned, theoretically speaking, the volatility of the international financial market typically affects domestic financial market through three basic channels. Firstly, the overseas pessimism may affect domestic expectations. Secondly, it is likely to affect China via the flow of international capital. Thirdly, the deterioration of balance sheet of some multinational corporations and foreign financial institutions may also affect Chinas domestic financial market. However, despite the volatility in the international financial market, the Chinese market has actually stood the test with high stability and minor fluctuations. So far, the overall performance of our financial market remains stable with relatively stable expectations and sufficient space and tools for macro policies. There are several reasons for this. First, the soundness of Chinas financial system has been significantly enhanced thanks to the progress made in the tough battle of preventing and defusing major risks and in advancing the supply-side structural reform in the financial sector, as well as the achievements of further promoting high-level financial opening-up. Second, following the market reopening as scheduled, both the market itself and its financial infrastructure have been in stable operation, which has substantially shored up investor confidence. Third, since the COVID-19 outbreak, sound monetary policies have been practiced in a flexible and appropriate manner, responding with early and swift actions. In addition, financial regulation policies have also been put in place quickly, providing strong and accurate support for heavily affected regions, MSMEs and private enterprises, thus stabilizing the economy. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 7/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability Next, facing international financial market turbulence, we will focus on the following two aspects under the leadership of the Financial Stability and Development Committee (FSDC) under the State Council. First, in line with the established principles and the policy framework, we will perform our own duties. With 70 years of high-speed development, China has become a global financial power with the worlds largest credit market and foreign reserves, as well as the second largest stock market, bond market and insurance market. Therefore, a stable financial market in China is a major contribution to global financial stability. Second, we will play an active role in the international coordination of macroeconomic policies. The performance of the international financial markets will be more closely monitored with our deepened analysis and study on the inherent laws of the current international financial volatility. Based on our experience in policy response to the epidemic, we would provide timely and constructive suggestion on the international coordination of economic policies. Meanwhile, we would join other countries in multilateral international aid for hard-hit developing countries with great difficulties, so as to collectively maintain the stability of global financial markets. Thank you. Journalist with Reuters: Recently, the US Federal Reserve swiftly lowered its benchmark interest rate to zero, and restarted quantitative easing (QE). Will the PBC further loosen its monetary policy? Is there still any space for interest rate and RRR cuts? Also, how could we prevent imported financial risks? Thank you. Chen Yulu: Thank you. As is widely known, since the international outbreak of COVID-19, countries around the world have been adopting measures to increase liquidity and reduce financing costs of the real economy, including relatively marked reduction in interest rates. Of course, some countries are raising interest rates in a bid to maintain the stability of the value of their currencies. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 8/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability With regard to China, since the domestic COVID-19 outbreak, China has fully supported epidemic control and the resumption of work and production of enterprises based on the actual situation at home and the established policy framework. In light of the overall framework of the monetary policy, the implementation of key policies are as follows. First, the RMB300 billion special central bank lending has supported over 5,000 key enterprises crucial to epidemic control, with over RMB200 billion worth of loans granted at favorable rates in total and actual financing cost at about 1.27 percent only. The central bank lending and central bank discount quotas have been increased by RMB500 billion to support restarting MSMEs work and production, and over RMB130 billion has already been issued as preferential loans with an interest rate significantly lower than the required level of 4.55 percent. Second, as the PBC has actively guided the lowering of market lending rates, the actual interest rate of corporate loans has significantly decreased. In February, the interest rate for general loans was 5.49 percent, 0.61 percentage points lower than that prior to the loan prime rate (LPR) reform. Therefore, with the strong support of structural monetary policies as well as measures to increase liquidity and guide the decline of market lending rates, Chinas real economy is marginally improving. According to the statistics of payment and settlement in March, as well as deposits and loans, from a dynamic perspective, Chinas real economy has displayed sound development. It is estimated that the economic indicators will improve remarkably in Q2, and Chinas economic growth will recover to the level around the potential output in a relatively fast manner. Regarding the direction of the monetary policy at the next stage, we will mainly focus on the following aspects. First, we will adjust the intensity, pace and priority of monetary policy according to different stages, and always ensure reasonably adequate liquidity. In particular, the growth of M2 and AFRE should basically be in line with and slightly higher than nominal 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 9/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability GDP growth. As we see, M2 increased by 8.8 percent year on year in February, whereas AFRE expanded by 10.7 percent. The two indicators well reflected the stance of our monetary policy. Second, the unique role of structural monetary policy will be brought into full play. Both the RMB300 billion special central bank lending and the RMB500 billion new quotas of central bank lending and central bank discounts should serve to guide financial institutions to enhance credit support for core enterprises in the industrial chain, as well as MSMEs and private enterprises in the upstream and downstream. In addition, the structural monetary policy also involves targeted RRR cuts and additional targeted RRR cuts for joint-stock commercial banks, which serve as their incentives and guidance. These policies should also be more vigorously leveraged at the next stage. Third, we will give full play to the role of policy finance. The RMB350 billion special credit quotas of policy banks should be properly used to provide strong credit support for work and production resumption of micro and small enterprises (MSEs) and private enterprises, key sectors for spring farming and tillage preparation, hog production and foreign trade, especially production linked to the international industrial chain with favorable interest rates. Fourth, more support will be given to small and medium-sized banks in capital replenishment and financial bond issuance, so as to further improve the overall willingness and capacity for credit supply among commercial banks. Finally, we will continue to promote LPR reform to guide further decline of real lending rates. The PBC will actively guide the banking system to surrender part of their profits to the real economy, and stabilize both the economy and finance at the same time. Thank you. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 10/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability Journalist with Hong Kong Economic Herald: Since the COVID-19 outbreak, risk incidents in domestic bond market have been on the rise. What responsive measures has the PBC taken and what are the results? What other measures are expected in the future? Thank you. Chen Yulu: The bond market is a core component of Chinas direct financing mechanism, so its stability is of high importance. Based on the current situation, the epidemic did not directly lead to a higher default rate in the market, nor did external shocks from the volatility in the international financial market result in major fluctuations at home. Therefore, Chinas bond market is generally stable. According to the statistics, since February, defaults in the domestic bond market has stayed at a normal level, with the number of first-time defaulting enterprises significantly lower than that of a year earlier. Since the outbreak of the epidemic, under the instruction of the PBC, the National Association of Financial Market Institutional Investors (NAFMII) has achieved remarkable results from three aspects. First, it has set up expeditious channels. A green channel for bond registration and issuance has been established. In particular, it provides expeditious services to heavily-hit enterprises regarding issuance, thus effectively mitigating the potential risks of interrupted capital flows. In February, issued corporate bonds totaled RMB750 billion, more than twice higher than a year earlier. Second, it has provided more facilitation. The validity period for the registration and filing of corporate bond issuance has been extended, and charges related to the registration, trading and custody of corporate bond issuance have been either reduced or exempted. Third, it has enabled early mitigation, defusing possible default risks by various means well in advance. In accordance with market- oriented and law-based principles, bond extension and replacement have been conducted for enterprises in need, so as to mitigate default risks at an early stage. Since February, RMB5.1 billion worth of bonds have been disposed of in the interbank market using different approaches. 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 11/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability The above measures have enabled the direct financing mechanism of Chinas bond market to play a highly effective role in this special period, and the market has generally remained stable. In the next step, we will continue to pay attention to enterprises in hard-hit industries including traditional services, labor-intensive manufacturing, transportation and those central to the industrial chain, continue to improve the mechanism for resolving bond defaults, make solid efforts to safeguard the stability of the bond market, and provide stronger direct financing support for epidemic control and the upcoming work and production resumption. Thank you. Journalist with Jiaohuidian, Xinhua Daily: I have two questions. First, since COVID-19 is spreading globally at an accelerated pace, will it have a decisive impact on turning the direction of the RMB exchange rate? Meanwhile, we have noticed that recently RMB has depreciated against the US dollar. Will this affect Chinas cross-border capital flow, or result in massive cross-border capital outflow? Thank you. Chen Yulu: The general public are highly concerned about the RMB exchange rate. It is known that China adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies, with the market playing a decisive role in the exchange rate formation. In recent years, the RMB exchange rate has appreciated or depreciated at times, featuring two-way fluctuations, which is driven by the market forces. Recently, due to the global spread of the epidemic, we have witnessed notable volatility in the international foreign exchange market. Despite some fluctuations, the RMB exchange rate has maintained basically stable at a reasonable equilibrium level. For instance, since the beginning of 2020, the euro has depreciated by 4.7 percent against the USD, whereas the pound has depreciated even greater by 12 percent against the USD. In comparison, RMB has only depreciated by 1.8% against the USD. From a comprehensive perspective, there has even been a rise in the CFETS RMB Index. Generally, we estimate that the RMB exchange rate against the US dollar will 3688110/3688175/3997404/index.html 12/14 26/10/2021, 10:41 Deputy Governor Chen Yulu Attends the Press Conference on Responding to Global COVID-19 Outbreak and Maintaining Financial Market Stability continue to fluctuate around 7, with downward or upward at times, featuring two-way fluctuations. The foreign exchange market is operating stably, and so is our expectation of the exchange rate. In the long run, the trend of the RMB exchange rate still depends on the stability of economic fundamentals. With a continuously improving situation of epidemic control and an increasing rate of work and production resumption at home, Chinas sound economic fundamentals in the long term will provide strong support for a stable RMB exchange rate. Meanwhile, it can be observed that in the financial market, the interest-rate spreads between domestic and foreign currencies are within a reasonable range, and Chinas foreign exchange reserves are sufficient and stable. The two factors can also help to shore up a stable RMB exchange rate. Thank you. Title: Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance
text: 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance To Read Chinese Version A press conference of Joint Prevention and Control Mechanism of the State Council was held at 10 a.m. on Friday, April 3, 2020. At the conference, Xu Hongcai, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Finance (MOF), Liu Guoqiang, Deputy Governor of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC), and Zhou Liang, Vice Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC) introduced the measures to increase local government special bonds and enhance support for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) with inclusive finance, and took press questions. Selected transcript is as follows. (This English version only covers the speech and answers of PBC Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang.) Liu Guoqiang: Friends from the press, good morning. Faced with the material impacts of the COVID-19 outbreak on MSMEs, the PBC has followed the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and resolutely implemented the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, taking 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 1/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance swift and proactive actions to cope with the new challenges posed by the epidemic, and supporting the expansion of domestic demand, the resumption of production and the protection of employment. We have introduced a series of measures to offer targeted financial services for the purposes of epidemic containment, work and production resumption, and real economy development. First, liquidity has remained reasonably adequate. Since the financial markets reopening, we have supplied short-term liquidity of RMB1.7 trillion to the markets. On the basis of the cut in required reserve ratio (RRR) across the board by 0.5 percentage points at the beginning of the year, releasing over RMB800 billion, we launched a targeted RRR cut for banks to issue inclusive loans in March, releasing another RMB550 billion of longterm fund. Second, targeted support has been provided through central bank lending and central bank discounts. The PBC launched RMB300 billion worth of special central bank lending for the battle against the epidemic, over half of which was directed towards MSMEs. With interest subsidies, the interest rate costs born by MSEs are lower than 1.3 percent. In addition, we increased the quotas on central bank lending and central bank discounts by RMB500 billion, and lowered the interest rates of central bank lending for agriculture and MSEs by 0.25 percentage points, from 2.75 percent to 2.5 percent. The central bank has contributed to support work and production resumption of MSMEs in key sectors through low-cost inclusive finance funds. Third, lending rates have decreased under the central banks guidance. On March 30, the interest rate of reverse repos in open market operations declined again by 20 basis points, bringing a total decrease to 30 basis points since the beginning of this year. Fourth, the synergy of the financial system has been leveraged. The PBC has urged large-scale state-owned banks to step up their inclusive support for MSEs, soundly implemented the special credit support for policy banks, guided local incorporated banks to serve the local economy, and strengthened countercyclical adjustments. 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 2/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance So far, these measures have achieved marked outcomes. The growth rates of broad money supply (M2) and aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) are basically in line with and slightly higher than that of the nominal GDP. Against the backdrop of partial resumption of work and production in the real economy, the amount of new loans has reached a record high. The financing of MSMEs features increase in scale, expansion in coverage and drop in cost. Money market pivot interest rates have shifted downwards as a whole. The RMB exchange rate has remained relatively stable, and shocks from external financial risks have been effectively fended off. It was determined at the 88th State Council Executive Meeting that inclusive financial support for MSMEs would be further enhanced. First, central bank lending and central bank discount quotas for small and medium-sized banks will be raised by RMB1 trillion. The RMB300 billion, RMB500 billion and RMB1 trillion represent a consecutive process which helps a large number and a wide range of MSMEs facing relatively high financing costs to access policy support of central bank lending and central bank discounts. Second, targeted RRR cuts for small and medium-sized banks were further put forward. With wide geographic distribution and acquaintance to local economy, small and medium-sized banks are innately inclusive. To put it simply, lacking opportunities to serve behemoths, they could only serve small enterprises instead. Therefore, they are endowed with inclusiveness. Exercising a relatively low RRR on small and medium-sized banks is an important initiative to promote financial supply-side structural reform, through which the structure of financial supply and allocation of credit funds are improved. As a result, small and medium-sized banks will be able to focus more on MSMEs, increase credit supply, reduce financing costs and serve the real economy. Third, support for bond financing has been reinforced. With the support of the PBC, financial institutions have issued RMB300 billion worth of MSE financial bonds, and the growth of net financing of corporate credit bonds, under the PBCs guidance, has risen by RMB1 trillion over the previous year, which not only further 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 3/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance diversifies the sources of funds for financial institutions, but also expands various low-cost financing channels for enterprises and improves financial services. In the next step, the sound monetary policy will be practiced in a more flexible and appropriate manner. We shall hold the bottom-line thinking, properly manage the intensity, priority and pace of policies in line with the different stages of epidemic containment and economic situations, and attach greater importance to supporting the restoration of the real economy. While strengthening the aggregate and countercyclical adjustments of the monetary policy, we need to properly deal with the relationship among stabilizing growth, preventing risks and managing inflation, and ensure that the growth rates of M2 and AFRE are basically in line with and slightly higher than that of the nominal GDP. Fully taking the characteristics of MSMEs and their current constraints into account, we will effectively put existing responding measures in place to help enterprises weather the tough times. We are also going to strengthen international cooperation and guide market expectations through multiple channels. Thank you. Journalist with Nihon Keizai Shimbun: Since last August, the loan prime rate (LPR) has declined by 26 basis points, which has narrowed banks spread, so some banks are calling for lowering benchmark deposit interest rate. What is your opinion on this issue? Liu Guoqiang: Ostensibly, falling interest rates does lead to narrowed spread of banks. We will, however, take many other measures, such as offering low-cost funds and ensuring reasonably adequate liquidity in the market, so as to facilitate banks to access funds with much lower financing cost in the financial market. Meanwhile, we are also mulling over enhancing support for banks, especially for small and medium-sized ones. Benchmark deposit interest rate is the ballast of Chinas 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 4/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance interest rate system. While it may be used as a tool, its special nature requires more consideration in practice. For instance, Chinas current CPI is 5.3 percent, remarkably higher than the one-year deposit interest rate, which is 1.5 percent. This has to be factored in. Besides, economic growth, internal and external equilibrium and possible greater currency depreciation pressure resulted from excessively low interest rates are also the ones that need to be taken into account. In particular, the deposit interest rate is more directly related to the general public, so any adjustment into the negative territory should involve a full assessment as well as considerations on peoples reactions. In sum, it can be used as a tool, but a more sufficient assessment is required. Journalist with Economic Daily: With its worldwide spread, will the epidemic have a greater impact than the 2008 financial crisis? And what else will the central bank do if the Q1 economic data are below expectations? Thank you. Liu Guoqiang: This is a very important question. Many people are concerned about how to look at the current economic situation and what should be done. Opinions vary, some of which are vastly different. My answer is that there will be a big impact on the world economy. But uncertainties remain as to how severe it will turn out to be and when the situation will improve. The impact has been clearly felt in several ways. The first is the industrial chain. Without the supplies of raw materials, some industries and enterprises cannot produce. The second is trade. Without orders, some enterprises cannot sell their products. Both are prominent problems. The third is expectations. Peoples sentiments are affected, with risk aversion on the rise and the market undergoing fluctuations. These are the three marked influences. 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 5/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance What will happen next? Or will the impact exceed that of the 2008 financial crisis? Not yet so far. For example, stock markets around the world have dropped by roughly 25 percent since February 24, whereas their decline in the 2008 financial crisis was about 50 percent, which is typical of a crisis. What will happen next is still hard to predict. The International Monetary Fund lately projected negative global growth for 2020, and a recession that could be worse than the downturn in the 2008 financial crisis. This was a relatively clear message, but they still used the wording could be worse. Despite the severity of the impact, it should be noted that countries around the world have introduced strong countermeasures. Moreover, they have stepped up epidemic prevention and control efforts and strengthened international cooperation. Therefore, what things will be like in the coming days should be closely watched. How will China be impacted? And how do we view the impact? Judging by normal standards rather than in the context of the epidemic, the Q1 data, I think, will surely be discouraging. Nevertheless, in terms of marginal change, March is expected to see a notable upturn compared with February. That is why I think the impact of the epidemic on China wont last long. The Chinese economy will continue to show strong resilience. And we have plenty of tools and ample room for policies to stabilize economic growth. What will be done next? As far as the central bank is concerned, greater importance will be attached to the flexibility and appropriateness of a sound monetary policy, and higher priority will be given to supporting the recovery of the real economy. To be specific, first, the intensity, priority and pace of policy conduct will be properly managed at different stages. Different stages refer to the preceding stage of epidemic prevention and control, and then the gradual resumption of work and production followed by the current stage of resuming work and production all through the industrial chain to activate the entire economy. Therefore, work will be done based on the conditions at different stages to keep liquidity reasonably 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 6/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance adequate and fully satisfy market demand. In other words, we wont allow a liquidity crunch to ever occur in the market. Of course, we dont want to see currency devaluation, either. Our aim is to keep liquidity reasonably adequate and meet market demand so that the growth rates of M2 and AFRE are basically in line with and slightly higher than that of the nominal GDP. Second, we will continue to make proper use of the RMB300 billion of special central bank lending and the RMB500 billion of central bank lending and central bank discounts, both of which have already been launched and have not been used up yet. Certainly we should use the funds in a targeted manner. Third, the newly increased RMB1 trillion of central bank lending and central bank discounts for inclusive finance will be effectively put in place. With a wider coverage than the preceding RMB500 billion, this new policy will be implemented at a faster pace so that it will link up seamlessly with the prior policy. Fourth, targeted RRR cuts will be carried out effectively so that the guiding role of the reserve instrument as a positive incentive will be brought into play. Fifth, efforts will be made to push ahead with the LPR reform, enhance the self-regulatory mechanism for interest rate pricing, and guide banks to sacrifice part of their profits to support the real economy, so as to bring down significantly the overall financing costs of enterprises. Sixth, we will strengthen international cooperation and foster a favorable international environment so as to fight the pandemic and stabilize the economy together with the international community. Also, we will further increase communications with the market and the media to convey our policy intent in a timely, public manner. Thank you. Journalist with CNBC: My first question is about the RMB300 billion and RMB500 billion worth of loans you mentioned just now. How much of the amounts is in place now? When will the additional RMB1 trillion of central bank lending be released? Liu Guoqiang: I can share some data with you. Lets start with the RMB300 billion worth of special central bank lending, which is primarily spent on key enterprises securing supplies for the fight against the epidemic, such as producing medical supplies. 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 7/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance As of March 30, nine banks operating nationwide and 10 provincial- and municipal-level locally incorporated banks had issued a total of RMB228.9 billion of loans at preferential rates to 5,881 key enterprises, each of which received no more than RMB40 million on average with an average weighted rate of 2.51 percent. The real lending rate is around 1.26 percent with a 50 percent interest subsidy granted by the MOF. The RMB500 billion worth of central bank lending and central bank discounts primarily support the orderly resumption of work and production. As of March 30, locally incorporated banks had issued a total of RMB276.8 billion loans at preferential rates including discounts to 351,400 enterprises (including rural households). To be more specific, agriculture-related loans amounted to RMB55.2 billion with an average weighted rate of 4.38 percent; inclusive loans issued to MSEs totaled RMB155.6 billion with an average weighted rate of 4.41 percent; and discounts reached RMB66.1 billion with an average weighted rate of 3.08 percent. None of these rates are higher than 4.55 percent, a ceiling set by the State Council. As to the additional RMB1 trillion of central bank lending and central bank discount, it was determined at the 88th State Council Executive Meeting a few days ago. The main purpose was to align this policy with the real economy in recovery and with the preceding policies worth RMB300 billion and RMB500 billion respectively to avoid any policy vacuum. The PBC introduces the tools of central bank lending and central bank discounts to provide small and medium-sized banks with lowcost financing support. Like previous arrangements, the interest rate of this additional central bank lending and central bank discounts is as low as 2.5 percent, so as to reduce the debt cost of these banks and accordingly expand room for the moderate lowering of their lending rates in favor of MSMEs. For this new policy, we will request small and medium-sized banks to lend loans to MSMEs at preferential rates, which are to be determined at their discretion. The ceiling rate for the RMB500 billion worth of central bank lending is 4.55 percent. However, we didnt set any limits this time. Instead, we will take certain 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 8/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance measures, such as incentive-based evaluation to encourage loan extension to MSMEs at lower rates. Even though this policy does not involve any fiscal interest subsidies, the effect of the preceding RMB500 billion central bank lending and central bank discounts shows that local governments have come up with subsidies in the absence of central government interest subsidies. On that account, we expect local governments to provide interest subsidies this time as well, so that enterprises can actually benefit from more preferential rates. As to when the policy will be carried out, we have started planning and will launch it as soon as the RMB500 billion is used up. The specifics of the policy will come out soon. Thank you. Journalist with Bloomberg News: Good morning, Im from Bloomberg News. I have a question for Deputy Governor Liu about the stability of the banking system that you mentioned earlier. According to the China Financial Stability Report released by the PBC in 2019, under the scenario of the GDP growth falling below 4.1 percent, 17 large banks failed to pass the stress test and more than 180 large banks failed to pass the liquidity test. This years projection of GDP growth is 3.1 percent, much lower than the worst scenario of 4.1 percent projected last year. So what do you think of banks performance? Will there be another stress test? Thank you. Liu Guoqiang: Based on macroeconometric models, historical situations and expert judgement, the scenario in the stress test of the banking sector in 2019 was primarily hypothetical. The stress scenario was extreme but possible, with small likelihood to materialize. It was a hypothetical condition. Since the outbreak of the epidemic, we have been closely monitoring risks in the banking system and systematically assessing the impact of the epidemic on the banking sector. Stress tests have been conducted. Relevant results will be released to the public in the updated edition of the financial stability report in a timely manner. 3688110/3688175/4006067/index.html 9/11 26/10/2021, 10:49 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends the Press Conference on Expanding Local Government Special Bonds and Enhancing Support for MSMEs with Inclusive Finance In the short run, risks will rise inevitably as the epidemic has exerted severe short-term impact on the economy and some sectors have been heavily hit. Also, the credit assets of banks will surely face some downward pressure. Nevertheless, Chinas banking sector on the whole has relatively strong loss-absorbing capacity, and is well prepared to counter risks. At end-2019, the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio of commercial banks in China stood at 1.86 percent, far below the regulatory line of 5 percent. The provision coverage ratio was 186.08 percent, and the outstanding amounts of loan loss provisions totaled RMB4.5 trillion, enough to cushion the rise in the NPL ratio. In 2019, the banking sector resolved RMB2.3 trillion of non-performing assets, with banks managing their asset quality by various means. Although some banks are having a hard time, they are able to pull through.
