Title: Exclusive Interview by Xinhua News Agency
text: 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency To Read Chinese Version Since the beginning of this year, the unexpected outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic has taken an unprecedented toll on the Chinese economy and the global economy as a whole. The Peoples Bank of China (PBC) has resolutely strengthened countercyclical adjustments of monetary policy, developed innovative policy instruments and thus provided solid support for stabilizing businesses and safeguarding employment. Facing the current economic and financial situations, how will the PBC implement the monetary policy in H2 2020 and how will it address the increasingly complicated and volatile international situations? The Xinhua News Agency had an exclusive interview with the PBC Governor Yi Gang on these issues. Monetary Policy Has Been Effectively Implemented Journalist: What financial policies has the PBC adopted to cope with the impacts of the pandemic? Yi Gang: In response to the impacts of the pandemic, the PBC has resolutely strengthened countercyclical adjustments of monetary policy and developed innovative policy instruments. The major measures can be summarized in six aspects, namely 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 1/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency expanding aggregates, securing supply, promoting growth, lowering interest rates, adjusting structure, and protecting market entities. During the Spring Festival holiday, the PBC launched RMB300 billion worth of special central bank lending as an emergency measure, which yielded positive results in securing supply. Decisive efforts were made to support the reopening of Chinas financial markets on February 3 following the holiday as scheduled, and a total of RMB1.7 trillion of short-term liquidity was injected into the markets, which was more than expected. After announcing an across-the-board cut of 0.5 percentage points in the required reserve ratio (RRR) on January 1, the PBC lowered the RRR for another two times, releasing RMB1.75 trillion of long-term funds in total. Subsequently, the volume of monetary policy instruments increased from RMB300 billion, to RMB500 billion, and then to RMB1 trillion. Policies have different implications under different circumstances. As the volume grows, the interest rates are increasingly market-based. With these instruments, commercial banks have provided low-cost loans for the real economy, thus rendering strong support for stabilizing businesses and safeguarding employment. Journalist: Whats your comment on the financial performance in H1 2020? Yi Gang: There are indeed many gratifying outcomes registered in macro financial statistics for H1, which shows that the sound monetary policy has been effectively put in place. In terms of macro aggregates, various financial indicators were significantly higher than those of the same period last year. At end-June, broad money supply (M2) increased by 11.1 percent year on year, and outstanding aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) reported a year-on-year growth of 12.8 percent. Loans increased by RMB12.1 trillion in H1, RMB2.4 trillion more than the growth in the same period last year. 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 2/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency As for prices, since the beginning of this year, we have focused on guiding a downward movement of major market rates. The 7-day reverse repo rate dropped by 30 basis points to 2.2 percent. The interest rate of medium-term lending facility (MLF) was lowered by 30 basis points to 2.95 percent. The 1-year loan prime rate (LPR) fell by 30 basis points to 3.85 percent. The interest rate of central bank lending was reduced by 50 basis points. With the guiding of the monetary policy, the overall market rates declined, which led to a significant reduction of the financing costs for businesses. In June, the weighted average interest rate of bond repos stood at 1.89 percent, 0.21 percentage points lower than that at end-2019; the 10-year government bond yield was 2.82 percent, down 0.32 percentage points from end2019; and the interest rates on loans for inclusive finance, micro and small businesses (MSBs), private enterprises and the manufacturing sector all reached a record low. In particular, the lending rate for inclusive finance stood at around 5 percent, down 0.8 percentage points from a year earlier. Descending interest rates have enabled vigorous support for the real economy, leading to significant optimization of the loan structure and a remarkable increase of market entities supported by inclusive MSB loans. At end-June, there were nearly 30 million market entities with a credit line, and over 23 million had outstanding loans. Most of these entities are MSBs and selfemployed businesses. Financial aggregate and increment will be kept at reasonable levels. Journalist: Whats your view on Chinas macroeconomic situations for the time being? 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 3/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency Yi Gang: Since the pandemic has been effectively contained domestically, China has taken the global lead in economic recovery. In Q2, Chinas GDP bounced back strongly, expanding by 3.2 percent from a year earlier. This made China the only major economy to post positive growth. For one thing, the industries have experienced rapid recovery; for another, demands have witnessed gradual revival, investments rebounded markedly, consumption continued to recover, and export picked up greatly. Along with the economic recovery, prices have remained stable. Meanwhile, we are especially concerned about some prominent issues amidst economic recovery, including the huge pressure on ensuring the stability of businesses and security of employment and the difficulties in the recovery of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and self-employed businesses. Generally, the hallmark of the Chinese economy, namely huge potential and strong resilience, remains unchanged. The Chinese economy is set to continue on a recovery path in H2 and is expected to achieve positive growth for the whole year. Journalist: What are the priorities of the PBC in H2 2020? Yi Gang: In H2, the PBC will continue to fully implement the decisions and arrangements of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, adhere to the underlying principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, and follow the new development philosophy. Remaining committed to the primary task of advancing supply-side structural reform, the PBC will take solid steps to ensure stability on the six fronts (employment, the financial sector, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment and expectations) and maintain security in the six areas (the employment of residents, the basic 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 4/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency livelihood of the people, operations of market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and the normal functioning of primary-level governments). The PBC will keep both the financial aggregate and increment at reasonable levels, stabilize businesses and safeguard employment, forestall and defuse major financial risks, accelerate reform and opening-up in the financial sector, and thus promote sound development of the economy and the financial sector. The priorities at the next stage are as follows: First, the monetary policy will be more flexible and appropriate and better targeted, and existing policies to stabilize businesses and safeguard employment will be fully implemented. A mix of monetary policy instruments will be used to guide M2 and AFRE to grow much faster than last year. With well-suited pace and improved structure, inclusive MSB loans and medium and long-term (MLT) manufacturing loans will be expanded at a reasonable level. In terms of forestalling and defusing financial risks, the PBC will uphold the bottom line of risk prevention and make every effort to promote the conclusion of the three-year tough battle as scheduled. In the meantime, the PBC will make stepped-up efforts to shore up weak links in the financial risk resolution system, improve the contingency mechanism for major financial risks, and shift to routine risk management and resolution. Furthermore, the financial institutional reform will be deepened. The PBC will promote the implementation of existing policies for financial reforms, and support the local governments mission of defusing regional financial risks and deepening the market-based reform of rural financial institutions within their means. Besides, financial management and financial services will be enhanced. The PBC will make overall arrangements for poverty alleviation through financial means, and launch the pilot programs of green finance, inclusive finance and sci-tech finance. 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 5/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency Unswerving efforts will be made to promote orderly opening-up of the financial sector. Journalist: Will the increasingly complicated and volatile international situations impact Chinas financial opening-up, international cooperation and RMB internationalization? Yi Gang: No matter how the international situations change, the most important thing is to run our own businesses well and unswervingly deepen the reform and opening-up of the financial sector. First, we will continue to effectively implement the China-US phase-one economic and trade agreement as well as the financial reform and opening-up measures unveiled in recent years, including the policies to remove foreign ownership limits on securities, fund management, futures and life insurance companies, to abolish the investment quota restriction on qualified foreign institutional investors (QFIIs) and RMB qualified foreign institutional investors (RQFIIs), and to approve the entry of American Express, MasterCard, Fitch Rating and other institutions into the Chinese market. Second, we will continue to implement the management model of preestablishment national treatment plus a negative list, and unify the foreign exchange administration policies applied in the opening-up of the bond market. China has consistently called for international cooperation in response to the pandemic. We will continue to engage deeply in global economic and financial governance, earnestly safeguard multilateralism, constructively participate in the G20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI), and extend support in reducing debts for developing countries, emerging markets and some low-income countries. Currently, RMB internationalization enjoys a very favorable momentum. In H1, the amount of cross-border RMB payment and receipt grew 36.7 percent year on year to reach RMB12.7 trillion, making RMB the second largest currency for cross-border 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 6/7 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Governor Yi Gang by Xinhua News Agency payment and receipt in China for eight consecutive years. The share of RMB in global foreign exchange reserves was more than 2 percent in Q1, nearly doubling compared with 2016 when RMB was included in the Special Drawing Right (SDR) currency basket. We will continue to pursue the international use of the RMB and capital account opening-up in an active and prudent way. Date of last update AUG. 14, 2020 3688110/3688175/4072483/index.html 7/7

Title: Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency
text: 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency To Read Chinese Version The pandemic is a big test. How does the financial industry respond? As the blood of the real economy, has the financial industry been effective in supporting the economic and social recovery and development? Facing the pressure of potential rebound of non-performing loans (NPLs), is the dam against risks solid enough? With complicated and volatile environment at home and abroad, does reform and opening-up keep up as always? In response to these hot issues, Guo Shuqing, Secretary of the People's Bank of China (PBC) Committee of the Communist Party of China, and Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC), was interviewed by the Xinhua News Agency. Newly issued loans exceeded RMB12 trillion, which strongly supported and facilitated the recovery of the economy. Financial support plays an important part in stabilizing businesses and securing employment as well as maintaining stable economic fundamentals. 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 1/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency "In the second quarter of this year, China's economy resumed positive growth, which wouldnt have been possible without the strong mitigation impact of macroeconomic policies against the pandemic, including fiscal policies and other policies in taxation, social security, employment, etc. Monetary and financial policies also played an important role." Guo Shuqing said, citing the three rounds of required reserve ratio reductions since the beginning of this year, the increase of RMB1.8 trillion in central bank lending and central bank discounts quota, and the timely introduction of the policy to temporarily allow deferred repayment of loan principal and interest, which effectively facilitated the economic recovery. Data show that in the first half of this year, new RMB loans increased by RMB12.09 trillion, which was RMB2.42 trillion more than the increase over the same period last year. As of the end of June, loans to micro and small businesses (MSBs) for inclusive finance increased by 28.4 percent year on year, and R&D loans increased by 26.95 percent year on year. Compared with the same period last year, unsecured corporate loans increased by 13.8 percent, and medium-to-long-term loans increased by 13.4 percent, both higher than the average loan growth. "The funds are mainly invested in key areas and weak links of the economy such as manufacturing, infrastructure, scientific and technological innovation, MSBs, as well as agriculture, rural areas and rural people, etc. In the first half of the year, new manufacturing loans reached a record high, exceeding the sum of the previous four years' increases, and the total amount and structure of these loans have greatly improved." Guo Shuqing said. In addition to credit support, direct financing is also making its share of contributions. In the first half of the year, corporate bond investment by the banking industry increased by 28.5 percent year on year. Bond investment by insurance funds increased by 16.5 percent year on year, and long-term equity investment increased by 18.2 percent year on year. "Growth rate 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 2/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency of this kind is rare in recent years and has played an important role in promoting the structural adjustment of the financial industry and supporting the development of the real economy." Guo Shuqing said. At present, to push forward the economic and social recovery and development, it is necessary for the financial industry to act more proactively, to have a deep understanding of the needs of the real economy and to provide more targeted services. "The next step is to better support MSBs for inclusive finance. At present, more than 23.6 million MSBs have obtained bank loans, which is among the highest levels even in a global perspective. The key is that commercial banks management and risk control capabilities have greatly improved." Guo Shuqing said. To better support the real economy, we need to promote the balanced development of direct financing and indirect financing. "In the second half of the year, we will continue to promote corporate bond issuance, and banking and insurance institutions should be more active in capital markets such as the fixed-income market. Enterprises can obtain long-term and low-cost funds through direct financing, and a considerable part of them help to increase capital, which is more beneficial to the growth of enterprises. " Guo Shuqing said. To help enterprises tide over difficulties, the banking sector has provided re-financing support for RMB6.12 trillion of enterprise loans due. Faced with the on-gong impact of the pandemic, we should be prepared. "The CBIRC and the PBC have also done some research and prepared stand-by policies. We will be watching the market situation closely. If there are still some problems in recovery, these stand-by policies will be rolled out to help." Guo Shuqing said. The financial industry is operating steadily and actively addressing the rebound of non-performing loans. 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 3/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency Financial support for the real economy must be based on its own steady operation. As Guo Shuqing said, at present, China's financial industry is operating steadily, risks are controllable as a whole, and the main indicators are in a reasonable range. "Since the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, the international financial market has experienced extreme volatility. In comparison, China's stock market, debt market and foreign exchange market have all shown strong resilience and capacity to resist risks." As shown in the data, at the end of the second quarter, the liquidity coverage ratio of China's commercial banks was 142.4 percent, showing sufficient liquidity; the non-performing loan ratio was 1.94 percent, up 0.08 percentage points from the beginning of the year; the provision coverage ratio was 182.4 percent, and the capital adequacy ratio was 14.21 percent, indicating strong capacity to provide sufficient risk cover. Guo Shuqing said that at the same time, it must be noted that currently financial risks are prone to high incidence, and there are still some considerable potential risks, such as the existing risks that havent been completely resolved, the increasing upward pressure of non-performing assets, and the misconducts in the market that tend to rebound and regain its momentum against the background of ample liquidity. We must keep a cool head, calmly judge the situation and take precautions. "In the first half of the year, due to factors such as the pandemic, new non-performing loans in the banking sector increased somewhat compared with the same period of last year. At present, the economy has not fully recovered. There are still uncertainties concerning the pandemic, and there is a certain time lag between the pandemic and the accompanying financial 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 4/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency risks. It is expected that the exposure of the risks of a considerable amount of loans will be delayed. Upward pressure on non- performing loans is building up in the coming future." Guo Shuqing said. Guo Shuqing said that we should pay close attention to these potential risks, plan ahead and respond actively. First, to reinforce asset classification. Banks will be urged to use the expected loss approach to assess loan risks, and truly reflect changes in business operations. Second, to prepare enough ammunition to guard against risks. Banks are required to adopt various methods to replenish capital, increase provision in advance, and improve their ability to resist future risks. Third, to strengthen the disposal of non-performing loans. In the premise of full risk exposure, government agencies will consider lowering requirements on provision coverage ratio in stages, and require that all released resources be used in disposing nonperforming loans. Fourth, to strictly contain the risk of new non-performing loans. Banks are urged to strengthen internal controls and risk management, enhance the pre-lending investigation, loan approval and post-loan management, so as to reduce loan losses. "It is estimated that the banking industry will dispose of RMB3.4 trillion non-performing loans this year, which is more than last year's RMB2.3 trillion. More efforts will be devoted in NPL disposal next year, because the principal and interest repayment of many loans have been extended and some problems wont come to surface until next year." Guo Shuqing said. He said that under the sudden impact of the pandemic, some well-run enterprises encountered suspended sales and fewer orders, and it was inevitable the non-performing loans would rebound. "Fiscal, financial, employment and industry policies should be combined and various means should be explored to help these enterprises, so that our overall economic circulation will be smoother and sooner back to normal." 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 5/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency Reform and opening-up policies will continue, with more attention paid to policy implementation. The opening-up of the financial sector is a key component of China's opening-up. Guo Shuqing said that in the past two years, a total of 34 opening-up measures have been rolled out and put into effect in the banking and insurance sectors, setting forth a number of exemplary cases. For instance, the first foreign-controlled wealth management company and the first wholly foreign-owned insurance holding company were approved for establishment. In the first half of this year, AIA was approved to set up the first wholly foreign-owned life insurance company in Chinas Mainland. Regarding the financial opening-up policies going forward, Guo Shuqing said that the current focus is to ensure the implementation of the policies already introduced. Chinese and foreign institutions are encouraged to enhance cooperation in the areas of products, equity, management and talents, so as to broaden and deepen the opening-up. Supporting policies and infrastructure should be improved, thereby fostering a more market-oriented, law-based and international business environment. "Although great changes have taken place in the international environment, this will not change our general trend of opening up to the outside world. That foreign financial institutions have been attracted to start operations in China during the pandemic has provided a good proof. The policy of opening up China's financial industry to the outside world is unchanged as always. " Guo Shuqing said. 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 6/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency Deepening reforms is a key to solving the difficult problem in Chinas economic development. The same is true in the financial sector. Guo Shuqing said that more efforts will be made to deepen key financial reforms, including speeding up the reform of small and medium-sized banks, vigorously supporting direct financing, and improving the corporate governance of banking and insurance institutions. "We will accelerate the reform of small and medium-sized banks and use it as a breakthrough to enhance the stability and resilience of the financial system. Fund sources should be broadened to enhance risk resolution and speed up capital replenishment. Meanwhile, targeted and differentiated policies should be taken to well balance and integrate the policy objectives of deepening reform with risk mitigation and improvement of governance." Guo Shuqing said that in pushing forward the reform, attention should be paid to maintaining the integrity of local financial institutions, especially to maintaining the overall stability of legal persons status of rural credit cooperatives or rural commercial banks at the county level. He said that efforts will be made to vigorously support direct financing and improve financing structure. Trust companies, wealth management and insurance companies and other institutions will be guided to establish the philosophy of value investment, make real professional investment and value investment, and become the backbone in promoting capital market development and maintaining the stability of capital market. At the same time, we should take corporate governance as the starting point, optimize the ownership structure, and improve the modern financial corporate system. 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 7/8 26/10/2021, 10:40 Exclusive Interview with Guo Shuqing, Secretary of CPC PBC Committee and Chairman of CBIRC, by Xinhua News Agency Date of last update AUG. 19, 2020 3688110/3688175/4074765/index.html 8/8

Title: Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks
Subtitle: In its 16th issue of 2020, theQiushijournal published the articleUnswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risksauthored by Guo Shuqing, Secretary of the CPC Committee of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC) and Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC)
text: 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks To Read Chinese Version In its 16th issue of 2020, the Qiushi journal published the article Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks authored by Guo Shuqing, Secretary of the CPC Committee of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC) and Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC). The main content is as follows: At the 19th CPC National Congress, it was stated that in order to secure a decisive victory in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, we must win three critical battles, and one of the battles is to prevent and defuse major risks. General Secretary Xi Jinping emphatically pointed out that the key to preventing and defusing major risks lies in the prevention of financial risks. In recent years, under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, crucial progress has been secured in the critical battle of preventing and defusing financial risks. The unexpected outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic has severely compromised the normal functioning of both domestic and international economies, and brought about many new financial risks and challenges. Nevertheless, as there is no turning back, we must cope with the situations with aplomb, confront difficulties head on, and strive to achieve a long-term equilibrium between ensuring stable 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 1/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks growth and preventing risks, thus providing solid financial support for building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. I. Safeguarding financial security is crucial to Chinas overall economic and social development. General Secretary Xi Jinping pointed out time and again that finance is the core of modern economy, providing the lifeblood for the real economy; that financial vitality will lead to economic vitality, and financial stability is of vital importance to economic stability; and that financial security is an important part of national security, and safeguarding financial security is a strategic and fundamental matter for Chinas social and economic development. It is of great responsibility to ensure sound functioning of the financial system, and no negligence or slacking is allowed. Since the reform and opening-up, China has made historic progress in its financial sector, and established a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics. By relying on Party leadership and leveraging the institutional strength of socialism, in the spirit of self-revolution, we have taken the initiative to eliminate hidden dangers and successfully overcome various hits and shocks, including the serious inflation in the late 1980s, economic overheating in the mid-1990s and a number of external risks. In this way, we have not only provided a relatively stable financial environment for Chinas economic and social development, but also contributed to the worlds financial stability and development. Since the international financial crisis in 2008, the international economic and financial situations have become more complex and volatile, and a combination of cyclical, structural and institutional problems in the Chinese economy have made the landscape of financial risks more complex and challenging. As the balance of payments gradually improved, the leverage ratios of domestic enterprises, governments and the household sector rose rapidly. Financial products and market structures 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 2/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks became increasingly complex with a low degree of transparency. More and more funds circulated within the financial system without entering the real economy or were diverted out of the real economy. Some illegal financial groups and illicit financial activities grew frantically. Moreover, corruptions and violations of disciplines and regulations within the financial system continued to spread. If these problems had been left unattended, they would certainly have bred systemic risks, produced disruptive effects and severely endangered the sustainable economic development and Chinas political security. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, faced with the challenging landscape of risks, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has gained profound insights into the situations, made keen judgments, and acted resolutely in decision-making. Shortly after the closing of the 18th CPC National Congress, General Secretary Xi Jinping exhorted the whole party that we should attach great importance to the risks and hidden dangers in the fiscal and financial sectors, and hold the bottom line that no systemic financial risks should occur. At the Central Economic Work Conference in late 2016, it was explicitly required that greater priority should be given to preventing financial risks. In 2017, General Secretary Xi Jinping personally planned and arranged a series of major measures to prevent risks, address irregularities and shore up weak links, launching a preliminary campaign for the critical battle against risks. The important remarks made by General Secretary Xi Jinping on the financial work shed light on the fundamental and strategic issues in the financial sector, constituted a systemic and general plan for preventing and defusing financial risks, and provided us with a cardinal principle for securing good performance in financial work in the new era. II. Substantive breakthroughs have been made in the critical battle of preventing and defusing financial risks. 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 3/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks In line with the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC Central Committee and under the command of the State Council and the Financial Stability and Development Committee (FSDC) under the State Council at the forefront, all local authorities, all government departments and the financial system made concerted efforts to push forward the work, and made remarkable achievements in the critical battle of preventing and defusing financial risks. The reckless expansion of financial assets has been fundamentally reversed. From 2017 to 2019, the annual growth rates of credit funds and bond investments of the banking sector in support of the real economy reached as high as 12.1 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively. In contrast, the average annual growth rate of assets registered only 7.7 percent, less than half of that from 2008 to 2016, indicating an increase of RMB64 trillion funds injected into the real economy and a decline of RMB88 trillion in the asset growth of the banking sector. The aggressive investment and wealth management businesses in the insurance sector were curbed, and the proportion of short and medium-term premiums in the life insurance business dropped from a historic high of 31 percent to 4 percent. The leverage ratio of the corporate sector remained generally stable with a slight decline, and those of the household and government sectors grew at a slower pace. The macro leverage ratio, reversing the average annual growth of over 10 percentage points from 2008 to 2016, basically stabilized at around 250 percent in the past three years. The risks of shadow banking have continuously contracted. Shadow banking in China used to be exposed to high risks. Featuring multi-layer nested investment and elusive risks, shadow banking was closely intertwined with real estate bubbles, implicit debt of local governments, and illegal Internet financing, etc. Starting from 2017, intensive measures have been taken to rectify market disorder related to interbank wealth management and off-balance-sheet businesses. After the 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 4/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks implementation of the Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions in 2018, preliminary results have been achieved in making a fundamental improvement of the market with efforts made over the past years. At end-2019, the size of shadow banking decreased by RMB16 trillion from its peak. The interbank wealth management business, interbank investment business and asset management business of securities companies shrank by 87 percent, 26 percent and 42 percent, from their peaks, respectively. Entrusted loans, trust loans and various types of cross-market financial investment products continued to decline. Some international organizations and specialized institutions spoke highly of these efforts, noting that China had achieved the most significant progress in mitigating the risks of shadow banking and fundamentally safeguarded the stability of its financial system. Vigorous steps have been taken for the recognition and disposal of non-performing assets (NPAs). To address the widespread problem of untrue asset quality, examinations and evaluations were conducted on financial institutions (FIs) from multiple perspectives, and stringent requirements were laid out for the prudential classification of risk assets. Stepped-up efforts were made to crack down on the misconducts of covering up NPAs or cooking the books. The ratio of loans overdue for more than 90 days to non-performing loans (NPLs) of commercial banks once exceeded 128 percent in 2016, and fell to 82 percent at end-2019. From 2016 to 2019, RMB5.8 trillion worth of NPLs were disposed in the banking sector, which exceeded the sum of NPLs disposed of in the previous eight years. In the meantime, sped-up capital replenishment and increased provisions comprehensively strengthened the capability of various FIs to respond to external shocks. Rigorous measures have been taken to punish law breaking and corruption. We resolutely clamped down on illegal financial groups and illicit financial activities, and pushed forward asset liquidation, corrupt proceeds and loss recovery and risk isolation in an orderly manner. Efforts were also made to protect legitimate incomes, ban illegal incomes and deal with 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 5/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks problem shareholders who maliciously manipulate FIs in accordance with laws. The Baoshang Bank was taken over according to the law. During the takeover, measures were taken to sufficiently protect the legitimate interests of depositors, break the rigid payment, promote credit stratification and strictly enforce market discipline. Enterprises which seriously violated laws and regulations, such as Anbang Insurance Group Co., Ltd. and CEFC China Energy Co., Ltd., were addressed according to the law, and several holding companies suspected to be illegally engaged in financial businesses were restructured, reorganized and liquidated in a timely manner. Small and medium-sized banks and trust companies with high risks have undergone restructuring and risk resolution with targeted measures for each enterprise. A number of corrupt officials who were engaged in business collusion, tunneling or embezzlement have been brought to justice, among which some were officials from financial regulatory departments who did an inside job. Internet financial risks have been reduced substantially. There used to be a great number of unlicensed platforms which were illegally engaged in financial activities, and many of them operated in the name of financial innovation or Internet Plus initiatives to confuse the public. After intensive rectifications, Internet financial risks decreased significantly, and rampant unlicensed businesses were curbed. An array of illegal Internet wealth management, insurance and securities companies, funds and token institutions were cracked down on. The number of peer-to-peer (P2P) Internet lending institutions in operation nationwide was decreased from the peak of around 5,000 to 29 at end-June 2020, and both the size of P2P Internet lending business and the number of participants dropped for 24 consecutive months. The debt risks of large and medium-sized enterprises have been defused in an orderly manner. By end-2019, around 20,000 creditors committees of banking FIs had been established across the country, and the volume of investment in market-based and law-based debt-for-equity swaps reached RMB1.4 trillion, which helped many enterprises with 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 6/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks development potentials to tide over difficulties. The risks of bond default and stock pledge of many enterprises with liquidity difficulties were mitigated, and a considerable number of zombie enterprises with backward production capacity or poor management were cleared in an orderly way. Approximately 500 large and medium-sized enterprises have implemented pilot programs of joint credit extension, which enhanced the endogenous motivation of debt restraint. The growing tendency of real estate financialization and bubble forming has been contained. Real estate bubbles are the biggest gray rhino threatening financial security. In recent years, local authorities and government departments have acted on the principle that houses are for living in, not for speculation, employed specific measures suited to the cities individual conditions, optimized the allocation of financial resources, and strictly guarded against the illicit flow of funds into the real estate market. In 2019, the growth of real estate loans and the proportion of new real estate loans in the total increments dropped 12 percentage points and 10 percentage points, respectively, compared with the level in 2016. This can not only satisfy the normal needs of the stable development of the real estate sector, but also avoid any larger risk caused by an excessive concentration of funds. The implicit debt risks of local governments have been initially brought under control. Implicit debts are a potential trigger of financial risks. In recent years, China has exercised strict control over the financing increments of local governments, and prohibited illegal provision of financing. Meanwhile, measures have been taken to allow proper forms of financing while curbing irregularities, and to unwind the outstanding implicit debts in an orderly manner. The financial system has also worked actively to cooperate with local governments on debt replacement. The sale of local government bonds over the counter of commercial banks to individual investors has been encouraged, which provided a variety of funding support for 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 7/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks local government debt newly issued according to law. In the past three years, banking and insurance institutions have accumulatively increased their holdings of local government bonds by RMB11 trillion. A long-lasting mechanism which tackles both symptoms and root causes has been gradually improved. From 2017 to 2019, regulators worked to hold FIs and financial professionals strictly accountable for their violations of laws and regulations, imposing 8,818 penalties on banking and insurance institutions and 10,713 penalties on persons liable, with the volume of fines and confiscation amounting to RMB7.24 billion, more than the sum over the past dozen years. With efforts to shore up institutional weaknesses, the regulatory work has been further integrated into the framework of rule of law. Since 2017, a total of 209 pieces of regulations and normative documents for the banking and insurance sectors have been rolled out. The FIs development philosophy and business models, which tend to prioritize speed over quality, have been largely corrected. The quality and efficiency in serving the real economy has been raised markedly. From 2017 to 2019, RMB loans registered a growth of RMB46 trillion. Specifically, loans issued to infrastructure, affordable housing projects and the manufacturing sector grew by RMB8 trillion, RMB3.3 trillion and RMB1.6 trillion, respectively. The average annual growth rates of loans to scientific and technological research, information software, and eco-environmental protection reached 31.2 percent, 20.8 percent and 19.5 percent, respectively, remarkably higher than the growth of total loans in the same period. The goal of increasing volume, expanding coverage and lowering price for financing of micro and small businesses (MSBs) has been generally achieved. Inclusive MSB loans registered an average annual growth of 23.2 percent. The coverage rate of basic financial services in impoverished regions neared 99 percent. In 2019, serious illness insurance covered over 1.1 billion urban and rural residents, and agriculture insurance provided over RMB3.8 trillion of risk protection nationwide. Insurance proceeds have become an important source of funding for recovery and reconstruction after various types of natural disasters. 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 8/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks After continuous efforts, financial risks have tended to be restrained, and the resilience of the financial system has been greatly enhanced. We have not only succeeded in preventing latent risks from evolving into financial crisis, but also created valuable policy space and room for maneuver to cope with various complexities. Past practices have proved that the CPC has made perfectly right and timely decisions and arrangements on preventing and defusing financial risks. If we had spoiled the opportunity and delayed rectifications, we would have to deal with greater difficulties and the adverse consequences would have been immeasurable. III. Major challenges have emerged in the financial sector since the breakout of COVID-19 pandemic. During a critical period of transition to high quality growth, the Chinese economy have run into difficulties such as accelerated population aging, the decline in the savings rate and greater environmental and resource constraints. The once-in-a-century pandemic directly caused a sharp decline of the Chinese economy in Q1 this year. Though its growth returned to positive in Q2, the economy still faces many uncertainties in its development in the short and medium term. According to the projection of Global Economic Prospects, which was released by the World Bank in June, the global economy is expected to experience a 5.2 percent contraction in 2020. For some time to come, the Chinese economy will suffer from the pressure from both the supply and demand sides, and in both the domestic and overseas markets. The financial system will undoubtedly encounter great difficulties. To curb the recession, when economic activities sharply contract, financial activities must expand instead. Previously, the policy target was to ensure that the growth of broad money supply (M2) and aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) is slightly higher than the nominal GDP growth. In H1 this year, there was a positive margin of over 10 percentage points. It is 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 9/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks estimated that the overall leverage ratio and sectoral leverage ratios will all experience a considerable rebound in 2020, and the bad debts of FIs may markedly increase. In 2019, the banking sector recorded RMB2.7 trillion of new NPLs. Following the onset of the pandemic, or the Black Swan, the quality of assets in the banking sector will only deteriorate at a faster pace. Since there is a time lag for financial accounting to reveal such influence, the real risks have not been accurately reflected in the current asset classification. The spot book profits of banks are largely overestimated. Nevertheless, this will not last long, and more NPAs will be exposed successively. It is essential to take macro countermeasures to offset the impact of the pandemic. If any fresh abnormal situations arose in the process of implementation, efforts in this regard would be further intensified. But we must not ignore that, in a loose financing environment, enterprises, households and governments are all likely to become more indebted. The strengthened homogeneous expectations for lower interest rates may fuel leveraged deals and speculations, thus giving birth to another round of asset bubbles. As real estate prices in some regions have started to pick up, financial resources may be once again concentrated in high-risk areas. Borrowers with relatively poor credit ratings may exploit deferred repayments or other preferential policies to maliciously evade repayment obligations for bank loans, and the high-risk shadow banking with complex structures may make a comeback easily. Furthermore, after years of rapid development, Fintech has presented many opportunities and significant challenges. Ranking high globally in the development of Fintech in some fields, China has no ready-made experience for reference regarding risk prevention and control. The widespread application of big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies has profoundly changed the forms and transmission pathways of traditional financial risks, and made non- 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 10/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks traditional risks such as those concerning data security ever more prominent. As these risks may break out suddenly and are highly hidden and destructive, they deserve our great vigilance. IV. The financial system should be committed to ensuring that the targets for economic and social development are achieved as scheduled. In the face of the complicated and grave economic situation, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has made deployments for the next stage in a timely manner. While effectively strengthening the awareness of opportunities as well as risks, we should maintain overall stability and take a coordinated approach to further enhance the quality and efficiency of financial services and bring economic development back on track as soon as possible; at the same time, we should take differentiated measures and defuse bombs with precision so as to resolve major risks in key areas in an orderly manner and achieve a long-term balance between stabilizing growth and preventing risks. The following tasks are especially important for the current stage. All-out efforts should be made to bring the circulation of the national economy back to normal. The financial sector and the real economy share common stakes. Serving the real economy is not only the duty and purpose of the financial sector but also the fundamental means to guard against financial risks. Just as an old saying goes, With the rise of agricultural, industrial, and commercial trades emerge currencies in various forms. Currently, the overarching task is to fully restore the industrial cycle, the market cycle as well as the economic and social cycle on the condition that a resurgence of the pandemic is strictly guarded against. Committed to ensuring stability on six fronts, namely, employment, the financial sector, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment, and expectations, and to maintaining security in six areas, namely, 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 11/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks employment, people's basic livelihood, operations of market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and the normal functioning of primary-level governments, we should make the best use of Chinas advantages in enjoying huge market potential, enormous savings resources, and wide-ranged international cooperation, and give play to the enthusiasm and initiative of government agencies at all levels. We should strengthen the synergy among fiscal, financial, employment, and industrial policies to serve the needs of all types of market entities, such as those of MSBs, and remove the obstacles to production, distribution, circulation, and consumption so that a new development pattern will be formed in China, where domestic and international circulations boost each other, with the domestic circulation as the mainstay. We should accelerate the financial supply-side structural reform. Finance is the heart and lifeblood of the economy in modern times. It is also an important tool for resource allocation and macro regulation. As long as finance works well, it is like a right chess move making a difference across the board. Therefore, the financial supply-side structural reform plays a pivotal role in the economic supply-side structural reform. While sticking to the direction of reform to develop the socialist market economy, we should pick up pace in transforming the development mode of the financial sector. Work should be done to adapt the financial structure in line with economic and social development, promote funding facilitation, reduce costs for the real economy, and increase the efficiency of resource allocation. Corporate governance in FIs should be improved to redress insider control as well as manipulation by large shareholders. Continued efforts should be made to improve the fundamental institutions of the capital market and to guide wealth management, trust and insurance companies to step up stable long-term funding for the capital market. Moreover, we should speed up the building of the second and third pillars for old-age insurance, and increase the share of pension funds in the capital market to reach the global average. 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 12/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks The NPAs should be disposed of as early as possible. As credit risk is the most fundamental risk in the financial sector, toxic assets are like lesions that must be removed resolutely. Any attempt to conceal the problems or procrastinate the treatments only leads to missing the optimum timing of disposal, and ultimately causes severe consequences. The FIs need to adopt a more prudential financial and accounting system, effectively implement asset classification and fully expose NPAs. In routine supervision, we cannot simply take the rise of non-performing assets ratio as the assessment criterion. FIs shall step up the disposal of NPAs by leveraging the financial space set aside according to regulatory requirements on provisions. In addition, they need to make realistic income and profit plans, and increase provisions and capital replenishment. The policy obstructions of NPA disposal should be removed so as to create more favorable conditions for greater soundness of the financial system. Measures should be taken to prevent high-risk shadow banking from staging a comeback. Shadow banking risks can easily break out and result in enormous impacts. Even the rustle of leaves in the wind may trigger a prairie fire and cause endless fallout. At present, owing to unremitting governance, we have put the risks of shadow banking under control to some extent. However, the soil nurturing the shadow banking has not been fully eradicated. Any slight regulatory relaxation will probably lead to a big revival, wasting all of our previous efforts. We should maintain a strategic resolve and tough stance toward high-risk businesses. By emphasizing the principle of simplicity and transparency and regulating cross-market financial products, FIs must draw a clear dividing line between publicly offered and privately offered products, isolate the risks of on-balance-sheet businesses from those of off-balance-sheet businesses, ensure separate-account management of entrusted and proprietary businesses, and differentiate savings products from investment products. Efforts should be made to clearly define the function of stock market, bond market, credit market and money market with orderly division of work. 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 13/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks We should continue to rectify Internet financial risks and crack down on illegal fund-raising and other financial activities violating laws and regulations. Different types of institutions risks should be resolved in a timely manner. We should take targeted and effective measures to address institutions with different risks. For high-risk financial groups, their risk resolution should, in line with laws and regulations, be advanced according to existing plans and division of work. Maintaining a generally stable status of county-level incorporated bodies, rural FIs are encouraged to replenish capital and introduce strategic investors in various forms. For city commercial banks, trust companies and other locally incorporated institutions, provincial governments will be supported in formulating and implementing resolution plans with strengthened professional guidance of financial regulators. A list of domestic systemically important banks should be developed as soon as possible, while recovery and resolution plans should be made for institutions on the list. For problematic institutions, an effective risk resolution mechanism should be set up. FIs shall perform primary responsibilities with the shareholders, especially principal shareholders, assuming important responsibilities. Local Party committees and governments shall fulfill jurisdiction duties by integrating the responsibility of Party leadership at the local level, the responsibility of managing local state-owned financial capital, and the responsibility of resolving local risks and safeguarding social stability within their jurisdiction. Financial regulators shall assume primary regulatory responsibilities. The deposit insurance system and institutional system shall be perfected to fully leverage the role of early intervention, early warning and early resolution. The opening-up of the financial sector should be steadily broadened. Following the guideline of autonomy, orderliness, equality and security, we will strive to realize financial opening-up at a higher level without compromising financial sovereignty. We will step up efforts to construct an open, transparent, stable and predictable regulatory policy environment, 3688110/3688175/4078031/index.html 14/17 26/10/2021, 10:40 Unswervingly Fight the Critical Battle of Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks and encourage domestic and overseas FIs to compete on an equal footing, deepen cooperation, learn from each other and promote innovation. We should consolidate the capability of macro financial management as well as risk prevention and control under the open circumstances, so as to identify in time and effectively contain the spread of external shocks into domestic markets. We will actively engage in international financial governance and the formulation of regulatory rules, promote international coordination on macro policies, and increase Chinas voice in the international arena. Solid work should be done to enhance financial consumer education and protection. We should make greater endeavors to publicize financial knowledge, helping both urban and rural residents understand that investment is not risk-free and there is no financial product featuring high returns yet low risks, let alone the so-called wealth management program that guarantees profits. In other words, any product advertised to ensure protected principal with high yields is financial fraud. Both institutional and individual investors should develop the awareness of value investment, rational investment and risk prevention. We should promote the spirit of contract, consolidate the awareness of rule of law, act in strict accordance with the law, and increase the costs for violation of laws. Product structures should be simplified, client layering rigorously implemented, and risks honestly reported. Information disclosure should be enhanced to make a more transparent market. The construction of the social credit system should be advanced and the mechanism for joint punitive action against bad faith further improved, so as to correct all kinds of violations that mislead financial consumers in a timely way. Title: State Council Policy Briefing on 'Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy'
text: 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy To Read Chinese Version The State Council Information Office held a regular press briefing at 10 a.m. on August 25, 2020 (Tuesday). Liu Guoqiang, Deputy Governor of the Peoples Bank of China (PBC), and Xiao Yuanqi, Chief Risk Officer and spokesperson of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC), introduced the implementation of policies for promoting the support extended by financial institutions to the real economy, and answered questions from the press. Selected transcript is as follows. (This English version only covers the speech and answers of PBC Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang.) Liu Guoqiang: Dear friends from the press, good morning! The CPC Central Committee and the State Council have been attaching great importance to financial support for the real economy. General Secretary Xi Jinping stressed that market entities were the vehicles of economic power, and that securing market entities was securing productivity. Efforts should be made to ramp up policy support, invigorate market entities, provide stronger financial support for market entities, and implement policies in a more targeted and timely manner, so as to effectively ease the financing difficulty and reduce the 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 1/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy financing costs of enterprises, especially micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and push for greater development of market entities. On August 17, Premier Li Keqiang presided over the 104th State Council executive meeting, requiring that policy measures for promoting financial support for the real economy be further implemented to help market entities overcome difficulties and achieve development. Next, I will briefly introduce financial support extended to the real economy this year. Since the beginning of 2020, the PBC and CBIRC have worked together with relevant authorities to earnestly implement the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council and guide financial institutions to enhance efforts to effectively support the development of the real economy. First, the sound monetary policy has been carried out in a more flexible and appropriate manner. A mix of monetary policy tools, including required reserve ratio (RRR) cuts, medium-term lending facility (MLF), open market operations, central bank lending and central bank discounts, have been applied to keep liquidity adequate at a reasonable level and keep overall market interest rates stable with a slight decline. Second, the loan prime rate (LPR) reform has constantly delivered benefits. The loan prime rate is typically referred to as the LPR. The PBC has guided the MLF rates and open market operation rates to move downward by 0.3 percentage points, which drove the LPR down correspondingly and continuously pushed down lending rates for enterprises. Steady steps have been taken to push forward the transition of the pricing benchmark of outstanding floating-rate loans so as to reduce the interests paid by enterprises for outstanding loans. Third, structural monetary policy tools have been implemented to provide liquidity in a well-targeted way. The policies of RMB300 billion special central bank lending and of RMB500 billion central bank lending and central bank discounts have been fully implemented, following which the policy of RMB1 trillion central bank lending and central bank discounts was put in place as an orderly continuation. Great attention has been paid to the pace of monetary 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 2/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy policy, which is a major feature of the policies implemented this year. Instead of firing all the bullets from the outset, we have acted in accordance with the needs of coordinating pandemic containment with economic development and adopted a phased approach to address priorities at each stage patiently, refraining from rushing into anything and properly handling the pace of our work. In addition, two innovative monetary policy tools that can provide direct support for the economy were introduced, namely, a support instrument for deferring the repayment of inclusive loans to micro and small businesses (MSBs) and a support plan for providing unsecured loans for inclusive MSBs. The two policies have increased direct support for MSBs. Fourth, banks have been urged to reduce the fees charged on enterprises. The Notice on Further Regulating Fees Related to Credit Financing and Reducing Overall Financing Costs of Enterprises was published to regulate the collection of fees in the course of credit granting, assistance for loan acquisition, credit enhancement and appraisal, and to urge banks to implement various policies for the reduction of fees and take the initiative in easing the burden on the real economy. Fifth, we have further tapped into the potential of policy finance. The annual loan quotas of policy banks have been increased, and funds have been established to provide relief for the manufacturing sector and foreign trade enterprises. Policy banks have been guided to make full use of low-cost financing through debt issuance and other advantages, so as to provide targeted support for MSBs through on-lending of wholesale funds. Overall, these policy measures have harvested remarkable results, with the quality and efficiency of the financial sector in serving the real economy continuously improving, and money and credit increasing reasonably at a rate significantly higher than a year earlier. At end-July, broad money supply (M2) and aggregate financing to the real economy (AFRE) grew by 10.7 percent and 12.9 percent respectively year on year, 2 percentage points and 2.2 percentage points higher than those at end2019 respectively. In the first seven months of 2020, loans increased by RMB13.1 trillion, RMB2.4 trillion more than the 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 3/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy increase in the same period last year. Lending rates for enterprises fell markedly. All these are about volume, and next I will move to interest rates. In July, the lending rates for enterprises stood at 4.68 percent, decreasing by 0.64 percentage points year on year. The goal of increasing volume, expanding coverage and lowering price for MSB financing has been achieved; the year-on-year growth of outstanding inclusive MSB loans has been much higher than that of total loans; and the financing costs of MSBs has substantially declined. According to estimates, since the beginning of 2020, following the principle of commercial sustainability, the financial sector has eased the burden on market entities by more than RMB870 billion in the first seven months through interest rate cuts, reduction of fees, deferment of loan principal and interest repayments and other measures, and has remarkably strengthened its support for MSBs. The amount is expected to reach around RMB1.5 trillion for the entire year. Going forward, the PBC and CBIRC will continue to work together with relevant authorities to resolutely implement financial support policies, including those for easing the burden on market entities. First, we will keep the liquidity adequate at a reasonable level, refrain from indiscriminate massive stimulus, bring into full play the role of structural monetary policy tools which can directly support the economy in providing liquidity in a precise and targeted manner, and ensure that newly-added funds primarily flow into the real economy, especially to MSBs. Second, financial support policies will be made more convenient, so as to support small and medium-sized banks to forge effective connection with enterprises by means of the big data technology, smooth the transmission mechanism and deliver benefits to more market entities. The LPR reform will be deepened to guide downward movement of lending rates. The policies of issuing loans at preferential interest rates with funds from central bank lending and central bank discounts and supporting the issuance of unsecured loans will be put in place, so as to achieve the goal of increasing volume, expanding coverage and lowering price for MSB financing for the entire year. 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 4/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy Third, inspections will be conducted to address unjustified and unauthorized fees charged by banks, thus guiding banks to cut profits in favor of the real economy by taking the initiative in reducing service fees, and regulating and limiting fees charged on MSB loans. Fourth, efforts will also be made to prevent financial risks and improve the sustainability of banks in serving the real economy. Thank you. Journalist with Peoples Daily: Recently, the market has been concerned about financial institutions lowering profit margins in favor of enterprises. We have noted that it was pointed out at a recent State Council Executive Meeting that financial institutions eased the burden on market entities by RMB870 billion in the first seven months this year. How did they manage to do so? Just now, Deputy Governor Liu mentioned that financial institutions are expected to lower profit margins by RMB1.5 trillion in favor of market entities for the entire year. With RMB870 billion already accomplished, what do you plan to do to pull off the rest of the task? Liu Guoqiang: Thank you for the questions. In the first seven months this year, the financial sector has proactively eased the burden on market entities by a total of RMB870 billion with measures such as lowering interest rates, reducing fees and charges, and deferring loan principal and interest repayments. The burden reduction covers the following aspects. First, RMB470 billion was saved for market entities with lower interest rates. To be more specific, RMB354 billion was attributed to lower lending rates which were guided by the decline of LPR; RMB37 billion was attributed to loans issued at preferential interest rates with central bank lending and central bank discounts; and RMB79 billion, saved for bond issuers, was attributed to the cut of interest rates on bonds. Second, the two monetary policy tools which enable directly support for the real economy, namely one for supporting unsecured inclusive MSB loans and the other for provisional deferment of MSME loan principal and interest repayments, as well as the policy of deferred loan principal and interest repayments introduced in the 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 5/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy previous stage, contributed to a burden reduction of RMB133.5 billion. The deferred loan principal and interest repayments alleviated corporate burdens by around RMB121.5 billion, and the support for the issuance of unsecured inclusive MSB loans helped enterprises save around RMB12 billion in fees such as those for guarantee. Third, banks relieved the burden on market entities by RMB204.5 billion through reducing and waiving service fees. Fourth, the support for enterprises restructuring and debt-for-equity swaps enabled a burden reduction of around RMB66 billion. Besides, the financial sector also redoubled efforts to resolve non-performing loans (NPLs) through write-offs and other means, and took on the costs incurred to market entities with its own financial resources, which not only strengthened its own resilience against risks, but also contributed to the real economy. I want to take this opportunity to clarify a concept, that is, the process of the financial sector easing burdens on market entities in line with the principle of sustainable business development is not in tandem with profit changes of commercial banks. In other words, it is not the case that RMB1.5 trillion worth of burden reduction would translate into a profit cut of RMB1.5 trillion for commercial banks. That is not how it works. The loan income of commercial banks is determined by both the rates and the amounts of loans. After commercial banks lower their lending rates, the demand for loans will grow, which can lead to an increase in amounts. As lower prices result in larger amounts of loans, the income losses, which are caused by lower lending rates, will be offset. This is smaller margins, but greater volumes. In addition, the profits of commercial banks also depend on many other factors, such as the cost of funds and disposal of NPLs. Since the beginning of this year, the PBC has conducted monetary policy operations to guide a downward movement of overall market rates, and lowered the cost of funds for financial institutions by cutting interest rates on central bank lending and central bank discounts. Therefore, financial institutions got funds at lower rates, although the loan rates for enterprises declined. The spread has been narrowed, 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 6/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy but not considerably. Lower costs could offset the profit shrinking, so the profits of commercial banks would not fall that much. We still have several months to go this year. From August to December, the financial sector will continue to ease the burden of market entities by over RMB600 billion, bringing this years total burden reduction to RMB1.5 trillion. The estimated amount is calculated on the basis of a combination of factors, including the current interest rates, a slight decline in lending rates through smoother interest rate transmission, and effective implementation of policies introduced before. Thank you. Journalist with Market News International: As we can see, the banking sector saw a decline in profits in H1 this year, and now banks are faced with mounting pressure from non-performing assets (NPAs) and difficulties in capital replenishment. Id like to know, how will the regulators properly balance and handle the three challenges? Will you relax the requirements for capitals of banks to some extent? Thank you. Liu Quoqiang: Thank you for your questions. Due to the impact of the pandemic, the downward pressure on the domestic economy has grown, and the earnings of the banking sector has registered a year-on-year drop. In H1 this year, banking financial institutions secured a profit of RMB2.4 trillion, down 12 percent year on year. This was mainly attributed to banks move to ease the burden on the real economy, increased provisions and responses in advance to the pressure of mounting NPLs in the future. Overall, the performance of the banking sector has been sound, with adequate provisions and capital. By the end of Q2, 2020, the capital adequacy ratio registered 14.21 percent, 0.43 percentage points lower than that at the beginning of this year. Though lower than the level of early 2020, it was still well above the minimum regulatory requirement of 10.5 percent. Thus 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 7/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy for the time being, there is no need to ease the regulatory requirement in this regard. Capital is necessary in doing business, so it is very important to keep capital adequate. Even if the capital adequacy ratio drops in the future, we cannot lower regulatory requirements to make up for it. Doing so would be fooling ourselves as well as others. Instead, banks should have a wealth of practical means to replenish their capital. In order to improve the ability of the financial sector to serve the real economy, to serve MSBs and the agricultural sector, rural areas and farmers, the PBC will work with relevant authorities to improve the mechanisms and systems for banks capital replenishment and support banks to replenish capital through multiple means, including perpetual bonds, second-tier capital bonds and other innovative capital tools. Moreover, steps will also be taken to well use funds from local government special bonds to replenish the capital of small and medium-sized banks, deepen the reform of these banks, and improve their corporate governance structures as well as risk prevention and management mechanisms in line with their characteristics. Thank you. Journalist with Reuters: The US and many other countries are encouraging their companies to leave China and gradually reduce their dependence on the Chinese market. Is the PBC worried about the situation and its possible impact on RMB internationalization in the future? Thank you. Liu Guoqiang: Your question concerns a wide range of issues. I will answer it in terms of financial opening-up. In April 2018, General Secretary Xi Jinping announced that China would substantially broaden market access and put in place relevant measures as soon as possible. The earlier the better, the faster the better. Over the past two years, despite changing international situation and the impact from of the pandemic, financial opening-up has been moving ahead as planned. With the coordination of the the State Council Financial Stability and Development Committee, the PBC, CBIRC, 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 8/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy CSRC and SAFE have announced and pushed ahead with over 50 concrete measures, markedly speeding up the opening-up of the financial sector. First of all, foreign-funded financial institutions have been allowed much wider market access. Foreign ownership caps have been abolished for sectors such as banking, securities, fund management, futures and life insurance. The business scope of foreign-funded financial institutions has been expanded substantially, while the requirements for total assets, years in operation and shareholder qualification have been eased. A number of foreign-funded institutions have become controlling shareholders of some domestic securities firms and insurance companies, and several global asset management institutions are inclined to establish wholly foreign-owned fund management companies or foreign-controlled wealth management companies and to participate in the establishment of commercial banks wealth management subsidiaries. Achievements have been made in the development of Shanghai as an international financial center. Judging from the financial perspective, foreign-funded institutions are now better motivated to enter rather than leave the Chinese market. Second, we have been steadily pushing ahead with the two-way opening-up of the capital market. Quota limits under the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor (QFII) and RMB Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor (RQFII) schemes have been removed completely. The quotas were expanded step by step previously and now there are no longer any limits. Restrictions on the proportions of RMB and foreign currency funds repatriated by overseas institutional investors have been relaxed, and the pilot scheme of Cross-border Wealth Management Connect has been launched in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Moreover, foreign-funded institutions have been allowed to underwrite bonds and conduct bond ratings in the interbank market, and the type-A underwriting licenses have been granted to some foreign-funded institutions, allowing them to act as lead underwriters for debt financing instruments issued by non-financial enterprises. The 3688110/3688175/4087230/index.html 9/18 26/10/2021, 10:44 Deputy Governor Liu Guoqiang Attends State Council Policy Briefing on Implementation of Policies for Promoting Support Extended by Financial Institutions to Real Economy bond market has seen overseas issuers and investors increasing, and supporting systems  such as those for accounting, taxation and trading, improving. The Shanghai-London Stock Connect kicked off. A shares were included in FTSE Russell and S&P Dow Jones indices, while MSCI increased the inclusion factor of A shares to 20 percent.
